title: Researchers Discover Earth May Have Made Its Own Water 4.5 Billion Years Ago
content:
Artist’s illustration of early Earth, showing rocky debris raining through a scorching atmosphere onto a molten surface. Credit: University of New Mexico
Laboratory experiments suggest that rocky planets could generate their own water as they form, potentially giving distant worlds an essential ingredient for life.
Rocks, hydrogen gas, and intense heat might sound like an unlikely recipe for an ocean. Yet experiments suggest that these ingredients could have produced much of Earth’s water while the planet was still taking shape.
One leading explanation for Earth’s water involves small particles containing ice, known as icy pebbles. These formed in colder regions of the early solar system, where water could remain frozen, and may have carried that water to the growing Earth. Questions remain about how the particles traveled such long distances and whether those deliveries can fully explain Earth’s chemical composition.
Water in minutes from rock and hydrogen
Graduate student Susmita Garai led the new research with Zachary Sharp, professor and director of Earth and Planetary Sciences, and Peter Olson at the University of New Mexico. Their study, published in
Nature Geoscience
, investigated whether iron-bearing silicate rocks could react with atmospheric hydrogen under conditions resembling those of early planetary formation.
Experimental apparatus heating silicate rock samples. Credit: University of New Mexico
“In order to evaluate the possibility of ‘pebble’ rain’ being a source of water, we needed to construct and execute some very challenging high-temperature experiments. Dr. Garai’s efforts paid off mightily, as she found that water is produced in just minutes in the high-temperature environment of the Early Earth’s atmosphere,” Sharp said.
The researchers heated silicate rock samples to between 1,200 and 1,400 degrees Celsius, or about 2,192 to 2,552 degrees Fahrenheit, in experiments lasting from 15 minutes to three hours. Some samples were exposed to streams of hydrogen. Others were heated in helium for comparison, allowing the team to test hydrogen’s role in the reaction.
In the hydrogen experiments, nearly 80% of the iron oxide in the samples was converted into metallic iron, producing water vapor in the process. Hydrogen reacted with oxygen bound to iron in the rocks, leaving the iron as metal and forming water. The same reaction did not occur in helium.
Pebble rain could supply Earth’s oceans
“Previous ideas about the source of water to Earth rely on an external source, such as comets or meteorites. Here we show that virtually any Earth-sized planet should have water by this newly identified mechanism,” Sharp explained.
Results from the experiment. Left showcases the molten iron in silicate melt. Right shows the solid iron crystals in silicate melt. Credit: University of New Mexico
For this chemistry to supply a growing planet with water, rocky material, and hydrogen would need to meet under suitable conditions. That could happen during pebble accretion, a process in which small rocky particles accumulate to build a larger planetary body. Once the growing planet became sufficiently massive, it could develop a hot, high-pressure atmosphere rich in hydrogen. Silicate pebbles falling through that atmosphere could then undergo the water-producing reaction tested in the laboratory.
“We had suspected and hoped that we would produce iron metal and water in our reduction experiments, but we really had no way of knowing how fast and how much. We were quite surprised to find that extrapolation of our work suggests that hundreds of oceans worth of water were likely produced in this way. Looking out over a large body of water, it is hard to imagine that that water may have been produced 4 ½ billion years ago in a hell-like atmosphere, but it very well may have,” said Sharp.
AI generated illustration of pebble rain. Credit: University of New Mexico
Earth-sized worlds could make their own water
If comparable conditions developed around other rocky planets during their formation, the reaction could provide a widespread route to water on Earth-sized worlds beyond our solar system.
“The idea of pebble accretion is still relatively new. It’s only been around for the last decade. But it seems to solve many problems that exist with the existing paradigm for planet formation,” Sharp said. “And now we see that it also can explain why our planet is habitable. By extension, it is reasonable to expect that other Earth-sized bodies circling other stars would also have water and possibly life.”
The experiments demonstrate a potential mechanism for producing water during planetary formation. Determining how much of Earth’s water actually originated this way will require further research.
Reference: “Dry pebble rain could have delivered water to Earth through hydrogen reduction of iron oxide”, 12 October 2026,
Nature Geoscience
DOI: 10.1038/s41561-026-02138-3

title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe Discovers Something Unexpected Hidden in the Chaos of Space
content:
Artist’s illustration of NASA’s “Parker Solar Probe” mission. Credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL/Steve Gribben
NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has uncovered hidden order in space turbulence, a finding that could help scientists understand magnetic storms on Earth.
Smoke rising from an incense stick can begin as a thin, steady stream before curling and spreading unpredictably. The smoke makes turbulence in the air visible. Turbulence also occurs in space, where the moving material is plasma, an ionized gas containing electrically charged particles. Electric and magnetic fields strongly influence how those particles move, making this turbulence different from the movements of ordinary air.
Space plasma is also so dilute that its particles rarely collide, making it effectively collisionless. Physicists are still working to understand how turbulence develops under these conditions and how its energy is distributed. Measurements from NASA’s Parker Solar Probe have now revealed an organized pattern within that irregular activity.
Magnetic fields reverse rotation at smaller scales
At large scales, plasma behaves like a fluid, and turbulence develops through swirling motions called vortices and through electromagnetic waves. The fluctuations become random. At smaller scales, the dynamics of individual particles become important. These are different ways the same material behaves depending on the size of the disturbances being examined.
Using high-precision magnetic field and particle data from Parker Solar Probe, an international research team directly demonstrated, for the first time, that turbulent magnetic fields reverse their preferred direction of rotation across this transition. Picture the magnetic field’s direction as an arrow that can turn as the field fluctuates. Viewed looking radially away from the Sun, the fields preferentially rotate counterclockwise at larger scales. At smaller scales, they rotate clockwise.
Reversal of the field rotation from left-handed rotation (blue) to right-handed rotation (red), plotted on the frequency spectrum (y axis) against distance from the Sun x axis). Analysis based on the data from the Parker Solar Probe. A low frequency corresponds to a long wavelength in the spectrum. Credit: Iizawa et al., Astrophys. J. Lett., 2026
The reversal occurs at the wavelength, or spatial scale, where fluid-like behavior gives way to particle-like dynamics. Farther from the Sun, the reversal becomes more pronounced and shifts toward longer wavelengths, corresponding to larger spatial scales.
“We see a clear structure in the spectrum, even though the turbulence represents unstructured motions,” says Dr. Masatomi Iizawa of Technische Universität Braunschweig (TU Braunschweig), the article’s first author.
The study brought together researchers from the Institute of Theoretical Physics at TU Braunschweig and the University of Tokyo, in cooperation with Tohoku University, Kyushu University, Osaka University, and other research institutes. The collaboration spanned ten countries, and the results are published in
The Astrophysical Journal Letters
Turbulence shapes space weather
Dr. Yokoi of the University of Tokyo says, “The results are of great significance for both plasma physics and astrophysics.”
Plasma turbulence plays an important role in the solar wind, solar eruptions, and interplanetary space, as well as in Earth’s magnetosphere, the region dominated by our planet’s magnetic field. It also matters in accretion disks, where material orbits and moves inward toward a central object. In interplanetary space, turbulence can influence the shock waves and magnetic clouds produced by solar eruptions, making it an important factor in predicting geomagnetic storms.
Reference: “Nonlocal Evolution of Magnetic Helicity across the Magnetohydrodynamic–Kinetic Interface” by Masatomi Iizawa, Yasuhito Narita, Tommaso Alberti, Stuart D. Bale, Axel Brandenburg, Abraham C.-L. Chian, Horia Comişel, Shuichi Matsukiyo and Nobumitsu Yokoi, 13 October 2026,
The Astrophysical Journal Letters
DOI: 10.3847/2041-8213/aea84b
This work was funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation)—535057280 and also by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research JP23K25895 and JP26K00767.

title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Is About to Become the First Spacecraft One Light-Day From Earth
content:
Nearly 50 years after launch, NASA’s Voyager 1 is overcoming mysterious glitches and dwindling power as it approaches an extraordinary milestone 16 billion miles from Earth. Credit: NASA, ESA, and G. Bacon (STScI)
Voyager 1 is nearing a distance from Earth that light takes a full day to cross, while NASA engineers stretch its dwindling power to keep it exploring.
NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s most distant spacecraft, was about 16 billion miles (25.75 billion kilometers) from Earth when its radio signal disappeared in October.
NASA’s Deep Space Network
, which uses large antennas at three facilities around the globe to communicate with spacecraft at the Moon and beyond, could not detect the probe during two scheduled contacts on October 18 and 19, 24 hours apart.
The signal returned on October 20, ending the 48-hour interruption before engineers had sent commands to troubleshoot the problem. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 since then.
Engineers are still investigating what caused the communication loss. They have determined that one group of thrusters went offline and its backups switched on. Thrusters are small rocket engines used to control a spacecraft’s movement or orientation. Voyager 1 is programmed to make the switch automatically if its computers detect something wrong with the active thrusters. This response, called fault protection, puts the spacecraft into a safe, stable configuration and pauses normal operations, giving engineers time to diagnose the problem and act.
“This is the first time we’ve seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected,” said Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California. “We’re relieved to be back in contact with Voyager 1 and are eager to understand what happened.”
This image, taken on April 27, 1977, shows one of the Voyagers in the 25-Foot Space Simulator thermal vacuum chamber at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech
Interstellar science on a shrinking power supply
Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 are the only spacecraft ever to study interstellar space directly. Both now travel beyond the heliosphere, the bubble of particles and magnetic fields created by the Sun. Keeping their instruments running preserves access to measurements that no other spacecraft can provide.
Both probes draw electricity from radioisotope thermoelectric generators, which convert heat from decaying plutonium into electrical power. As that fuel supply diminishes, each spacecraft loses about 4 watts of power a year. Nearly half a century after the mission’s 1977 launch, little spare power remains, and engineers have been shutting down nonessential devices and systems to conserve energy.
The mission began with 10 dedicated
science instruments
. Some were shut down after the spacecraft completed their planetary encounters, while others stayed on to study the heliosphere’s outer region. In recent years, dwindling power has forced the team to turn off two science instruments.
Three simultaneous swaps extend Voyager’s science mission
Saving electricity also requires keeping the spacecraft warm enough to work. In early September, engineers completed a months-long effort to turn off three devices aboard Voyager 1 and replace their functions with three lower-power alternatives. The operation, nicknamed the “Big Bang,” came about six weeks after the team
performed the same swap on Voyager 2
All six devices involved help keep the spacecraft warm in the cold of space. To reduce electricity use while maintaining the proper distribution of heat, engineers had to make all three swaps simultaneously. The successful operation will allow Voyager 1’s
remaining science instruments
to work longer than previously anticipated. Without it, the team would have needed to shut down another instrument as early as summer 2027.
A two-day wait for Voyager’s reply
Voyager 1 is traveling at 38,000 mph (61,155 kph) toward another milestone. On November 18, it will be 16.09 billion miles (25.89 billion kilometers) from Earth. That distance equals one light-day, the distance light travels in a day. A radio message from Earth will take 24 hours to reach Voyager 1, and its reply will need another 24 hours to travel back.
Crossing that threshold will cause no change in the spacecraft’s surroundings or anything aboard it. The milestone marks the reach and endurance of humanity’s most distant explorer.
“If you want to say ‘hello’ to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response,” said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL.

title: A Woman Who Lived 30,000 Years Ago Is Changing What We Know About Ice Age Europe
content:
Cave of Isturitz, the cavity in which the bone of a Gravettian woman was found. Credit: Severine Dabadie
DNA preserved in ancient cave sediments reveals how some Ice Age Europeans endured extreme cold, while genetic evidence from France uncovers unexpected connections across the continent.
A woman who lived in southwestern France around 30,000 years ago carried a genetic history that stretched far beyond her corner of Ice Age Europe. Most of her ancestry was western European, but part of it was related to populations in central and eastern Europe. Her DNA challenges the idea that ancient populations on opposite sides of the continent remained largely separated from one another.
For archaeologists, evidence of these distant connections is not entirely new. The Gravettian culture, which spread across Europe roughly 34,000 to 25,000 years ago, left behind evidence suggesting extensive contact between groups. Ancient DNA, however, seemed to tell a different story, pointing to relatively stable eastern and western ancestry groups. The two lines of evidence had been difficult to reconcile.
Now, an international research team led by the
University of Vienna
has found genetic evidence that helps bring those pictures together. In a study published in
Science Advances
, researchers combined new and previously published genomes with human DNA recovered from cave sediments, uncovering evidence of both long-distance genetic exchange and populations that endured in the same regions for thousands of years.
Eastern and western populations exchanged genes
The clearest evidence of those distant connections came from a woman whose remains were discovered at Isturitz Cave in southwestern France. Her remains yielded the oldest genome-wide dataset yet obtained from a modern human in southwestern Europe. Genetic modeling places the exchange between eastern and western populations around 32,500 to 31,500 years ago, before she lived.
“Our results show that eastern and western European populations were not as genetically isolated as previously assumed,” says first author Pere Gelabert, Department of Evolutionary Anthropology at the University of Vienna. “Gene flow across such large distances adds a new dimension to our understanding of how Gravettian populations were connected.”
She was not the only person to carry evidence of these connections. A previously studied individual from Ormesson, France, showed a similar genetic signal. When considered alongside archaeological findings, the results also strengthen the possibility that Isturitz served as a meeting place for different groups, although the DNA cannot reveal exactly how those encounters occurred.
Western European ancestry survived the Ice Age
Yet contact across Europe did not necessarily mean that established populations disappeared or were replaced. In northern Spain, researchers uncovered another part of the story: western European ancestry persisted for thousands of years, including through some of the harshest conditions of the last Ice Age.
Genomic evidence from Chufín Cave points to this long-term continuity. At El Mirón Cave in Cantabria, the researchers went a step further, recovering human genetic information without relying on bones or teeth. A sediment layer dating back approximately 22,000 years contained enough human nuclear DNA to identify the genetic ancestry of people who had occupied the cave, despite the absence of human skeletal remains in that layer.
The DNA revealed that western European ancestry had persisted through the Last Glacial Maximum, when Ice Age conditions were particularly severe. Together with the evidence from Chufín, this supports the idea that the Iberian Peninsula served as a refuge where human populations endured during a period of extreme cold.
“Sedimentary DNA allows us to recover genetic information from periods where human remains are missing,” says senior author Ron Pinhasi, Department of Evolutionary Anthropology at the University of Vienna, whose team led this study. “This gives us a way to connect archaeological layers with the genetic ancestry of the people who occupied a site.”
Ancient family offers clues to inbreeding avoidance
In southern Italy, the team examined a different aspect of ancient population life through the remains of Ostuni1b, a male fetus who was most likely the son of a previously studied woman known as Ostuni1. Genetic analysis suggests that his father probably belonged to the same population as his mother, yet the parents were not closely related. The researchers interpret this as a possible sign of mating practices that helped prevent high levels of inbreeding, even among people who shared a common genetic background.
These findings offer a more complicated picture of Ice Age Europe than one divided into isolated eastern and western populations. Genetic ancestry could endure in a region for thousands of years while connections between populations extended across much greater distances. The evidence suggests that remaining part of an established regional population did not necessarily mean being cut off from people elsewhere.
Gelabert’s team is now extending this research by combining sedimentary DNA with advanced proteomic analyses, which examine proteins, to investigate the earliest expansions of modern humans across Europe. The approach may also help researchers understand how these populations interacted with carnivores at archaeological sites where organic remains are too scarce to provide a clear record of the past.
Reference: “Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM” by Pere Gelabert, Susanna Sawyer, Vanessa Villalba-Mouco, Olivia Cheronet, Victoria Oberreiter, Diego Gárate, Christian Normand, Lawrence G. title: Japan’s proposed solar panel recycling rules would leave perovskite out for now
content:
Japan’s proposed solar panel recycling rules would leave perovskite out for now
Japan’s Ministry of the Environment and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) have proposed leaving perovskite solar cells out of the scope of the country’s new solar cell waste recycling law, at least for now. The proposal was presented at the first meeting of a study group that is drafting the law’s subordinate regulations, held on October 30.
According to the ministries’ materials, organic solar cells, a category that includes perovskite, are not yet widespread and have no established recycling technology, so they are not proposed as a covered cell type. Flexible panels made with glass fiber are also proposed for exclusion, as no recycling technology or processing route exists for them yet. The ministries say the scope would be reviewed as technology progresses and markets develop.
The proposal would cover silicon, CIGS and CdTe modules, including double-glass and building-integrated panels, with a minimum weight of 3.7 kg per panel. Commercial owners disposing of 50 metric tons or more of panels would have to file a disposal plan in advance. The ministries estimate that this threshold would cover about 38% of the panel waste expected between 2027 and 2050. Final values will be set in the implementing regulations.

title: Researchers identify the spin mechanism that limits spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites
content:
Researchers identify the spin mechanism that limits spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites
Researchers at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, the Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Huazhong University of Science and Technology have identified the mechanism that limits spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites, and used it to demonstrate such lasing at low temperatures. Spin-polarized lasers could be used in secure communication, optical interconnects and other photonic devices, but they need spin states that last long enough to be sustained during lasing.
Quasi-2D perovskites are promising gain media because their structural asymmetry gives strong spin-orbit coupling. The same coupling, however, makes spins relax quickly. The team found that the dominant relaxation channel is the Bir-Aronov-Pikus mechanism, driven by electron-hole exchange interactions within excitons. To get around it, the researchers compared two organic cations in FAPbBr₃-based quasi-2D films: phenylethylammonium (PEA) and 1-naphthylmethylamine (NMA). NMA, with its lower triplet energy, captures triplet excitons, and its film showed only a fast spin decay, with a temperature-independent lifetime of about 7.2 ps. In the PEA film, triplet excitons remain in the perovskite layers, where reverse intersystem crossing activates a second spin-relaxation pathway (the D’yakonov-Perel’ mechanism). The result is a spin lifetime of 35.4 ps at 77 K, about five times the BAP-limited lifetime, which falls to 17.0 ps at room temperature.
The longer spin lifetime also helped the optical gain. Under circularly polarized excitation, the PEA film’s gain threshold dropped by half compared with linearly polarized excitation, and its peak gain coefficient rose 2.1-fold, from 1,410.5 to 2,983.7 cm⁻¹. The film showed spin-polarized lasing below 200 K, with a threshold 30.2% lower than under linear polarization. Above that temperature the spin lifetime becomes comparable to the exciton lifetime in the lasing regime, and the advantage disappears.
The team describes the lasing as random lasing from the polycrystalline film. It was optically pumped, and the key results were obtained at 77 K. They say the work contributes to the development of perovskite spintronic devices.

title: 重磅成果集中发布：2026数字能源白皮书正式亮相、2027专项报告编制同步启动-索比光伏网
content:
在为期一日的技术研讨、产业对接分享全部结束后，2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛迎来最受行业期待的成果发布环节，论坛将行业两年间在物智融合、数字能源领域沉淀的系统研究成果集中对外披露，为当前处于转型探索期的能源数字化产业输出了成体系的共识性指引。
白皮书发布和报告编制启动仪式在论坛成果发布环节举行，由世界物联网大会执委会副主席张华主持。
世界物联网大会执委会副主席张华
本次论坛一大成果是形成了《数字能源白皮书2026——物智融合，开启数字能源新征程》并启动《万物智联-Agent与Token赋能能源数智化(2027)》报告编制，总设计师林承桢在发布白皮书时讲话。他表示，继2025年第一届智慧能源论坛进行《万物智联驱动数字能源革命》2026年度报告编制启动仪式上他提出顶层设计、技术路径、核心技术、标准编制与国际合作提供基础做了宣讲后，编制团队就为深入调研生态与场景，团队聚焦AI+能源与能源数智化，进一步聚焦新型电力系统-AI Agent、物联网和Token开展工作。编制团队由行业政-产-学-研-金单位的多位专家组成，包括老中青结构的学者和工程实施专家。认为在当前行业处于内卷的状态下，要提高行业服务的质量，编制调研报告和白皮书、蓝皮书，汇集行业共识，并不断迭代。探索行业思路的创新，是一个非常伟大艰巨和必要的工作。2026年，我们正站在万物智联与物智融合的交汇点。这本白皮书是我们对这个起点的系统回答，也希望能成为各位推进数字能源的工作底稿。欢迎大家共同交流和批评指正。
《数字能源白皮书2026——物智融合，开启数字能源新征程》主笔、无锡灏宏能源科技有限公司合伙人牟英峰发布白皮书时讲话。他表示，受世界物联网大会组委会委托，在主编单位、参编单位、编制专家和评审专家的共同努力下，以研究设计初稿为基础，经过两轮专家评审和修订，编制小组完成了白皮书的编制工作。他先用一句话概括这本报告：能源的世界，正在从“哑”变“聪明”。他指出，物联网与人工智能正在重塑传统能源体系，将零散的光伏、风机等能源设备全面联通，让整个能源系统实现可感知、可计算、可调度、可交易。行业运行逻辑迎来本质革新，彻底从“人找数据”转变为“数据找人”，从传统的“源随荷动”，升级为源网荷储全域智能互动。本次白皮书重点提出万物智联核心理念，突破了单纯设备联网的浅层认知，构建起从感知、决策到确权、流通的全流程智能闭环，带动能源行业发生五大深刻变革：能源生产向柔性分布式转型、电网实现双向互动、行业管理全面AI赋能、能源价值更加多元，能源数据也正式从运维附属数据，转变为可确权、可计量、可入表的核心生产要素。明确了2026至2030年行业发展路线与政策建议。报告以数据要素、可信数据空间、数据资产为主线，推动能源数字化升级为国家级基础设施体系，依托标准共建与市场化跨境运营，助力物智融合落地，为数字能源发展提供重要实践依据。
随后，林承桢就《万物智联-Agent与Token赋能能源数智化(2027)》报告编制启动讲话。他表示，在2027年开启《万物智联-Agent与Token赋能能源数智化(2027)》，现在也开始编制，欢迎大家择机共同参与和研讨。
发布仪式由梁志鹏、曹军威、王永杰、吴静、赵风云、
竺新原、于鸿雁、张海勇等见证嘉宾出席。
成果发布环节结束后，论坛开展跨领域开放式圆桌交流，不同细分领域的嘉宾跳
出单一主题的分享边界，围绕行业当前最受关注的共性议题展开深度碰撞，为全天的密集分享补充更具落地参考性的共识内容。
圆桌讨论与交流由胡兆光主持，议题为：1. AI+能源与能源数智化的核心要素与技术;2. Agent、Token如何实现双轮驱动;3. 产品碳足迹与国际市场重要路径。曹军威、吴静、王思宁、王函韵、张海勇、刘琳娜等参与讨论交流。
论坛最后举行世界物联网大会数字能源委员会新成员颁证仪式，由张华颁证，受证专家包括林承桢、胡兆光、张晋宾、牟英峰、张海勇、李菁、戴晨松、蔡漪、徐洪峰，成员单位包括京东方能源科技股份有限公司、盛隆电气集团有限公司。
由世界物联网大会执委会副主席张华作总结，祝贺各位专家正式成为委员会新成员，同时也感谢成员单位京东方能源科技股份有限公司对论坛的大力支持。指出我们今天围绕万物智联、算电协同，从技术、产业、金融、标准多维度进行充分交流，完成白皮书发布、报告启动、专家聘任等多项重要工作。期待未来我们聚力共生，携手共建全球数字能源新生态，共同助力全球碳中和事业。到此，2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛全部议程圆满结束。

title: ‌算电协同跨境破局：绿色投资、可持续金融与电力标准数字化共筑数字能源新底座-索比光伏网
content:
在完成技术层面对Agent、Token与算电协同的深度研讨后，2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛专门设置了本届论坛新增的「国际市场、标准和绿色金融」专题单元，从产业落地的配套支撑维度展开分享，补上数字能源从技术概念走向规模化商用的关键环节。
世界物联网数字能源委员会、上海新能源行业协会专家、总策划竺新原
本单元由论坛总策划竺新原主持，她在开场中特别强调，数字能源不止是技术创新，更离不开跨境投资、绿色金融、标准化体系的支撑，这也是相较上一届论坛特别增加金融板块的核心原因——通过技术、产业、资本、规则的完整联动，形成深入推动数字能源发展的全链条闭环。
国际投资促进会副理事长兼秘书长刘琳娜
国际投资促进会副理事长兼秘书长刘琳娜作了《面向AI算力全球化布局的绿色基础设施跨境投资机制探析》演讲。她指出，在AI算力加速走向全球的浪潮下，算力配套绿色基础设施跨境投资迎来全新挑战，传统新能源投资研判模型已不再适用。算力、能源、合规三重耦合，催生复合型跨境投资新机制。
她介绍，作为注册于美国华盛顿州的国际性非政府非营利机构，GIC汇聚全球政产学研高端资源，拥有平均30年以上国际投资促进经验专家团队，业务覆盖22个国家，促成200余个国际投资项目，总规模超百亿美元，可为企业提供智库咨询、资源对接、全链条项目落地一站式服务。
她分析，算力出海投资主要面临三大底层矛盾：资产久期错配、跨领域风险传导、东道国公共利益平衡。算力设备3至5年快速迭代，而绿电基建回报周期长达20至30年;芯片管制、跨境数据合规风险会直接传导冲击绿电资产现金流;项目还需适配当地社会接纳度、电网承载与国土治理要求。市场普遍存在“电价低即项目可行”等认知误区，不少海外算力配套绿电项目因机制失灵遭遇搁置、取消。
对此，GIC搭建五道前置研判闸门：算力负荷核验、芯片全周期合规、跨境数据治理、能源土地并网保障、融资退出闭环，前置化解算力—绿电跨境投资各类潜在风险。GIC诚邀中外政企、产业及金融机构携手合作，推动跨境算电协同、绿色算力认证、数据中心碳足迹核算标准国际互认，打造适配算力绿电复合资产的跨境绿色金融产品。依托GIC专业研判与项目落地服务能力，助力出海企业规避海外投资陷阱，安全高效布局AI算力配套绿电跨境投资，把握全球数字能源投资机遇。
中国社会科学院研究员、中国环保产业协会政策与发展专委会副秘书长徐洪峰
中国社会科学院研究员、中国环保产业协会政策与发展专委会副秘书长徐洪峰作《支持数字能源发展的可持续金融产品创新》主题演讲，系统梳理可持续金融支持数字能源发展的最新实践。随着“东数西算”工程全面推进，绿色金融产品正加速渗透数据中心、智算中心等数字能源领域，形成多元化融资供给体系。
在绿色金融产品层面，创新已覆盖信贷、债券、租赁、保险、信托全链条。信贷方面，截至2026年6月末，国家开发银行宁夏分行累计向中卫数据中心集群投放贷款40.63亿元，其中12.2亿元专项支持大唐中卫云基地200万千瓦绿电项目，投运后集群绿电比例将达79.3%，用电价格降至0.36元/千瓦时。债券领域，金开新能成功发行两期绿色中期票据(碳中和债)，合计募资10亿元，精准投向新疆伊吾“绿电+算力”智算中心。同时，苏银金租落地6.9亿元高性能服务器直租项目，搭建万卡级算力资源池;人保财险发布全国首单算力专属保险“算力保”，为行业提供定制化风险保障;华能信托与世纪互联合作规模超16亿元，重点支持乌兰察布、太仓数据中心，项目PUE低于1.2，绿电直供占比达50%。
转型金融聚焦高碳产业低碳改造。2025年，我国可持续发展挂钩债券(SLB)发行58只，规模达458.89亿元，发行数量位居全球首位。不过，数字能源领域的标准化可持续挂钩债券仍处破冰阶段，存量产品以资产证券化工具为主，主要挂钩PUE、绿色建筑认证等能效指标。
央行结构性货币政策工具也迎来重大升级。2026年碳减排支持工具利率大幅降至1.25%，全年设定8000亿元额度并按季度常态化操作，支持范围从原有3大类拓展至节能降碳、能源转型、绿色数据中心等6大领域23个细分方向。湖南人工智能算力数据中心、甘肃庆阳绿电算力协同项目已率先享受政策红利，形成“以绿电引算力、以算力促绿电”的良性循环。徐洪峰指出，绿色金融、转型金融与央行政策工具的深度协同，正为数字能源高质量发展构建全链条、低成本的资金保障体系，有力助推“双碳”目标如期实现。
北京国网信通埃森哲信息技术有限公司副总经理王思宁
北京国网信通埃森哲信息技术有限公司副总经理王思宁作了《电力标准数字化创新发展和新实践》演讲。作为国家电网公司新型电力系统标准数字化攻关团队负责人，她系统阐述了国家电网公司在电力标准数字化领域的最新进展与创新成果。一是全球标准数字化已经迈入新阶段。从全球视野介绍标准数字化历经萌芽、探索、共识达成、战略发展四个阶段的演进脉络，2026年是标准数字化的加速之年，标准形态正加速向机器可执行的知识单元演进，呈现出“标准制修订向起草即数字化转型、标准交付转向可信内容服务、标准应用向标准即服务转变”等六大发展趋势。二是国家电网打造电力行业首个企业级数字标准馆的领先实践。目前馆藏标准1万余项，其中结构化标准9700余项，提供标准资源统一供给等十大能力，一批应用场景加速落地，比如输变电工程可研评审平台解析95项标准条款，自动化构建标准作业流程，显著提升了评审效率与准确性。三是分享攻关团队最新成果SG-SMART模型，提出构筑“即插即用”可解释可追溯的“电网标准规则引擎”等新方向。

title: 中国学者国际论坛首提TokenNet概念 构建Agent与Token双轮驱动数字能源技术底座-索比光伏网
content:
在2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛的第二主题单元中，“Agent、Token双轮驱动，聚力共生数字能源新生态”成为核心议题，中国学者首次在国际会议上提出TokenNet(词元互联网)概念，系统阐释其理论体系与工程架构，为万物智联走向物理世界提供全新安全路径。
中国电力发展促进会智库专家、国家电网能源研究院原副院长胡兆光
本单元由中国电力发展促进会智库专家、国家电网能源研究院原副院长胡兆光主持，他表示Agent智能体、Token词元技术正在成为万物智联的重要技术底座，为工业能源、零碳园区带来全新解决方案。本单元我们就围绕技术底座、工业能源闭环、零碳园区实践展开研讨。
世界物联网大会数字能源委员会副主席、中国电力发展促进会碳达峰碳中和专委会高级顾问林承桢
世界物联网大会数字能源委员会副主席、中国电力发展促进会碳达峰碳中和专委会高级顾问林承桢作了《TokenNet：词元互联网，万物智联的下一代语义底座》演讲，首次在国际会议上正式亮相TokenNet(词元互联网)概念，阐释理论体系与工程架构，提出“硅基神经系统”破解AI物理安全难题，并倡议产学研界共同推进“两次路由”与“物理熔断”相关标准建设。他从万维网Web页面、互动服务再发展至对Token语义与价值的服务，提出TokenNet概念，将TokenNet比作AI的“硅基神经系统”：“如果把大模型比作超级大脑，TokenNet就是让指令安全传导到物理四肢的神经系统。”他指出，当前AI走向物理世界面临“三重断层”：网络失语(协议层不感知业务意图)、算电协同(算力布局与绿电供给脱节)、虚实割裂(数字空间的计算错误可能直接引发物理风险)。
TokenNet并非替代TCP/IP，而是叠加于其上的“语义与物理路由膜”。其核心引擎“两次路由”在本次演讲中首次系统阐述：第一次路由通过意图向量匹配，解决“找谁做”;第二次路由定位物理执行节点并计算合规路径，解决“去哪、干什么”。
他重点介绍了“物理意图”机制：Token携带“半衰期”，过期指令在网络层即被丢弃;同时承载算力、电力、碳排放三维标签，为“算随电动、绿电优先”提供协议层支撑。在安全维度，TokenNet提出从“边界防御”走向“物理免疫”：一次路由识别异常意图，二次路由的边缘网关在指令违背预设物理规则时执行物理熔断，形成“软件防护与物理兜底”的双重机制。
他提出三阶段标准化路线图：12个月内推动网关技术规范立项，1至3年开展算力枢纽与
双域试点，3至5年推动物理熔断与AI对齐机制进入国际标准讨论。中国信息协会能源工作委员会主任委员王永杰在前期审读中认为，该架构具备成为跨境绿色算力协同“中国方案”的研究潜力。据悉，TokenNet网关原型机研发、相关团体标准预研工作正在推进中。
罗克韦尔自动化创新研究院院长李栋
罗克韦尔自动化创新研究院院长李栋在《Agent驱动的工业能源闭环和算电协同》演讲中，提出与政产学研各界代表共探数字技术与能源产业深度融合的新路径。面向能源波动、系统割裂与用能优化难等工业挑战，他以工业现场实践为切入点，阐释如何以AI Agent连接生产、能源与经营决策，通过感知、分析、决策、执行的闭环机制，让数据从“可见”走向“可行动”;并以算力需求与能源供给协同优化，推动源、网、荷、储及生产系统高效联动，实现安全、环保、节能、高效的SEEE可持续价值。作为工业自动化、信息化和数字化转型领域的全球领先企业之一，罗克韦尔自动化持续以IT/OT融合创新赋能制造业。本次分享不仅呈现Agent从辅助分析迈向自主协同的技术演进，更传递一个鲜明观点：未来工业竞争力，来自“智能制造”与“智慧能源”的双向融合。罗克韦尔自动化期待携手产业伙伴，共建可复制、可扩展的绿色制造新范式，为全球数字能源生态注入工业级创新动能。
明阳智慧能源集团股份有限公司智投事业群资深专家武镜海
明阳智慧能源集团股份有限公司智投事业群资深专家武镜海作《数智驱动，绿电新生——明阳的零碳园区探索与实践》主题报告，与全球业界嘉宾共话能源物联网的未来图景。他指出，2026年零碳园区的发展正式步入运营时代，随着相关政策标准的陆续出台和建设规模的不断扩大，工业园区已成为中国降碳的“主战场”。然而，能源、碳排、成本、市场四维协同难题，仍制约着园区的绿色转型。
为突破困局解决痛点，结合能源物联网的技术发展，明阳研发了明曦智慧能源平台。该平台以“云-边-端”为架构，基于统一的技术底座，融合MyCarbon能碳管理、MyEnergy源网荷储一体化控制、MyVPP
和MyTwins数字孪生四层结构，推动平台从“工具”向“智能体协同”跃迁，构建从资源聚合、智能预测到市场变现的全链路闭环。从技术攻坚到规模落地，明阳正以数智之力点亮零碳园区，为“双碳”目标贡献坚实力量。

title: 算电协同成行业共识 多领域专家共探AI+电力安全可控发展路径-索比光伏网
content:
在2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛的第一主题单元中，与会嘉宾围绕“新型电网与零碳技术算电协同”展开深度研讨，多位来自电力规划、能源科研领域的专家分享前沿观点，明确算电协同是保障电网安全、推动零碳转型的关键抓手。中国能源研究会首席专家赵风云主持本单元讨论.
中国能源研究会首席专家赵风云
赵凤云主持主题一 新型电网与零碳技术算电协同，她指出新型电力系统建设离不开人工智能、数字技术的深度嵌入，算电协同更是保障电网安全、推动零碳转型的关键抓手。本单元我们将围绕电力行业数字化发展、Agent与Token技术赋能能源、算电协同实现路径展开交流。
电力规划设计总院副总工程师张晋宾
电力规划设计总院副总工程师张晋宾作了《 “人工智能+”电力行业高质量发展之思考》主题讲演。张晋宾指出：AI是世界经济增长的新引擎和新旧动能转换的加速器，已被视为是继资本、劳动力、土地之后的第四大生产要素，其注定即将成为人类历史上影响深远的通用技术之一。
能源安全独立和绿色低碳升级是全球能源发展的两大核心主题。AI和能源电力是相辅相成、双向赋能的关系，一方面能源电力为AI高速发展奠定坚实的能源基石，另一方面AI可极大赋能高比例可再生能源电力系统的加快构建，强力支持能源强国建设。
“AI + 能源电力”的成功，不能只依靠技术进步，而是需要推动人、企业文化、战略规划、过程管控等诸多要素的协同发展。电力作为关键的国家基础设施，在推动“AI+电力”融合发展时，要注重价值创造，严守“AI应用三原则”：一是须“人在环中”，而不是“人在上，即影响能源电力关基安全运营的每项AI决策必须有审计跟踪及确认环节;二是需区别AI的确定性和概率性，严禁AI统计类模型直接承担电力系统关键控制回路及安全保护回路的核心功能;三是遵循AI可解释性原则，不应采用黑盒AI，AI架构应支持监督检查和推理跟踪。为保障“AI+电力行业”的高质量发展，亟需基于AI机理及应用场景，设定“AI+电力”的“红灯-黄灯-绿灯”，以确保AI安全、可靠、可控。
清华大学信息国家研究中心研究员、北京智中能源互联网研究院首席科学家曹军威
清华大学信息国家研究中心研究员、北京智中能源互联网研究院首席科学家曹军威作了《万物智联，Agent 与 Token 赋能能源数智化》主题演讲，他首先梳理了从互联网、物联网到智联网的技术演进路径，指出三者融合是大势所趋——智联网以智能体(虚拟/具身)为核心，能跨域协作、自主决策，无需人工干预。
在能源领域，曹军威提出“以能补算、以算促能”的算能融合理念。随着国家能源局推动能源数字化智能化发展，传统电力系统正转向以新能源为主体的新型电力系统，面临间歇性、不确定性挑战，亟需储能、时空转移和智能调度。
关键技术方面，智能体平台通过感知增强、规划增强、记忆增强和工具增强，结合电力、交通、环境等垂域大模型，推动能源系统智能化。曹军威还引入Tokens/kWh作为算力效率指标，衡量每度电产生的Token数量。他指出，AI Agent和Token正引爆信息技术变革，应加快借鉴智能体技术发展能源电力行业智能体，打造杀手级应用，落地集中与分布相结合的智算中心，赋能能源数智化转型。他表示，清华大学团队长期深耕AI+能源领域，致力于技术研究、示范工程和产业落地，愿意开展相关方面的广泛合作交流。
全球能源互联网经济技术研究院副院长杨方
全球能源互联网经济技术研究院副院长杨方作了《算电协同发展形势与实现路径》主题讲演，围绕算电协同的发展形势、面临的挑战以及从电力行业促进算电协同的思路路径分享观点。他指出，在迈向万物智联的新阶段，电力和算力基础设施都将成为最重要的基础设施系统。以电强算解决的是算力中心的高可靠、绿色、经济供电问题，以算促电通过算力负荷的柔性再造，一定程度上促进解决新能源消纳、电力安全和降本增效等问题。目前来看，全球主要国家的算电协同问题集中体现在前者，我国新型电力系统建设在保障算力设施供电的基础上，通过跨行业协同来释放更大的算电协同价值和潜力。
她认为，算电协同走向落地，涉及技术、业务、安全、市场、政策、生态等多个层面，应该遵循分层分级、分类施策、先易后难、因地制宜的思路。规划层面，针对绿电供应与算力负荷时空不匹配的问题，电力主动对接算力规划，多措并举增强算电规划协同性和投资建设弹性。运行层面，关键要通过将算力负荷纳入电网安全运行管理、配电网智能化柔性化升级，有效控制跨系统的安全风险。调控层面，在分类精细评估算力任务调节能力的基础上，依托平台建设实现通信对接和数据共享，破解技术和规则障碍。市场层面是实现算电协同价值的机制载体，在持续扩大绿电供应规模的同时，推动电证碳市场的有机衔接，充分体现算电协同的经济价值和环境价值，这也将是未来数字生态系统构建的重要制度基础。

title: 2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛在京召开 政产学研金共话算电协同新方向-索比光伏网
content:
11月3日，2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛在北京·中关村展示中心举行。本次论坛以“万物智联，算电协同，聚力共生，共建全球数字能源新生态”为主题，来自能源、通信、AI及金融领域的政产学研专家齐聚一堂，围绕新型电网与算电技术、跨境AI算力协同、国际标准与绿色数字金融等核心议题展开深度研讨。在此国际论坛上，中国学者首提TokenNet(词元互联网)概念，系统阐述了其理论体系与工程架构，并倡议产学研界共同推进“两次路由”与“物理熔断”相关标准建设。本次论坛还发布了《数字能源白皮书2026——物智融合，开启数字能源新征程》，并正式启动了《万物智联-Agent与Token赋能能源数智化(2027)》报告编制工作，共同勾勒了数字能源新生态的落地路径。
2026世界物联网大会第二届智慧能源论坛现场
论坛由世界物联网大会组委会主办，世界物联网大会数字能源委员会联合主办，京东方能源、盛隆电气集团担任合作伙伴，中国信息协会能源工作委员会、中国电力发展促进会碳达峰碳中和专委会、上海新能源行业协会、清华校友总会能源专业委员会(筹)、国际投资促进会等提供支持。论坛主席为何强，联合主席为曹军威、赵风云、林承桢，论坛总策划为竺新原。
世界物联网数字能源委员会、上海新能源行业协会专家、总策划竺新原
竺新原主持开场致辞环节，她强调了此次论坛策划是立足于立足全球数字经济大会发展精神，对标联合国全球数字合作与可持续发展目标，以“万物智联，算电协同，聚力共生，共建全球数字能源新生态”为主题，围绕新型电网与算电技术、跨境AI算力协同与Token出海、国际标准、绿色数字金融三大方向，深挖数字技术与能源电力产业融合实践，打通全球能源算力、电网、碳资产协同通道，深化跨国数字能源合作，协同推进全球碳中和，共筑开放可持续的全球能源数字经济新未来。
世界物联网大会执委会副主席兼秘书长何强
何副主席致欢迎辞，他代表世界物联网大会组委会向与会嘉宾表示欢迎。指出的全球能源正在经历一场由物联网(IoT)与人工智能(AI)驱动的产业变革和革命。物联网与能源系统的深度融合是全球主要经济体的共同方向。能源与各行各业密不可分，而“能源数智化”则是这场数字经济转型的核心。希望汇聚各方智慧，期待参会嘉宾碰撞思想、分享创新成果，促成务实产业合作，赋能联合国可持续发展目标，推动构建人类命运共同体，让数字经济红利惠及全球，助力能源产业绿色智慧高质量发展。
中国能源研究会可再生能源专业委员会主任委员梁志鹏
中国能源研究会可再生能源专业委员会主任委员梁志鹏致主题词。他表示，“十五五”我国将初步建成新型能源体系与新型电力系统，新能源大规模发展背景下，亟需依托数智技术重塑能源系统。随着“人工智能+”能源行动落地，AI与能源已经从单向支撑迈向双向赋能，在功率预测、设备运维等多场景实现广泛应用。
他指出，当前能源数智化转型仍存多重瓶颈：高质量数据分散，新能源发电出力特性与算力等负荷的用电特性匹配不足，负荷的灵活调节价值尚未在市场中充分体现，能源企业提供综合智慧能源服务的系统集成与运营能力有待进一步提高。
对此他提出四点建议：加快能源与数智技术深度融合，推动企业向综合智慧能源服务商转型;推动AI与电力市场机制协同创新，聚合可调资源实现多方共赢;统筹算力与新能源布局，实现绿电与数字技术双向赋能;把数智技术融入能碳管理，打通碳足迹核算、碳资产数字化管理链条。他表示，本次论坛聚焦算电协同、“人工智能+”能源等议题，期待各界凝聚共识，产出务实成果，助力能源数字化智能化升级，预祝论坛圆满成功。
中国信息协会能源工作委员会主任委员王永杰
他在书面致辞中表示，万物智联正推动能源系统从“设备联网”走向“数据要素化”，行业应把握Agent与Token双轮驱动机遇，共建开放协同的全球数字能源新生态。
他讲到，万物智联的本质，是把物理能源流转为可确权、可治理、可流通的数据要素流。绿电、绿证、碳配额、辅助服务和
响应能力等，本质上是数据确权后的权益凭证。能源数字化正从“看得见”迈向“算得清、分得明、流得动”，而要素化的首要门槛在于确权与规则。他认为，能源智能体(Agent)正从单点辅助走向多智能体协同调度，实现分钟级决策与自主运维;Token则成为算力产出与绿色价值的计量凭证，推动物理电量与数字权益双向锚定。各方应加快构建“制度+标准+平台+安全+存证”五位一体数据基础设施，推动企业、聚合商和标准组织角色重塑，让数据“敢流、愿流、能流”。他强调，中国超大规模
、特高压调度等经验正成为可输出的公共产品，但标准互认是“走出去”的前置条件。呼吁以万物智联为底座、标准互认为基础、市场互通为经济纽带，共建全球数字能源共同体。
京东方能源科技股份有限公司董事长马亮
他作了《能碳协同，AI+能源物联网技术赋能产业绿色转型》主旨演讲。他指出，绿色低碳转型不只是环境课题，更是产业能源安全课题。数智化背景下，AI是绿色转型不可忽视的核心变量：算力驱动用电负荷持续增长，放大绿电价值，助力新能源规模化发展;高比例新能源并网叠加算力、社会用电增长，也加剧电力系统供需调配压力。企业主动推进绿色转型，能够在赋能电网的同时增益自身，形成双向共赢。他表示，京东方始终坚持可持续发展，明确2050年实现自身运营碳中和，并沿绿色管理、绿色产品、绿色制造、绿色循环、绿色投资、绿色行动六条路径布局。
作为京东方旗下专注零碳综合能源服务的公司，京东方能源结合集团高端制造的建设与运维经验，沉淀出“五维一体”的零碳园区能碳协同实施路径：通过诊断摸清碳家底，制定零碳规划;以风光储充及热泵等实现源头脱碳;围绕空调、电力、水处理、气化等公辅系统推进过程减碳;以末端负碳补齐“最后一公里”;以智慧管碳形成用能、管碳的长效闭环。该路径以京东方能源自研的BES智慧能源管理系统为底座，通过AI+能源物联网技术应用赋能，构建能源流与碳流一体化数字视图，实现用能、碳排放分钟级可监可视，帮助客户用好绿电、低成本买电买碳、用能调优，赋能客户推进绿色零碳发展的同时，实现增收节支的综合效益。

title: 新疆发布《自治区能源项目开发简明手册（2026版）》-索比光伏网
content:
为持续强化能源政策公开力度和服务指导工作，确保企业能够清晰、准确地执行政策，减少企业跑办、创优营商环境，自治区能源局制发了《自治区能源项目开发简明手册(2026版)》并设置门户网站专栏，旨在为全区能源项目管理部门、工作人员及能源企业提供一份实用的工作依据和参考指南，不断夯实扩投资稳增长的基础。
自治区能源局聚焦企业需求，精心梳理了煤炭、油气、新能源、电力等领域，汇编了国家、自治区发布的部分指导性强、适用普遍、企业急需的政策文件。不仅整合梳理了项目申报流程，更明确了申报条件、材料清单、受理部门、审批流程、办理时限等关键要素，并配以简明易懂的核准审批流程图，同时向全社会公开能源局各业务处室联系信息，全方位畅通政企沟通渠道。目前，正在将《自治区能源项目开发简明手册(2026版)》分发各地州、县市能源主管部门和在疆能源企业，委门户网站底端“热点专题”板块同步公开发布专栏(https://xjdrc.xinjiang.gov.cn/xjfgw/c116393/kfjmsc.shtml)，动态更新的同时，方便社会各界下载取阅、指导工作实践。
推进能源项目建设是将能源资源优势转化为经济增长胜势的核心抓手，而优质、高效、便捷的服务、指导、帮助则是关键保障和重要举措。下一步，自治区能源局将紧跟能源产业发展的形势、趋势，依据国家、自治区相关政策和文件，及时进行补充与完善，最大限度提高知晓度和规范性，持续助力新疆能源产业迈向更高质量的发展新阶段。

title: 《青海省清洁能源产业标准体系》正式印发-索比光伏网
content:
近日，青海省市场监督管理局、省能源局联合印发《青海省清洁能源产业标准体系》(青市监标〔2026〕47号)。这是青海省深入贯彻省委、省政府产业“四地”建设战略部署、全面落实“质量强省”工作要求的重要举措，标志着全省清洁能源产业标准化工作迈入系统化、体系化发展新阶段。
青海水、光、风能资源富集，清洁能源装机占比全国领先，已形成“水风光储”多能互补的发展格局。面对产业向高质量迈进的新阶段，高原环境适应性标准、产业链数字化协同、绿色低碳评价及特色实践转化等领域标准供给仍显不足。该标准体系立足全省清洁能源产业发展实际，着力为新质生产力发展提供技术支撑，是推动产业转型升级、提升核心竞争力的基础性工程。
标准体系以国家标准、行业标准为核心支撑，以地方标准、团体标准为特色补充，采用“产业板块—产业链环节—标准属性”三级维度相结合的划分方式，形成“一个总体、四大子体系、三个层级”的总体架构。标准体系锚定五大重点任务，涵盖攻坚高原适应性标准、布局数字化协同标准、完善绿色低碳标准链、固化创新实践标准、强化标准实施与推广。
下一步，省能源局将会同省市场监督管理局，深入推进标准宣贯和实施评估，加快重点标准研究，推动标准有效供给与落地实施，为打造国家清洁能源产业高地、服务全国绿色能源高质量发展贡献青海力量。

title: HEA Energy to acquire Seaway7 Heavy Transport business
content:
Marine services company HEA Energy has signed an agreement with Seaway7
to acquire Seaway 7 Heavy Transport AS, supporting the company's strategy
to expand its service offerings.
According to the announcement, Seaway 7 Heavy Transport AS owns and operates
a fleet of six semi-submersible heavy transport vessels designed to carry
large and complex cargoes.
The acquisition will enable HEA Energy to broaden its capabilities across
the offshore value chain, offering services ranging from transportation
and installation to operations and maintenance.
Omar Elali, managing director of HEA Energy, said: "With this fleet,
HEA Energy gains a global platform, a second line of business with its
own contracted backlog and the ability to combine transport, installation
and maintenance into a single offer for our clients."
Ahmed Omar, chief investment officer of HEA Group and chief executive of
Magellan Capital, said: "Each step has added scale, capability and
geographic diversification, and this acquisition takes HEA Energy into
a new segment with a highly capable platform."
The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject
to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions.

title: DenAr wins Turkey's first offshore wind site investigation contract
content:
Offshore survey and mapping company DenAr Ocean Engineering Services SA
has been awarded a contract by Turkey's Ministry of Energy and Natural
Resources (MENR) to carry out geophysical and geotechnical ground investigations
for the NCS-01 offshore wind site.
The award marks a milestone for Denar and represents Turkey's first offshore
wind site investigation campaign, highlighting progress toward the country's
renewable energy ambitions.
Under the Agreement Denar will carry out MBES, SSS, SBP and magnetometer
surveys, UXO survey, UHR seismic, Seabed CPT and sampling from their DP2
vessel along with further laboratory testing and reporting.
According to the announcement, the contract follows two decades of marine
survey work by Denar in Turkey and international markets.

title: R G Carter awarded design and build contract by ScottishPower Renewables
content:
R G Carter awarded design and build contract by ScottishPower Renewables TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
R G Carter awarded design and build contract by ScottishPower Renewables
ScottishPower Renewables has awarded R G Carter a design and build contract
for the East
Anglia offshore wind farm
operations base.
According to the company, the £9 million facility will comprise of a three
storey building featuring office and administrative space, a control room,
a marine coordination centre and a dedicated warehouse. The contract forms
part of ScottishPower Renewables' wider £100 million investment in the
regional supply chain.
Under the contract, R G Carter is set to begin construction in 2027, drawing
on more than 100 years of experience. The company is the latest addition
to ScottishPower's East Anglia supply chain, which now comprises around
100 businesses.
Alex Mackay of R G Carter said: "Our commitment to building for the
future has seen us deliver renewable energy projects for more than 20 years,
and this project represents a fantastic opportunity for us to support the
UK's clean energy transition while creating lasting benefits for local
communities."
Jess Asato, MP for Lowestoft, added: "This investment by ScottishPower
Renewables will bring skilled jobs, training opportunities and more people
working in the heart of Lowestoft, helping to support our town centre shops,
cafés and other local businesses."

title: Ørsted reaches key milestones across global projects
content:
Ørsted reported a 19% increase in EBITDA, excluding new partnerships and
cancellation fees, for the first nine months of 2026. Installed renewable
energy capacity also increased, bringing the company's total installed
capacity to 19.5 GW.
According to the company, the increase was driven by stronger wind conditions,
higher power prices and increased generation from recently commissioned
offshore wind farms.
Ørsted said its 8.1 GW construction programme remains on schedule and within
budget. During the period, the Borkum
Riffgrund 3
offshore wind farm in Germany and the Revolution
Wind project
in the US reached commercial operation.
Several projects also achieved key construction milestones. Ørsted completed
major construction work at the Greater
Changhua 2b and
4 offshore wind farms in Taiwan, completed foundation installation at Sunrise
Wind in the US and advanced construction activities at the Baltica
2 project
in Poland.
In the UK, the developer installed the second and final offshore converter
station at Hornsea
also completed construction of a 300 MW battery energy storage system at
the project's onshore converter station, which has now entered the testing
CEO Rasmus Errboe said: "We've maintained industry-leading execution
across our construction pipeline, adding 1.8 GW of renewable energy capacity
in Europe and the US over the past few months and supporting energy security,
competitiveness and decarbonisation."

title: Vattenfall finalises Hesselø and Holmsland offshore wind agreement
content:
Vattenfall and the Danish Energy Agency have signed an agreement to support
the development of the Hesselø
and Holmsland offshore wind projects, finalising the awards granted to
Vattenfall in Denmark's August 2026 offshore wind tender.
Vattenfall said the 1 GW North Sea I Mid project will be renamed Holmsland
to reflect its location off the coast of Holmsland.
The second project Hesselø is located in the Kattegat and has a minimum
capacity of 800 MW, the two offshore wind farms are expected to support
Denmark's long term climate ambitions.
"Our focus remains clear: delivering competitive projects with discipline,
creating long term value and continuing to build momentum towards fossil
freedom," said Anne Mette Traberg, country manager for Denmark at
Vattenfall.
Under the agreement, Vattenfall will continue developing both wind farms
and said it will work closely with authorities and stakeholders throughout
the process.
According to the announcement, both projects are scheduled to begin operations

title: California Sends AI Safety Lawmaker to Congress
content: Scott Wiener , the California politician who led the successful effort to pass AI safety legislation in the state’s legislature last year, is headed to Washington. The state senator won Tuesday’s election to succeed long-time House Speaker Nancy Pelosi , after his opponent conceded on Wednesday. When Wiener arrives in D.C., he will be among the few members of Congress to have authored significant AI legislation. Last year, Calif. Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Wiener’s SB 53 , which requires the largest AI companies to write and comply with their own safety policies for managing severe risks from their technology. The bill and the AI companies that supported it could indicate the kind of AI policies that a Democrat-controlled Congress will get behind. “Scott was working on these frontier AI safety issues before it was cool,” Nathan Calvin , chief strategy officer at Encode AI , an AI policy organization that backed SB 53, told me Wednesday. Calvin said he hopes the next Congress will go further than the state bill, including by requiring AI companies to work with embedded independent evaluators and test the safety of their models. Indeed, Wiener campaigned on a promise to build on SB 53 at the national level, including by creating a federal regulatory body for AI and expanding unemployment insurance to guard against AI job displacement—a concern Anthropic leaders frequently raise. SB 53 also provides whistleblower protections and requires AI companies to report to state officials if their models are involved in safety incidents, such as theft of a model that is then used to cause harm. While Congressional lawmakers have proposed a slew of bills to regulate frontier AI models, none have actually reached a floor vote. The most significant AI-related bill to be signed into law was the bipartisan Take It Down Act , which criminalized the publication of non-consensual sexual deepfake images. But supervision of leading models from labs like OpenAI and Anthropic has been left to the Trump administration, including a June executive order that created a voluntary framework for evaluating frontier models before they’re released to the public. Wiener has spent the last few years scrapping with the same big tech and venture capital firms that will try to shape future national legislation, an experience that should give the freshman Congressman a sense of where he’ll face headwinds. In 2024, Wiener’s SB 1047 , the predecessor bill to SB 53, drew significant opposition from Andreessen Horowitz , OpenAI, Google , Hugging Face , Meta and Y Combinator , which warned it would harm innovation. Anthropic opposed some elements, such as arguing its whistleblower protections were overly broad. Newsom ultimately vetoed that bill, but set up a working group whose recommendations informed SB 53. SB 53 ultimately won an endorsement from Anthropic, as well as some safety-minded investors. In fact, Anthropic went on to donate $40 million to Public First Action , an AI safety political organization that spent $3.5 million on a super PAC supporting Wiener’s campaign. However, none of Anthropic’s donation went toward Wiener’s election, according to a spokesperson for Public First Action. Anthropic’s donation is restricted to educational initiatives and cannot be used for political spending. (Though some employees of AI companies donated directly to the campaign, leading some of Wiener’s opponents to criticize him for receiving AI funding.) OpenAI initially lobbied against SB 53 . But in September, chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane wrote that OpenAI supported SB 53 , and last month the company wrote to Newsom recommending that California strengthen the regulation. Anthropic and OpenAI’s support for regulations has raised suspicions among tech notables such as David Sacks that the AI giants are attempting to pass policies that will favor their businesses by making compliance difficult for smaller startups. SB 53 tries to sidestep this concern by focusing on AI companies generating at least $500 million in annual revenue. In Congress’s absence, other states beside California have filled the policy vacuum: copycat bills in New York and Illinois followed California’s SB 53 this year, and Massachusetts is considering a bill of its own . These state laws have built on SB 53 by requiring independent compliance audits of AI companies. That’s an idea that is already catching on at the federal level, appearing in President Trump’s recent voluntary accord with AI companies, but has yet to be turned into national law. OpenAI, Andreessen Horowitz and other AI players have argued that a “patchwork” of state-level bills could become burdensome to AI companies, but several efforts by the federal government to preempt these state bills have flopped in the absence of a national replacement. If AI advocates do accept a preemption deal in the next Congress, Wiener’s platform offers some clues as to what a federal replacement for state laws could involve. “Exactly what is and isn't worth it on preemption is a hard question, but I do think Scott is one of the legislators that I would trust to really try to make that deal in the interest of the public,” said Nick Beckstead , co-founder and CEO of the Secure AI Project , another AI policy organization that sponsored SB 53. To be sure, Wiener will face an uphill battle as a junior member, especially as other Democrats clamor to advance their own bills. More broadly, any legislation faces steep odds in Congress thanks to Trump’s veto power. Still, Wiener will find some natural allies on the Hill. For example, Manny Rutinel , a Democrat who authored Colorado’s 2024 law against AI discrimination, won a seat in the House of Representatives during Tuesday’s election. However, Alex Bores , the state Assemblymember behind New York’s version of SB 53, the 2025 Raise Act , lost his Congressional primary over the summer. Here’s what else is going on… People on the Move Sequoia Capital , the venture capital firm that was an early investor in Google and YouTube and wrote the first check to Nvidia , is shutting down its London office, the company said on Wednesday. The firm is making a number of other structural changes and refocusing on Silicon Valley. Cat Wu , a product lead of Anthropic’s popular Claude Code product, announced that she would be joining OpenAI to lead product management for its core products. Overheard Microsoft said last week that it spent about $5 billion less on capital expenditures in the third quarter than it had previously projected because data center capacity it was planning to rent wasn’t ready on time. Microsoft didn’t name the “third party” behind those delays, but one of them is Iren , a publicly traded cloud provider that is already facing pressure as borrowing costs have risen, The Information reported . China has blocked SoftBank Group’s $5.4 billion acquisition of the robotics unit of ABB , a Swiss-Swedish electrical and automation technology company. The Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review , part of China’s powerful National Development and Reform Commission , told SoftBank that the deal will be prohibited, ABB said in a statement on Thursday. The same office earlier this year ordered the unwinding of Meta Platforms’ $2 billion acquisition of Chinese AI startup Manus . Earnings Report Uber plans to more than double the number of self-driving cars operating on its platform over the next year, the company said on Wednesday as it reported third quarter results, with plans to arrange financing to build self driving fleets of cars. Stocks of neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius dropped 9.9% and 6.7% respectively on Wednesday, even as most tech stocks rose, a sign that investors interpreted Tuesday’s votes in favor of anti-data center candidates as particularly bad for newer cloud firms. Deals and Debuts See The Information’s Generative AI Database for an exclusive list of private companies and their investors. Isomorphic Labs , which uses AI to discover new medicines, is in talks to raise about $5 billion at a roughly $50 billion valuation. AMD agreed to acquire Taalas , which designs specialized AI inference chips, in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at about $2.9 billion , including up to $1.4 billion in contingent consideration. Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security , which tracks passwords and authentication credentials used by AI agents, for a reported $500 million . Nooks , which uses AI agents to automate sales calls and prospecting, secured a $500 million growth-capital commitment from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund. Laza Medical , which makes AI-powered robotic imaging for heart procedures, raised up to $160 million in a Series B funding round led by GE HealthCare. Sentra , which helps companies keep AI agents from misusing sensitive data, raised $150 million in a Series C funding round led by Capital One Ventures. Pliant , which lets AI agents make business payments, raised $80 million in a Series C funding round led by Seaya Nova and Speedinvest. Rivio , which uses AI to manage hospital billing, raised $33 million (R$180 million) at a $200 million valuation in an extension of its Series A funding round led by Valor Capital Group. Supa , which uses AI to run UK apartment-block management firms, raised £21 million (about $28 million ) in a seed funding round led by 2150 and OpenOcean. Brava Security , which uses AI agents to simulate attacks and test security defenses, raised $15 million in a seed funding round led by Pitango and F2 Venture Capital. Finpilot , which uses AI agents to help institutional investors with research and reporting, raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Lobby Capital. Atmospheric AI , which uses AI to track raw-material supply chains, raised $10 million in a seed funding round led by DBL Partners. Meta has acquired AI coding startup Conductor . Apple lowered its AI budget for some engineers from $300 to $200 in an attempt to rein in its AI spending, with further cuts to as little as $100 for some teams, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. title: How a Claims Investor Got Kalshi to Open a Market on the NCAA Payout
content: Kalshi wants to become a major challenger to traditional financial markets by encouraging big funds and companies to use prediction markets to protect against losses. Behind the scenes, it’s developing new contracts to win those big investors over. That includes wagers aimed at niche corners of finance like the market for legal claims, where investors buy up claims at a discount betting they’ll be worth more once settlements are resolved. Last month, at a big investor’s request, Kalshi added new prediction contracts on the timing and size of payouts in the $2.8 billion settlement between college athletes and the National Collegiate Athletic Association. The idea came from investment firm Grand Teton Systems, which has bought about $400 million worth of claims from athletes. Louis d’Origny, co-founder of GTS, said he reached out to Kalshi because he wanted a way for claim holders to hedge the risk that the payments might come in smaller or later than expected. Under a court-approved settlement from last year, the NCAA is due to distribute back pay to college athletes who said they were illegally barred from sharing in revenue it made from broadcasting their games or using their name, image and likeness. But female athletes have challenged the settlement, saying they aren’t getting their fair share compared to male athletes, and that has put payouts on hold. The size and timing of individual payouts remains a question, which could also mean different tax implications for claimants based on when the back pay hits. Though Kalshi offers yes-no bets on everything from election outcomes and sports to “Dancing With the Stars” weekly winners—and even the outcome of some high-profile court decisions like Trump’s BBC lawsuit and Amazon’s antitrust case—it didn’t have any contracts to make wagers on how the NCAA settlement will play out. D’Origny said he suggested new contracts tied to some of the yet-to-be-resolved details. About 72 hours later, two new contracts went live on Kalshi— one allowing customers to bet on whether women will get a bigger share of the back pay and a second on when payments will begin. “Whats exciting is that this is a genuine hedging opportunity for real world risk,” d’Origny said. Kalshi and rival Polymarket both see a major growth opportunity in courting big traders to their platforms, arguing that they can use its contracts much as they would traditional futures contracts to hedge against things like interest rate changes or fluctuations in prices of commodities such as oil. Kalshi, which announced last week it had raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation, says that as of September it worked with 500 institutional customers making up around 25% of its trading volume. Both businesses are still dominated by sports betting, which accounts for about 90% of trading volume on each platform, and having more financial customers could also help with the prediction markets’ regulatory standing. Sports predictions in particular have drawn the ire of lawmakers and embroiled Kalshi, Polymarket and other competitors in lawsuits from dozens of states over accusations that the firms are running illegal gambling operations. Prediction markets offer more types of bets than traditional futures markets, creating the opportunity for entirely new forms of hedges. But high-profile examples of businesses using prediction market contracts have so far mostly involved hedgers using existing contracts. They’ve included a bar in New York hedging a free drinks promotion during the National Basketball Association finals and a Los Angeles ice cream shop betting on colder weather to insure against lower sales. And while Kalshi has announced it’s worked with investors like Ark Invest to develop new contracts, the examples it has cited include bets on topics with broad interest, like non-farm payroll numbers. That makes GTS’ request an interesting test case for Kalshi’s efforts to grow its institutional business. Large class-action settlements or major bankruptcies often attract investment firms because they involve thousands of claimants who may be enticed by an up-front payment payment, especially in complex cases that could take years to shake out. Notably, GTS became the largest buyer of claims in the bankruptcy of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX. D’Origny, himself an FTX creditor, spotted an opportunity to buy bankruptcy claims at a discount from others who wanted a quick payout. GTS launched a website called FTXCreditor to solicit claims and eventually took ownership of almost 5,000 FTX claims. The long-running dispute between college athletes and the NCAA, which covers athletes who competed as far back as 2016, is proving to be another opportunity for GTS. The firm has been running a website encouraging athletes to sell their settlement claims to receive immediate cash. The website notes that almost 6,000 athletes have opted in so far. The contracts Kalshi created for d’Origny so far have drawn meager volume, and GTS itself hasn’t traded them yet because it hasn’t seen a favorable position to take. “We would hedge more exposure if we saw interesting odds,” d’Origny said. But d’Origny said the markets offer other benefits, because athletes who sell a claim to GTS could use the markets to place bets that could boost their total payoff. “This actually competes with our product offering,” he said. “We take on the risk entirely for athletes. Here they have a new avenue.” The contracts could also offer free marketing for GTS’ efforts to buy up claims. “People talking about the settlement might encourage some to sell,” he said.

title: Palo Alto Networks in Talks to Pay $500 Million for AI Security Startup
content: Palo Alto Networks is in talks to buy three-year-old Israeli security startup Clutch Security for around $500 million, according to people familiar with the matter. If finalized, the acquisition would be the fifth Palo Alto Networks has announced this year, as CEO Nikesh Arora seeks to bolster the company’s products that counter new AI threats. Clutch develops software that helps companies track passwords and authentication codes used by AI agents. Discussions are ongoing and may not lead to a deal. A Palo Alto Networks spokesperson said the company doesn’t comment about “rumors or speculation.” A spokesperson for Clutch Security didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The startup has raised more than $20 million from investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners and SignalFire. Its current valuation couldn’t be learned. The acquisition could further deepen Palo Alto Networks’ offerings in identity security—the software that helps businesses manage logins and other permissions to make sure their users only access the data they’re supposed to. Earlier this year, Palo Alto, which has a market cap of $287 billion, completed its $25 billion acquisition for CyberArk, the market leader in identity security. While CyberArk had historically focused on managing human users’ logins, Clutch tries to corral AI agents’ use of passwords and data. The cybersecurity sector has found its services in high demand from rising AI-related threats, as new AI models have shown they can find serious flaws in widely used software that attackers can exploit. Meanwhile, a string of high-profile incidents involving AI agents that have breached other companies’ systems has highlighted the need for security that labels, tracks and controls customers’ AI agents. These risks have spurred a string of acquisitions for startups that provide safeguards against AI agent blunders. Last month, HR and finance company Workday acquired startup C1.ai to manage AI agent identities alongside human identities. In August, identity security company Okta acquired Permiso Security and rival Sailpoint acquired Entro Security in June, both due to the targets’ specialization in managing AI agent identities.

title: Voters’ Gift to Big Tech
content: Voters just handed big tech a gift—and we’re not just thinking of Californians who voted against the billionaire tax proposal. (Can all those billionaires come home now?) Wednesday’s rally in the stocks of Amazon, Microsoft, Apple and Alphabet suggests that investors see lots of upside for those tech firms from Tuesday’s Democratic victory. The vote put a lot of people into office who are no fans of AI and data centers. By implication, any slowdown in AI data center development will disproportionately hurt neoclouds such as CoreWeave and Nebius—which haven’t built out their facilities as much as bigger and older cloud firms. Notably, both their stocks dropped sharply Wednesday. On the theory that anything that hurts your rivals is good for you, that’s good for big cloud firms Amazon, Microsoft and Google. A forced AI slowdown might even allow big tech firms to pull back on capital expenditures, which investors would love. (For our in-depth look at the implications of Tuesday’s vote, see here and here . Today’s edition of TITV is also worth catching for smart interviews on the election’s ramifications with investor and political strategist Bradley Tusk, nonprofit official Charles Hua and Wall Street analyst CJ Muse.) Not all of tech stock’s reaction was related to AI, of course: The Democratic takeover might also lead to an end to the Iran war and maybe curtail President Donald Trump’s tariff addiction, both of which would be good for big tech firms. There’s also just the reality that markets hate uncertainty and the election result has given us a little bit more certainty, even if it has created a new set of questions. Still, given the potential upside of the election outcome for big tech companies, it’s a bit ironic how much tech folks have bad-mouthed the Democrats over the past few years. Then again, plenty of techies are facing tougher times ahead. Aside from the stocks of the neoclouds, stocks of chip designers like Nvidia and memory chip companies Micron and SK Hynix also sold off, reflecting the fact that they all rely on continued AI data center expansion for their revenue growth. Elon Musk, who spent a fortune trying to stop the Democrats, can’t expect too much love from them now. But as our story noted, it’s unclear how much he’ll really suffer. To be sure, this is all premature (but preparing analysis without all the facts in hand is what reporters do!). It’s going to take quite a while for us to figure out how the new state moratoriums on data center development will actually play out. Some people think that those who oppose data centers will soften their tone when they realize the impact on jobs in their community. “I would hope that cooler heads would…come to realize how important AI compute is,” said Cantor’s CJ Muse on TITV Wednesday. The best part of Wednesday’s reaction might have been the jokes on X. The award has to go to this one —that Republicans are “in talks to be acquired by Bending Spoons.” Perfect. Snap’s Community Quick question: Is someone who visits your app once a month as valuable as someone who visits every day? That’s not difficult to answer, right? Any company reliant on advertising (like Snap) theoretically wants more-frequent users. Snap doesn’t see it that way, however. The company reported on Wednesday that it plans to make monthly active users its “primary audience metric,” a shift away from the “daily active user” it has long relied on. Snap says that’s because MAU “represents the scale of our community.” In other words, more people use Snap once a month than once a day. Indeed, Snap says it has 977 million worldwide monthly users, nearly twice as many as its 495 million daily active users. And its daily user counts in the U.S. and Europe have declined over the past year—although they’ve grown everywhere else—which is something that looks bad for the company. Still, you have to wonder what’s next. Will Snap shift to yearly active users if the monthly user count starts to weaken? In Other News • Uber plans to more than double the number of self-driving cars operating on its platform over the next year, the company said on Wednesday as it reported third-quarter results, with plans to arrange financing to build self-driving fleets of cars. Uber also wants to bring in outside capital to help with that effort, Chief Financial Officer Balaji Krishnamurthy said. • OpenAI on Wednesday said it was buying Pierre Computer Co., a three-year-old startup that builds software tools to help developers manage and review code. • Charge Robotics’ chief technology officer, Max Justicz, said he used a specialized OpenAI model to find a vulnerability in a popular open-source software app that would allow someone to hack into major data centers. • The Department of Justice last week subpoenaed payroll startup Rippling, seeking all documents produced during discovery in an alleged corporate espionage lawsuit the company is waging against rival startup Deel, according to court filings. • Stablecoin issuer Circle reported that third-quarter revenue jumped 17% to $875 million, reflecting mostly a one-time bump from a token sale. title: Six Ways the Blue Wave Could Shake Up AI, Crypto and Tech
content: Democrats’ stunning victories in Tuesday’s election can at least partly be attributed to the fact that they capitalized on growing voter anxiety about AI and tech. What exactly lawmakers do with their newfound political power to address those anxieties remains to be seen, though. One of their biggest priorities is likely to be more regulation of data centers, since voters overwhelmingly backed state and federal candidates who supported moratoriums on their construction. But data center pauses were not the only AI issue on the ballot: AI safety also became a central talking point for prominent candidates like Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who was elected to the Senate on Tuesday night. “When we started all of these projects politically a year ago now or so, the idea that AI would be as salient and seemingly driving a lot of the debate about what happened in the election was unanticipated,” said Brad Carson, a former Democratic congressman from Oklahoma who heads the Public First super PAC network, a political advocacy group focused on AI safety that received backing from Anthropic. “The moment has arrived.” Still, how long will the anti–data center sentiment last? How will more moratoriums on their construction impact providers of AI compute? And how will Democrats regulate crypto, and will they make life harder for Republican megadonor Elon Musk? Here are six possible outcomes for the tech industry from Tuesday’s election: A narrow window for legislative action. Growing fears about AI capabilities over the past few months have spurred a wave of legislative proposals across Congress, including comprehensive bipartisan packages that would establish frameworks for regulating frontier models from labs like OpenAI and Anthropic. Still, if Democrats had eked out a 51-seat majority in the Senate and a small edge in the House, they would have struggled to reach a filibuster-proof 60 votes in the Senate—and then faced the prospect of a veto from President Donald Trump. Instead, Democrats could end up with 55 seats in the Senate and more than 250 seats in the House of Representatives, representing a commanding majority for Trump’s last two years in office. The margin of that victory creates more optimism for passing legislation, Carson said. He predicted a sweeping bill on frontier AI regulation, similar to one floated by Reps. Sara Jacobs and Don Beyer earlier this year, would pass by the spring. Jay Carney, the former Obama White House press secretary and a longtime tech executive, said the Democrats’ majority raises the possibility of bipartisan legislation that is veto-proof—a two-thirds majority in the House and Senate—given the appetite among some Republican lawmakers to take action on AI regulation. He was hopeful that meant Democrats could be more ambitious than just holding corruption-focused oversight hearings and strive to pass bills. “People don’t want just trials in D.C.,” Carney said. “They want action.” Some AI proposals have focused on creating so-called independent verification organizations that audit frontier models and guardrails to prevent catastrophic risks, but Carson said the Democrats’ majority could spur lawmakers to push for even further action, such as creating new regulatory agencies to oversee the AI sector. Still, data center regulation, a key area of alarm among voters, will likely be left to the states. That being said, oversight will be a hallmark of Congress come January, with Democrats holding the gavel and dragging executives to Washington to testify. “They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we’ll be printing,” wrote Ed Markey, a Democratic senator from Massachusetts, on X on Tuesday night. Data center blowback isn’t going anywhere . While kitchen-table issues like rising food and gas prices drove voters to the polls, data centers still represented a top issue. In an exit poll conducted by NBC in 45 states, 23% of voters said data centers were “crucial” in thinking about their vote for Congress, with another 64% describing them as a major or minor factor. More tellingly, 43 out of 44 local ballot initiatives to restrict data centers won on Tuesday, with many over 70%. Carson said the issue is likely to dominate the 2028 election cycle given data centers’ unpopularity with voters. “This shows you where people’s heads are, and where people who are running for president in either party are going to have to go,” he said. “You don’t run into a freight train of an 80/20 issue that’s salient to people.” Adam Kovacevich, a former Google executive who leads the center-left trade group Chamber of Progress, cautioned that AI safety organizations are trying to elevate their causes by “piggybacking” on data centers. “The two issues are completely different,” he said. AI safety, he said, is trying to “persuade voters to take action against an existential risk, whereas data centers are about impacting your community in a way that people can see and feel.” Even if pervasive opposition to data centers doesn’t mean voters are also allergic to AI, however, the likelihood of new moratoriums across the country will still affect many companies reliant on the buildout. A gift to big tech margins. The election results sparked wildly different reactions among investors in tech stocks. Chip stocks dropped, as did shares of the most prominent neocloud, CoreWeave, which fell more than 9%. At the same time, the three largest cloud providers—Amazon, Microsoft and Google—saw their shares jump more than 7%, 6% and 4%, respectively, outpacing the 2% rise in the Nasdaq Composite Index. The contrasting reactions make perfect sense, though. If you’re an Nvidia or a memory chip supplier like SK Hynix, anything that interrupts the data center buildout is bad news. The same is true for CoreWeave, which is already facing tough questions about whether it can access capital to build future data centers and has no other business to fall back on. In a statement, a CoreWeave spokesperson said the company doesn’t anticipate that any “shifts in the political landscape” will impact its existing customer commitments. “While future policy changes could affect data center development broadly, CoreWeave has strong visibility into its pipeline and retains flexibility to adjust where and when we build,” the statement said. “These factors limit our exposure and give us confidence in our ability to serve customers.” By comparison, the hyperscalers all have diversified portfolios of products. New data center pauses could stop future development plans, but most likely won’t impact the gigawatts’ worth of projects that are already underway. Even before the election, those companies’ investors were getting fidgety about the future capital expenditures these companies were planning. If data center legislation forces them to slow that capex spending, that will help to free cash flow at Amazon, Microsoft and Google. At the same time, if data center pauses prove fatal to neoclouds, the hyperscalers will have less competition in the market for AI compute. That could provide a boost to their margins. This could be true even for a company like Apple that isn’t in the cloud business. The iPhone maker has been forced to raise prices on its products largely due to the scarcity of memory chips, which are being gobbled up by the growth in AI data centers. If that data center growth slows, memory prices could stabilize or fall, which would be a welcome development at Apple. Its shares rose more than 6% on Wednesday. A black eye for Elon Musk, but how bad? No matter what you think of Musk’s accomplishments as a tech visionary and businessman, Tuesday’s results made it pretty clear his eye-popping investments in political races since Trump reentered the White House have backfired. He reportedly donated nearly $450 million to back Republican candidates in the midterm elections, a significant chunk of it in Texas, where his most important companies, SpaceX and Tesla, are based. Last year, he and allied groups pumped around $20 million into a Wisconsin Supreme Court race, an effort that flopped when the Trump-endorsed candidate, Brad Schimel, lost. But other than hurting his reputation as a player in electoral politics, it isn’t clear just how bad the blue wave will be for Musk’s businesses. Shares of SpaceX and Tesla dropped more than 4% and 2%, respectively, on Wednesday. Data center moratoriums could trip up future projects at SpaceX, which has quietly become a meaningful provider of AI compute to Anthropic and other customers. But you could also argue that no tech company stands to benefit more from an (improbable) total ban on data centers than SpaceX because of its efforts to put AI compute in space. Not only is SpaceX building its own constellation of orbital data centers, it also dominates the commercial rocket launching business that will allow other companies like Google to lob their own AI compute into space. “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk wrote on X late Tuesday night. SpaceX’s dominance of rocket launches also makes it unlikely that Democrats can do real damage to SpaceX’s government contracts without seriously undercutting U.S. ambitions in space. Democratic members of Congress certainly could make Musk’s life unpleasant by constantly calling him to testify or by probing his dealings with the government or his oversight of the Department of Government Efficiency. In Texas, the Democratic governor-elect, Gina Hinojosa, made Musk’s tax breaks from and contracts with the state and his relationship with her Republican opponent, Greg Abbott, a centerpiece of her campaign. Still, how likely is it that Hinojosa goes on the offensive to stop SpaceX-Tesla projects in the state, such as their Terafab semiconductor manufacturing facility? Doing anything that kills Texas jobs could blow up in her face and interrupt her political ascendancy. A crypto bloodbath. An unsung storyline Tuesday night was how resoundingly the election drove nails into the coffin of crypto’s legislative aspirations. The blockchain industry spent more than $40 million in 2024 to unseat Sherrod Brown, the Democratic senator from Ohio who oversaw the Senate Banking Committee. But Brown clawed his way back to office on Tuesday night in a special election, despite the crypto industry’s top super PAC spending $46 million on ads. Some onlookers have speculated that Brown could end up with oversight of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the small regulatory agency charged with supervising prediction markets and many crypto assets. With Elizabeth Warren likely to assume the chair of the Senate Banking Committee, two of the industry’s leading critics could have leadership roles in the next Congress. As a result, not only will the crypto industry’s hope for its flagship Clarity Act evaporate, but the industry will likely face a reckoning for its close ties to the Trump administration amid an onslaught of oversight hearings and investigations. Back on the campaign trail. While the 2028 presidential election is still two years away, the cycle starts now, according to Kovacevich. That means prospective candidates are beginning to sharpen their talking points around AI, and groups like Kovacevich’s are vying to help shape their platforms. In 2025, Chamber of Progress launched the Blue Horizon Project, an initiative to “restore tech optimism” to the Democratic Party. It is headed by Dave Vorland, a former senior official in the Biden administration’s Department of Defense. Kovacevich said the Blue Horizon Project has already met with the staff of would-be candidates, though he declined to name any, and is hiring a consultant to help engage directly with candidates. “I’ve been encouraged that a lot of the 2028 field is taking a pretty measured approach,” he said. “There aren’t that many who have called for a ban on superintelligence or data centers.” Carney is heading a similar group, Project Blueprint, created by Democratic megadonor and venture capitalist Ron Conway and announced in September. Carney said he’s met with a number of people who are likely to run for president and wants to help them work through their campaign platforms. He said the requirement shouldn’t be to have a 100-point plan on AI, especially given how fast the technology is moving, but that candidates should know what they’re talking about and have a positive message. Carney said the only times a negative, divisive message has won the presidency were in 2016 and 2024. “Not to get sentimental about my old boss, but I think that’s what people are really craving, and that includes AI. It can’t just be the industry is bad and tech is bad, and it can’t just be, ‘Get out of my way, we know better.’”
