title: How a Czech Math Professor Reinvented Solar Eclipse Photography
content:
With custom-built gear, his team seeks to solve a long-standing solar mystery
13 min read
Vertical
Advanced image-processing software developed by Miloslav Druckmüller combines scores of individual images, captured during a total solar eclipse and painstakingly calibrated. The techniques reveal fine details in the sun’s corona, which is white in this image. The tiny pink shapes seen along portions of the edge of the blacked-out solar disk are prominences, which are extensions of relatively cool plasma that can jut out hundreds of thousands of kilometers into space.
Miloslav Druckmüller, Shadia Habbal, and Václav Široký
The sun hangs low
over the plains of Castile and León, in the north-central region of Spain. But from a slope of the mountain
Pico Trigaza
, it appears that a few puffy white clouds have started to block the sun. That’s vexing.
A group of researchers, some wearing cardboard eclipse glasses, is clustered around sets of portable telescopes and cameras connected to laptops. All this gear is scattered on tabletops perched on the mountainside. On the computer screens, the sun’s disk looks like a deep orange crescent that is slowly waning. That’s because the
began to crawl across it about half an hour ago. In 25 minutes, it will obscure the sun completely, producing an eerie and wondrous phenomenon—a total solar eclipse.
In the late-summer, late-afternoon heat, the researchers watch anxiously as those fluffy clouds linger around the sun. From an abandoned hut on the slope a few meters above, where the researchers have set up camp, one of the grad students emerges and nods toward the cloud formation. “Do you think it will dissolve?” he blurts out.
“It will.”
Miloslav Druckmüller
glances calmly at his group of doctoral candidates, now making final checks of the equipment in preparation for totality. Here in Spain, on this 12th day of August, Druckmüller is getting ready for his 19th solar eclipse. He knows from long experience that weather can turn quickly when the moon’s shadow suddenly pushes the temperature down. Plus, there’s no sense in riling up the grad students any more than they already are.
Miloslav Druckmüller led the design and construction of a unique optical instrument that incorporates eight astrocameras. Each is equipped with a spectral filter for sensing and recording specific emission spectra from the solar corona. Each of those spectra, in turn, is associated with a particular ionic species of iron atoms. Because the temperature needed to ionize iron varies depending on the ionic species, analyzing the locations and relative abundance of these ionic species offers valuable insights into the distribution of heat in the corona.
Václav Široký
During totality, the moon blocks the overwhelming glare of the solar disk, revealing delicate structures in the sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona. Using custom-built
telescope
systems and image-processing techniques that Druckmüller has spent decades developing, the researchers aim to gain insights into the processes in this enigmatic region that is otherwise
hard to study
. In addition to imaging the visible coronal light, the team will try to track the dispersal of superhot ions of iron into interplanetary space, which could give rare insights into the pattern of heat emanating from the corona.
And they’ll have 107 seconds to do all that.
A Mathematician’s Path to Solar Eclipse Photography
Druckmüller is a professor of
mathematics
image processing
Brno University of Technology
in the Czech Republic and a leading figure in the
Solar Wind Sherpas
, an international team that studies the sun’s corona during total eclipses. In the solar eclipse world, he is nothing short of a legend, albeit a reluctant one.
An image from Miloslav Druckmüller’s first solar-eclipse expedition, to Hungary, vividly shows Baily’s Beads. These elongated white lights along a piece of the left edge of the blacked-out solar disk are caused by beams of sunlight shining through gaps in the irregular lunar surface during the eclipse. The pink shapes are solar prominences, which are jets of plasma extending out into space and held in place by the sun’s intense magnetic field.
Miloslav Druckmüller
He photographed his first solar eclipse in 1999, in what he thought would be a one-off lark. During that eclipse, the moon’s deep shadow missed Druckmüller’s native Czechia by just a few tens of kilometers, so he chased it to Hungary with a 30-year-old
Soviet MTO 1,000-millimeter lens
. All he remembers from that day is the rush of adrenaline he felt while trying to find the sun in the sky with the lens’s minuscule field of view and keep it in focus for the two minutes of the eclipse.
He insists that he has never enjoyed any of the eclipses he has photographed. “In fact, I have never properly seen any of those eclipses. You are just watching the screens, making sure that it’s all doing what it’s supposed to do. There are so many things that can go wrong and you can’t redo it.”
A composite sequence of photographs shows the 12 August 2026 solar eclipse as seen from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain.
Václav Široký and Miloslav Druckmüller
Despite Druckmüller’s outward tranquility on this Spanish hillside, the stakes are high. Just 45 minutes ago, his group heard from their colleagues in Iceland, where viewing conditions had promised to be better than in Spain. But a vast low-pressure system had clouded the entire sky, leaving all three Iceland teams without a view.
What Solar Eclipses Reveal About the Corona
On the Pico Trigaza mountain in Spain, two postgraduate researchers used a laser to get a rough, initial alignment for the tracking mount of an optical instrument. The alignment was necessary to precisely compensate for the Earth’s motion.
Martin Šebek
The corona has been a
for centuries. Though dimmer—by a factor of a million—than the sun’s visible surface, the corona is nevertheless extremely
: about a million degrees Celsius compared to 5,500 degrees on the surface. Because the sun’s
nuclear fusion
engine churns at the star’s heart, it might seem that temperatures should fall farther from the core.
To observe the faint corona in visible light, researchers must block the sun’s ferocious glare. Specialized telescopes called
coronagraphs
do this with an opaque disk called an occulter. But because light bends around the occulter’s edges in an effect called diffraction, it must block an area much larger than that of the solar disk to prevent light from spilling over and ruining the images. But doing so means obstructing the inner part of the corona, which harbors the most important processes that underpin the puzzling phenomena of the sun’s upper atmosphere.
That’s why total eclipses matter so much to solar physicists. By sheer chance, the moon is exactly the right size and at just the right distance to completely cover the sun during a total solar eclipse. Because the moon is so far away from Earth, the view is not marred by diffraction, and the corona reveals itself nearly all the way down to the sun’s surface.
As astrocameras recorded spectral data about the sun’s corona, a laptop computer [on table, at left] displayed the phase of the eclipse.
Václav Široký
Space probes
can image the solar surface in other wavelengths, but those views have limitations, too. Spacecraft such as NASA’s
Solar Dynamics Observatory
do see the innermost parts of the corona in
extreme ultraviolet
light, explains
Shadia Habbal
, a solar physicist at the
University of Hawaii
and leader of the
Solar Wind Sherpas
project. “But it cuts off very quickly, so you don’t see its extension into space as well as we can see it in the visible emission lines” during an eclipse. “That’s the biggest advantage,” she says, of solar eclipse photography.
The European Proba-3 mission, launched in 2024, simulates total solar eclipses by flying two spacecraft in a formation 150 meters apart with one acting as an occulter and the other as the telescope. The instruments aboard that satellite, however, have limitations compared to the equipment used by the Solar Wind Sherpas team.
How Eclipse Images Sparked a Scientific Partnership
When Druckmüller developed the film from his 1999 eclipse expedition, the photographs didn’t do justice to the event’s eerie beauty. He spent countless evenings applying his expertise in numerical image processing in an attempt to re-create in his photographs the sights he witnessed in that Hungarian corn field.
It took two years, but eventually he succeeded. Where before there were dull views of the blackened lunar disk surrounded by the blunt wisps of the corona, Druckmüller revealed the subtlest details of the magnetic field lines stretching from the sun far into space. As his photographs circulated among solar physicists, invitations to eclipse expeditions began to arrive.
Solar researchers Miloslav Druckmüller and Shadia Habbal have been collaborating for two decades and 15 eclipses.
Miloslav Druckmüller
Habbal learned about the images from a Ph.D. student who had seen them at a conference presentation that didn’t credit Druckmüller. When Habbal’s team later published the images in a paper, they misattributed them to another researcher. Druckmüller found out through an astrophysicist friend. “I wrote her a rather disappointed email and she responded within 10 minutes,” Druckmüller recalls. “She really didn’t have a clue.”
The error was corrected, and within weeks, Habbal and Druckmüller began a collaboration that grew into a friendship. “Milos’s processing brings out details that nobody has seen before, and they tell you a lot about very tiny features in the corona that you don’t see otherwise,” says Habbal.
How Image Processing Reveals the Solar Corona
Capturing the corona’s delicate structures means finding a way to show its brightest and faintest features in the same image. “During the solar eclipse, the contrast between the darkest and brightest parts of the corona is enormous, possibly one to a million,” Druckmüller explains. “But a computer monitor only allows you to display a contrast ratio of one to about 800.” (Some modern monitors, particularly
ones, can deliver higher contrast ratios.)
The human eye can adjust to this enormous range of brightness, allowing an observer to see both the bright corona and the faint stars and planets that briefly emerge in the darkened sky. To bring those details together in a photograph, Druckmüller uses custom image-processing
algorithms
to combine exposures that capture different parts of that range.
Researchers Martin Šebek and Peter Urgoš make fine adjustments to the focus and alignment of the astrocameras on a key optical instrument before the 12 August solar eclipse.
Václav Široký
To create a single image, Druckmüller’s teams need to take 200 individual frames during the eclipse at exposure times ranging from 0.001 second to two seconds. The data must then be
calibrated
against a vast number of reference images to filter out noise and imperfections.
Flat fields
, which depict a uniform light background, help correct for defects caused by telescope
, dust spots, and variations in pixel sensitivity.
Dark frames
, taken with light blocked from the sensor, help correct for artifacts created by the camera’s image sensor itself. “It takes the computer more than two days to process one image,” Druckmüller says. Including the calibration data, a single finished image requires about 3,000 input frames.
Choosing a Location for Solar Eclipse Photography
Since 2008, teams directed by Habbal and Druckmüller have traveled to every total solar eclipse, spreading out across multiple locations to hedge against bad weather. About half of the teams return with usable data. For the others, it’s just a short and stressful voyage. For the 12 August eclipse, three groups deployed to Iceland and two to Spain.
The teams seek sites close to the center of the band of totality, where the moon blocks the sun for longest. In Spain, the 12 August
band of totality cut across the north of the country
; the center line of the shadow passed within 11 kilometers of Pico Trigaza, promising Druckmüller and his colleagues a precious 107 seconds of totality.
But duration is only part of the calculation. Totality on Pico Trigaza will commence 51 minutes before sunset, with the sun just 8 degrees above the horizon. That low, the rays must pass through a much thicker layer of the atmosphere than when the sun is higher in the sky, increasing the light distortion that complicates photography. At the researchers’ camp on Pico Trigaza, 1,600 meters above sea level, the thinner air should help a bit.
An abandoned hut on the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain was spruced up so that it could serve as a home base for the research team recording the 12 August solar eclipse.
Martin Šebek
“Iceland would have been a much better place for us than Spain because the sun was higher up, some 25 degrees above the horizon,” Druckmüller says wistfully. But Iceland’s notoriously unpredictable weather made Spain an essential backup.
If you pack a van with thousands of dollars’ worth of cameras and optical gear and then set out on a 2,351-kilometer journey, you shouldn’t be surprised if you finish the trip with a few striking photographs [top]. The sleeping arrangements for the grad students at the Pico Trigaza hut [bottom] were spartan, but the views were first-rate.
Top: Martin Šebek; Bottom: Václav Široký
On the mountain, locals have spruced up a rustic, long-unused hut for the researchers, running power cables from a nearby telecommunication outpost and bringing in a water tank. Five Ph.D. students drove more than 2,000 kilometers from Brno and have spent nearly a week preparing the equipment. Druckmüller and his wife joined them two days before the eclipse. They cook on a small propane grill and sleep in sleeping bags on yoga mats. “We have plenty of space here to set up our telescopes, beautiful views, and a roof over our heads,” Druckmüller says with a grin. “It’s perfect.”
But even the best equipment and a carefully chosen site count for nothing if the clouds roll in. “So much work goes into the preparations and then, if you end up with nothing, you just feel terrible sadness,” says
Jana Hoderová
, an assistant professor of mathematics at Brno University of Technology and one of Druckmüller’s key collaborators.
As the moon continues to slide in front of the solar disk, the pesky cumulus cloud that kept everybody on edge begins to dissolve. It’s 10 minutes to totality. The relief is palpable.
Mapping the Solar Corona’s Temperature With Iron
The countdown on the computers that control the cameras has begun. The screens are now showing only a tiny orange sliver, and the evening is becoming perceptibly less bright.
Twenty astrophotography cameras, most of them drawing power from a car battery that was also buffering the cameras from any grid instabilities, are pointed at the sun. Alongside equipment capturing the corona’s visible light, the team has built an assembly of eight cameras to detect light emitted by various iron ions that arise in the corona.
Among the optical gear assembled at Pico Trigaza to capture the 12 August solar eclipse was a unique instrument designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona [at left].
Václav Široký
Those instruments looking for iron ions have been put together with resourcefulness and thrift. A colleague of Druckmüller’s laser-cut the aluminum plates holding the carefully aligned lenses in exchange “for two bottles of whisky.” The brackets and attachments were 3D-printed at Brno University of Technology. The lenses, produced for the defunct camera maker Contax, were bought at steep discounts on eBay. By far the most expensive elements are interference filters that isolate the wavelengths emitted by the iron ions.
Around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still.
“That’s something nobody else in the world can do,” Druckmüller says with visible satisfaction. The unique technology, codeveloped with Habbal’s Hawaii team, has already enabled researchers to map the
distribution of temperatures across the entire corona
and to discover previously unseen structures, dubbed “smoke rings,” in the coronal
. The photographs also revealed the boundary region where the solar plasma becomes so thin that its ions stop colliding.
The optical assembly designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona is outfitted with astrocameras, each of which captures spectra from a different ionic species. To do that, each astrocamera is equipped with a spectral filter whose bandwidth is so narrow—one nanometer—that the filter appears as a mirror.
Martin Fornůsek
“Iron is the most abundant of the heavy elements that we see in the solar corona,” says Habbal. “And because the corona is so hot, the iron atoms lose electrons and get ionized. The larger the loss, the higher the temperature.”
For example, a temperature of around 1.6 million °C is necessary to produce an iron ion that has lost 12 electrons. But only 1.4 million °C is needed to strip an iron atom of 11 electrons. Once it’s in a particular electrical state, the ion retains its specific ionization, even as it travels outward with the
solar wind
. Each of those ions, whether +11 or +12, emits a different wavelength of light, allowing the researchers to map not just temperatures within the corona, but also how those iron ions spread into interplanetary space and distribute heat. Habbal and her colleagues had long been trying to image those iron ions during solar eclipses. But it wasn’t until Druckmüller entered the picture that they were able to develop the gear and the mathematical techniques to do it.
Three, Two, One…Totality
With just a minute to go to totality, the researchers begin removing protective filters from the lenses. It’s 50 minutes to sunset, and the waning sun has just begun to light up the clouds above the horizon with the first tinge of orange. Then, suddenly, the evening begins a rapid and premature descent into darkness. Along the edge of the fantastically thin solar crescent, the brilliant orange points known as
Baily’s Beads
flash and disappear—the last fragments of photospheric light visible through deep lunar valleys. As totality begins, observers remove their glasses. The hot air cools. The graduate students remain quietly and intently focused on their gear.
Druckmüller looks up from his camera toward the darkened plains. Around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still. The sky is ablaze with fiery colors all along the horizon where the deep lunar shadow drops off.
burns brilliantly in the southwest, a sharp white pinpoint in the darkened sky. The sound of camera shutters suddenly fills the air. Then, as quickly as it fell, the darkness begins to recede, bid farewell with another handful of golden Baily’s Beads.
The crowd erupts in cheers. The Ph.D. students throw themselves at each other and hug like they mean it.
“The students did most of the work this time, so I actually allowed myself to really look at it,” Druckmüller says. “It was beautiful. Pico Trigaza may not have been the best for science photography, but from the aesthetic point of view, it was extraordinary.”
The 2026 solar-eclipse team at Pico Trigaza in Spain included [from left] Magdalena Šrotířová, Peter Urgoš, Martin Fornůsek, Miloslav Druckmüller, Václav Široký, and Martin Šebek.
Václav Široký
But for Druckmüller, this is just the beginning. While other eclipse chasers will race to release their images, he will take his time. He expects to publish the first
visible-light images of the corona
in about two weeks. Processing the iron-ion images, and uncovering whatever insights they may hold, will take months—maybe even a whole year.
“Probably until the next eclipse in 2027” in North Africa, Druckmüller says.
Who knows? Maybe he’ll even enjoy that one, too.

title: AI数据平台OceanBase获颁世界互联网大会杰出贡献奖
content:
11月3日，在2026年世界互联网大会乌镇峰会开幕式上，由蚂蚁集团打造的自主数据平台OceanBase获颁“世界互联网大会杰出贡献奖”。它的获奖，大会颁奖词一语道出要义：“OceanBase打造人工智能（AI）数据基础设施，服务全球数字经济发展。”
当前AI落地要考虑的问题不再是模型够不够“聪明”，而是数据能不能被AI真正用好。当AI从生成内容走向执行任务，数据基础设施也从后台支撑走向产业竞争的关键环节。如何将分散的企业数据转化为AI可理解、可检索、可调用的数据资源，成为AI规模化应用必须跨越的一道门槛，也为新一代AI数据库打开了产业空间。
而这正是OceanBase正在践行的价值方向。正如OceanBase CEO杨冰所说，“AI要真正释放价值，必须建立在能够统一管理全量数据、实时支撑交易与分析的底座之上。数据库要从记录系统进化为智能数据底座，帮助企业把分散的数据转化为AI可调用、业务可使用的数据资产，释放AI时代的企业数据价值”。
AI落地卡在“数据多但用不好”
过去两年，AI迅速进入各行各业。但直到AI真正深入业务系统后，很多企业才发现数据不少，AI却未必用得上。
原因并不复杂。企业的数据往往分散在数据库、文档、图片、音视频等不同系统和格式里。结构化业务数据和非结构化知识“各管一摊”，彼此缺少关联。
“AI要回答一个业务问题，既要懂企业知识，又要会看实时数据，还要能安全调用，这背后需要大量数据整合和知识加工。”一位企业负责人说，大模型像一个知识面很广的新员工。公司的账本、档案、生产数据分散在不同柜子里，格式还不同，如果不先整理成它能查、能懂的资料，“新员工”再聪明也没法干活。
一言以蔽之，谁能让数据真正被AI用好，谁就掌握了AI落地的关键基础设施。
“数据库的角色也因此发生变化。”杨冰说，它不再只是记录业务交易的“账本”，而要进化为智能数据底座，把分散的数据转化为AI可调用、业务可使用的数据资产。
湖库一体让“数据合在一起用”
OceanBase给出的答案是“湖库一体”。
湖库一体，简单来说就是把“擅长快速记账、查账”的数据库和“擅长存放各种格式海量文件”的数据湖装进同一套系统。过去，企业业务往往需要多套系统分别支撑，数据在系统之间反复复制、同步和治理，链路长、成本高。湖库一体通过统一架构减少跨系统流转，推动数据从分散存储走向统一管理和协同使用。
2026年，OceanBase发布湖库一体AI数据库，将数据库与数据湖能力融入统一架构，支持结构化、半结构化和非结构化数据的统一管理。杨冰介绍说，通过湖库一体、多模态数据管理等技术创新，OceanBase旨在推动一个系统同时承载交易处理、实时分析与AI应用等功能。这意味着，数据库不再只是企业数据的存储和处理工具，还是连接业务系统与AI应用的统一数据底座。
“湖库一体不是把数据湖和数据库简单拼在一起。”杨冰解释说，OceanBase重在数据治理，让AI既能查“字面”，也能查“意思”，还能结合业务条件找答案。
具体而言，OceanBase通过多模态数据模型，将文本、图片、音频、视频等数据与业务数据关联组织，并把模型生成的摘要、标签和语义信息纳入数据库管理；同时结合关键词、语义与业务条件的混合搜索，帮助AI从分散数据中获取相关知识，再结合实时业务信息形成更完整的上下文。
当AI进一步走向自主执行任务，数据基础设施还要为智能体提供持续运行的数据支撑。杨冰介绍说，为此，OceanBase通过提供独立数据空间、数据分支和快速回滚等能力，支持智能体保存和调用上下文、隔离不同任务的数据，并在探索失败后恢复数据状态，相当于给AI智能体准备了一个可管理、可复用、可恢复的“工作台”。
目前，OceanBase已在蚂蚁阿福、蚂蚁灵光、理想汽车等数十个用户场景中开展实践应用。例如，蚂蚁阿福基于OceanBase统一管理文本、语音、健康记录及智能设备数据，支持长期记忆、历史对话检索与健康趋势分析；理想汽车则将研发文档、测试数据、会议纪要等组织为可复用的智能体记忆，支撑2500多个智能体协同办公。
这些实践表明，数据底座的价值正在从支撑业务运行，延伸到帮助AI理解业务、参与业务和创造业务价值。
在产业需求痛点上迭代和延伸
OceanBase此次获得“世界互联网大会杰出贡献奖”，背后有一条持续10余年的技术演进路线。
2010年OceanBase在蚂蚁集团起步，2014年开始支撑支付宝核心交易，2015年扛下“双11”全部交易流量，2017年替换掉蚂蚁核心系统中最后一个Oracle数据库，2019年“双11”处理峰值达每秒6100万次，还曾打破TPC-C等国际数据库基准测试世界纪录。
打赢互联网的“硬仗”后，它又进入要求更高的金融行业。目前已有近七成万亿级资产的银行客户用它承载核心系统，75%的头部保险机构、80%的头部券商也在用它。此外，OceanBase支撑的数字政府覆盖22个省份、20大类政务场景，更有1/3央企的核心系统、三大运营商近4000个核心节点运行其上。赛迪顾问、沙利文、IDC等多家机构报告显示，OceanBase位居中国分布式数据库市场第一，并连续3年位居金融行业分布式数据库本地部署市场第一。
从分布式数据库到湖库一体AI数据库，OceanBase面对的产业问题在变，但技术演进的逻辑始终一致：围绕企业不断增长的数据需求，持续突破数据处理、管理和使用的能力边界。杨冰告诉记者，从分布式数据库到一体化数据库，再到湖库一体AI数据库，OceanBase走的不是“追火逐热”路线，而是同一套底层能力在产业需求痛点上的迭代和延伸。
现在，OceanBase希望把在中国核心业务场景中锤炼出的数据库与AI数据底座能力带入全球市场。
杨冰介绍，以东南亚及“一带一路”共建国家为重点，OceanBase将持续深耕亚太市场。从中国核心业务场景的长期验证到亚太市场的持续拓展，中国数据库正在从技术应用走向全球数据基础设施建设的广阔舞台。在他看来，“世界互联网大会杰出贡献奖”既是一个认证，也是一个起点，希望这个统一、实时、多模态的数据底座能长期服务于全球数字经济。

title: 中韩具身智能技术产业合作论坛在韩国举行
content:
近日，中韩具身智能技术产业合作论坛在韩国首尔举行。本次论坛由中国驻韩国大使馆主办，韩中数字经济研究院、中关村企业驻韩国首尔服务代表处、中日韩创新合作中心承办。来自中韩两国政府机构、科研院所、高校和企业的代表围绕具身智能核心技术、产业应用、商业化挑战及技术标准等议题展开交流，探讨两国科技产业合作路径。
中国驻韩国大使戴兵在论坛致辞中表示，中韩两国在具身智能领域各具优势，双方应把握具身智能发展带来的合作机遇，推动共同制定监管框架、技术标准和伦理规范，在智慧城市、医疗、养老等应用场景开展合作，共同进军国际高端市场。中韩两国应在合作中拓展共同利益，共同推动互利合作提质升级。
北京人形机器人创新中心首席技术官唐剑介绍了中国具身智能技术研发及产业应用的最新进展。他表示，在中国具身智能机器人已应用在电力巡检、物流搬运、实验室自动化等领域以及导览、迎宾等商业服务场景。
韩国首尔大学机器人国家研究所教授李东俊表示，当前机器人在智能架构、训练数据获取和硬件性能方面仍存在技术瓶颈，制约了人形机器人在实际生产场景中的应用，希望韩中两国科研人员加强合作，共同推动相关技术取得突破。

title: 这款国产通用Agent，拿下一项大奖
content:
11月2日，浙江乌镇，2026年世界互联网大会领先科技奖名单公布。阿里智能体平台Qoder凭借在编程智能体Harness上的技术突破和领先的全球市场份额入选，成为国内唯一获得该奖项的通用智能体（Agent）产品。
获奖之外，另一份成绩单同样醒目：今年7月，国际咨询机构IDC发布2025年中国人工智能（AI）编程市场份额报告，Qoder以47.6%的市场份额位居第一，超过第二名至第五名的总和；到2026年秋，Qoder已服务全球超过800万用户，超10万家企业已接入Qoder。
从2025年6月阿里成立面向Agent时代的Qoder产品线团队算起，这一切只用了500多天。一支内部孵化团队，在微软、谷歌、OpenAI等巨头环伺的赛道上，把“编程Agent”这个公认的核心技术壁垒，做成了中国科技企业第一次大规模商业兑现的样本。
500天， Qoder是如何跑完这段路的？这要从丁宇（花名叔同）的加入说起。
给AI装上“工程化的身体”
2010年加入阿里的丁宇，此前的十几年都在与云计算的“幕后工作”打交道：全面容器化、统一调度、混合部署，推动阿里巴巴业务整体云原生化上云。这些工作，极少出现在公众视野里。
转折发生在2023年，大模型的编程能力尚不成熟，业界只有Cursor、GitHub Copilot等少数玩家。丁宇敏锐地嗅到AI编程（AI Coding）的巨大潜力，并开始与公司内部大模型团队紧密协作，主导研发了通义灵码——Qoder的前身。
2025年初，丁宇向阿里高层汇报AI Coding业务并得到支持，当即就决定孵化这个业务。2025年6月，在核心研发、产品等团队组建完成后，Qoder团队应运而生。
这是阿里内部最早的智能原生（AI Native）团队之一：不光产品用AI打造，团队的研发范式本身就是一场实验——人与智能体共生协作，重新定义生产关系与生产力。
这支“特种部队”用行动验证了组织实验的价值：团队成立仅两个月，首款产品Agentic编程平台Qoder就正式上线。一款创业公司通常需要一年到两年才能交付的产品，在这里从零起步到发布，只用了60天。
Qoder上线即引发关注，靠的不是噱头，而是一种全新的开发范式。
阿里官方对它的定义是“为真实软件开发打造的AI原生IDE”——一个“自带AI大脑的编程软件”。它不仅提供传统代码编辑器的能力，还内置智能代码补全、AI对话编程、自主编程、知识库Repo Wiki、项目级上下文理解等功能。开发者可以直接在里面和AI协作写代码、调试、重构，甚至让AI自主完成较复杂的编码任务。
要理解Qoder的技术突破，需要先理解一个关键词：Harness。
如果说大模型是“聪明的大脑”，那么Harness就是让大脑真正能干活的“工程化的身体”——它负责把开发者的意图转化为任务规划，管理海量代码上下文，调度工具执行，校验运行结果，再把反馈喂回模型。
编程Agent的强弱，一半取决于模型，另一半恰恰取决于这具“身体”的工程水准。
Qoder在编程智能体Harness上的突破，正是其此次斩获世界互联网大会领先科技奖的核心理由，这也是AI编程领域公认的大模型和桌面Agent工具的核心技术壁垒。
更具破壁意义的是联合设计——Qoder实现了模型、Agent运行框架与产品的协同打磨，让Agent真正理解工程、自主编写工具、完成研发任务。
丁宇说，“大脑”与“身体”协同进化，是单纯调用外部API的“套壳”产品难以复制的路径。
Qoder迅速成为中国AI Coding工具的标杆，并为整个产品家族提供统一技术底座：Qoder JetBrains插件、Qoder CLI、Qoder企业版与Teams版接连发布——仅半年时间，一套覆盖不同开发者习惯的全产品矩阵搭建完成。这在AI时代以前，是难以想象的速度。
800万用户的背后：千行百业的认证
技术突破最终要靠商业兑现来证明。在Qoder全球用户超800万的背后，是一个个真实的企业场景。
在吉利汽车，智能座舱的工程师借助Qoder快速搭建网页预览界面，一次可生成五六版车机图文方案，先在电脑上比较、再到车端验证——过去需要三到五轮台架或实车验证的调整，如今开发周期大幅缩短；智能驾驶团队则用AI辅助编写繁琐的单元测试，把精力集中在关键情况是否覆盖、结果是否正确上。
在东方航空，Qoder被引入官方App研发，推动App开发全面转向AI原生模式。在中国石油，团队从零学习Qoder开发，仅用两个月便上线4个智能体，接入86个业务工具和超15个技能，完成集团超级App的智能化改造。在南京大学，基于Qoder开发的污水处理系统大幅压缩了从工程构想到系统落地的周期。
更有说服力的是“行业外”的认可。三维CAD企业山大华天旗下的CrownCAD接入Qoder，实现了对STEP、IGES等通用三维数据交换格式的特征识别与参数化重建；盐池滩羊产业领军企业“西鲜记”，基于Qoder搭建了覆盖养殖全流程的AI管理系统，服务3个养殖场上万只在栏滩羊的日常饲喂、生长监测和出栏决策，每年可避免数百万元的损失。
从汽车到航空，从石油到滩羊——当“养羊场”都能用编程Agent搭建自己的管理系统时，“编程”正在从一门专业技能，变成千行百业的生产力工具。
这些应用案例，也意味着Qoder已成为全球变现速度最快的编程Agent应用之一。当大量AI应用还在为“用户愿意为什么付费”焦虑时，Qoder用真金白银证明：靠谱编程智能体的价值，企业愿意买单。
而获颁“世界互联网大会领先科技奖”，则是行业权威组织对Qoder“重大科学价值、引领行业技术变革、创造广泛效益”的确认。作为国内第一个获奖的通用Agent产品，Qoder代表中国科技企业在全球Agent应用竞赛中跑在了前面。
从写代码到“碳硅共生”
Qoder的野心不止于“让AI写代码”。
近期，团队用18天开发上线了国内首个数字员工产品QoderWake，让组织里多出一种生产可用、安全可控、持续进化的数字员工，通过“碳硅共生”实现10倍的生产力提效。
研发的场景也在持续外扩：团队今年6月推出远程控制功能，用户在桌面端使用Qoder，可在手机上查看进度、审批操作、追加指令；10月底，桌面端互联功能上线，用户可以在常用的Qoder桌面客户端中连接另一台设备的Qoder桌面端，发起任务、跟进进度、补充要求、预览远端结果。
从桌面到手机、从单人协作到组织级数字员工——Qoder描绘的前景清晰可见：不是替代程序员，而是让每个人和组织都拥有随叫随到的“数字同事”。这正与Qoder团队一贯的主张呼应：智能化编程的终点，是帮助企业完成向AI Native组织的进化。
2025年6月，一支内部团队悄然成立；两个月后产品上线；半年里产品矩阵成型；随后市场份额登顶、用户破800万、进入Gartner挑战者象限、IDC中国AI编程市场第一、世界互联网大会领先科技奖……这500多天之所以值得记录，不只是因为它快，更因为它验证了一个范式的成立：当大模型的“大脑”与工程化的“身体”深度耦合，当组织本身先成为AI Native的实验场，编程智能体就能从演示走向生产，从工具走向商业闭环。
Qoder技术团队表示，乌镇的领奖台不是终点。尽管在这场竞赛的第一轮商业兑现中，他们代表中国公司“率先撞线”，但AI编程的竞争远未终局，他们会继续前进，去探索这个范式能走到多远的地方。

title: 中国科大发布开源RNA序列基础模型
content:
近日，中国科学技术大学教授周少华、特任研究员熊鹏团队发布一款开源RNA序列基础模型structRFM，提高了模型在RNA结构预测与功能推断一系列下游任务中的性能，有望助力人工智能驱动的科学研究、生物学机制理解、药物发现等。11月5日，相关研究成果发表于国际学术期刊《自然》。
RNA（核糖核酸）是一种重要的生物大分子，存在于生物细胞以及部分病毒、类病毒中，广泛参与蛋白质合成、基因表达调控和RNA剪接等生命过程，其功能与序列、折叠结构密切相关。RNA分子通过碱基配对形成二级结构，并进一步折叠为三维构象，这些结构影响着分子的生物学活性及其与其他分子的相互作用。因此，理解序列、结构与功能之间的联系，是揭示RNA生物学机制的重要基础，也是药物发现的支撑要素。随着测序技术的发展，研究者积累了海量 RNA 序列数据。借鉴自然语言处理中的预训练方法，RNA 基础模型能够从这些数据中学习序列规律，提取可用于不同任务的通用特征，为结构预测和功能分析提供支持。
此次研究旨在将结构知识融入大规模序列学习，同时保持模型在不同结构与功能任务中的适应性和泛化能力。研究团队研发了RNA基础模型structRFM，首先构建了约2100万条经计算注释的序列-二级结构配对数据。在此基础上，设计算法同时预训练学习序列上下文与结构依赖。预训练后的模型仅需输入序列，即可提取序列级、核苷酸级和核苷酸对级特征，用于多种结构与功能推断任务，并在多项任务中达到国际前沿水平。
实验显示，structRFM 在零样本同源性分类中表现良好，并提高了二级结构预测性能；将其特征融入三级结构预测模型后，也改善了三维结构及其对应二级结构的预测结果。在功能推断方面，模型支持剪接位点预测、内部核糖体进入位点识别和非编码RNA分类。此外，模型在新发布的RNA家族上保持了较好的二级结构预测表现，并通过分段策略扩展至长非编码RNA分类。消融实验进一步验证了结构信息的引入及掩码策略对模型性能提升的作用，为算法设计提供了实验支持。
研究人员介绍，目前，实验室已开放完整配对数据、模型权重和源代码，为研究结果的复现和相关模型的开发提供了可复用资源。

title: AI主导设计的创新药何时上市
content:
每一款成功上市的创新药，通常需要耗时10年、平均投入10亿美元，且成功率仅约10%。这是业内的“三个十定律”。
今年9月，两款由AI技术赋能的创新药相继取得关键进展：一款宣布获批上市，另一款完成临床Ⅲ期首例患者给药。“AI制药”由此再度成为行业热点。人们不禁要问：AI究竟能否改写创新药研发的行业定律？
然而，截至目前，全球尚无一款由AI完全主导设计的药物获批上市。据知名全球性战略咨询公司艾意凯统计，目前全球AI发现或赋能的在研资产已超过100个，其中约60%—70%处于临床Ⅰ期，25%—30%处于Ⅱ期，极少部分产品进入Ⅲ期。
9月18日，工业和信息化部等十部门联合发布的《医药工业发展“十五五”规划》提出，“十五五”时期我国首创新药占全球比例要达到25%以上。规划明确提出开发应用AI赋能靶点筛选、药物分子设计与优化等多种场景。
规划甫一出台，业界反响热烈。
那么，AI到底给创新药研发带来了哪些利好？它颠覆传统创新药研发路径和流程了吗？在AI赋能新药研发过程中，还有哪些现实瓶颈？围绕这些问题，科技日报记者采访了多位行业专家。
哪些环节可以“加速跑”
创新药研发周期长、投入高、风险大，从药物发现、临床前研究、临床试验，到最终上市，就像一场超长接力赛。不同的是，比赛有终点，创新药研发始终伴随着不确定性。
受访药企普遍认为，AI已深度嵌入新药研发全流程，并以前所未有的速度重塑药物发现的各个环节。
“确定临床前候选物，是从科研发现通往药物开发的分水岭，也是企业决定要不要继续投入研发的关键节点。”迈威（上海）生物科技股份有限公司海外首席医学官胡柯说。AI恰恰在这个环节按下了“加速键”。
AI提速创新药研发，究竟能快多少？两款药给出了看得见、可量化的答案。
9月2日，西湖大学宣布，该校与西湖实验室、西湖制药（杭州）有限公司联合研发的艾普司韦近期正式获得国家药品监督管理局附条件批准上市。
它是国内首款凭借AI辅助研发而获批上市的原创药，从源头发现到完成临床试验仅用时三年半。该药可用于治疗成人轻型、中型新型冠状病毒感染。
西湖大学在瞄准抑制新冠病毒的热门靶点3C样蛋白酶后，将目光投向包含多达490亿种化合物的DNA编码化合物库，并利用AI从中筛出了100多个“潜力股”。
按传统做法，这些“潜力股”仍需逐一合成和验证，耗费大量人力、物力。但这次，AI模型仅用几天便将“潜力股”迅速缩减至9个，其中6个表现出很强的病毒抑制活性。随后，团队通过成药性评估锁定候选分子，编号WLU6937。至此，西湖大学团队只用了6个月。
“在筛选准备和筛选过程中，我们利用AI模型帮助确定筛选条件以及对照化合物，提高筛选的成功率。”西湖大学生命科学学院教授黄晶告诉记者。
无独有偶，9月10日，英矽智能科技（上海）有限公司宣布，由AI赋能发现和开发的Rentosertib已在北京协和医院完成临床Ⅲ期试验的首例患者给药。Rentosertib是一种特发性肺纤维化小分子抑制剂，从靶点发现到被确定为临床前候选化合物，仅用时18个月。
英矽智能在《自然·生物技术》杂志刊发的论文揭秘了AI如何赋能Rentosertib迈出成药的关键一步：借助靶点发现引擎PandaOmics锁定靶点TNIK，再经生成化学引擎Chemistry42虚拟筛选与迭代优化，仅合成并测试了不到80个分子，就获得了候选分子INS018_055，最终确定临床前候选化合物。
2025年12月，口服减重创新药MDR-001以令人惊讶的速度，启动临床Ⅲ期试验。该药由杭州德睿智药科技有限公司研发，从项目启动到临床前候选化合物仅用8个月，仅用19个月即获得中美针对肥胖症和2型糖尿病的新药临床批件，并用四年半推进至Ⅲ期临床研究。而对比同期传统研发模式，同类药物往往需要8—12年的研发周期。
“我们发现，AI明显提升了分子筛选与多目标优化环节的效率。”德睿智药创始人兼首席执行官牛张明告诉记者。
在分子设计环节，AI把亲和力、毒性、稳定性和成药性等多个目标纳入同一优化框架之中，在海量化学空间中寻找最优解。“MDR-001便是利用全链路AI制药引擎MAP（Molecule Arts Platform）找出来的‘优等生’。”牛张明说。
AI在药物发现环节的应用更加深入，越来越多药物研发项目因此跑出“加速度”。今年7月，工业和信息化部发布《人工智能高价值场景应用案例集》。广药数科联合华为、首芯分子共同申报的《国产算力驱动的新药创制AI智能体研发与应用》项目入选。据介绍，该项目已完成概念验证测试，有望把苗头化合物发现周期从12—18个月缩短到1—3个月。
“AI提速增效作用是肉眼可见的、实打实的。AI正推动智能设计、实验验证与临床反馈紧密协同，改变新药研发范式，帮助更多患者早日用上好药。”牛张明说。
如何拓展研发新空间
“我认为，未来AI创新药最值得期待的突破之一，是帮助我们发现过去未被认识的疾病机制和药理作用，开发出疗效更好、安全性更高、真正具有临床价值的创新药物。”合肥综合性国家科学中心大健康研究院高级研究员宋明虎告诉记者。
如今，AI制药不再局限于围着已知靶点 “做文章”，而是能够从海量生物数据中“揪出”此前被忽视甚至从未发现的新靶点，建立靶点和疾病之间的关联，打开新药研发的新空间。
众多药企由此看到新机遇。
“如果一位研究人员过去一辈子能对100个靶点进行筛选评估，那么有了AI，他可以做1000个。”药物牧场联合创始人兼首席运营官许枞用“放大效应”解释AI为创新药带来的实质性提升。
据许枞介绍，药物牧场利用AI已在乙肝、心血管疾病、肾病等疾病领域识别20个潜在新靶点，正在推进多个首创新药进入临床阶段。
靶点锁定之后，研发迈入分子设计环节。AI进行蛋白质预测与设计则是另一项具有里程碑意义的突破。
此前，美国人工智能公司DeepMind研发的AI系统AlphaFold破解了困扰人类50年之久的“蛋白质折叠问题”，使科学家能够在没有晶体结构的情况下，高精度预测天然蛋白质的三维构象。“这可谓根本性突破，对科研人员弄清引发某些疾病的机制作用非常大。”宋明虎说。
包括2024年诺贝尔化学奖得主、美国华盛顿大学教授戴维·贝克在内的科学家们开发的生成式AI系统RFdiffusion（RFD），能够从头设计自然界尚未发现的蛋白质。今年10月发布在《科学》杂志的报道称，RFdiffusion3（RFD3）能够直接从原子层面设计蛋白质和核酸，其生成蛋白质结构的速度约为第二代系统的10倍。
研发人员期待的下一个突破，是借助AI推动药物研发从静态蛋白结构研究走向动态构象分析，为过去难以成药的棘手靶点寻找新的干预可能。
以过去公认的“不可成药”靶点KRAS为例。作为最常见的致癌驱动因素之一，KRAS基因突变与多种癌症的发生发展密切相关。
攻克KRAS的难点之一在于，其部分可供药物结合的口袋在传统静态结构中并不明显，而是在特定构象状态下才会出现。科学家通过共价化学探针和结构生物学实验发现了KRAS G12C的隐藏口袋，为后续抑制剂开发奠定了基础。
“最初发现这一口袋并不是AI的贡献。但如今，AI模型可以生成蛋白质在不同时间与构象状态下的动态轨迹，帮助研究人员探索隐藏口袋如何形成、开放和关闭。这有望揭示传统静态结构研究难以捕捉的潜在结合位点，为难成药靶点的药物设计提供新思路。”上海科学智能研究院AI科学家杨自雄告诉记者。
距离上市还有几道坎
尽管AI已展现出颠覆性潜力，但在业内人士看来，完全由AI主导的新药研发仍面临多重现实障碍。
采访中记者发现，行业内主要面临两大核心难题。
一是缺乏能够支撑因果推断的高质量动态与干预数据。当前AI制药使用的数据涵盖蛋白质结构、分子活性、多组学和细胞实验等多个层面，但许多数据缺乏连续时间观测、明确的实验干预条件及跨尺度关联信息，因此难以完整重建从分子作用到细胞响应的因果机制。
“研究生命系统的因果机制，仅仅知道某个时间点发生了什么是不够的，还需要了解系统如何随时间演化，以及在不同干预条件下如何响应。”杨自雄以抗癌药物作用于肿瘤细胞为例解释道，若实验仅在给药后某一时间点采样，就很难重建从药物结合、信号传导到细胞表型变化的完整过程。
此外，蛋白质、细胞、组织和器官尺度的数据与模型尚未充分贯通，进一步增加了跨尺度机制解释的难度。
“要增强AI对生命系统的因果理解，需要建设具有较高时间分辨率、明确干预条件和标准化实验记录的高质量数据集。”杨自雄表示，这需要自动化实验、高通量检测、动态多组学采集及标准化数据治理等技术共同支撑。
二是“湿实验”验证跟不上。AI能在一夜之间生成上万个成药假设，而人类验证这些假设的速度仍相对滞后。
AI使计算机模拟的“干实验”效率显著提速——在电脑上建模、筛选分子，通过更新模型、算法或计算参数快速迭代。但归根到底，药物还要回到“湿实验”进行线下最终验证——在实验室里动手做实验。真实实验往往成本高、周期长，无法像计算机那样快速迭代，目前“湿实验”验证速度并没有因为AI的出现而大幅加速。
“这是限制整个生命科学进步的一个重要瓶颈，也是AI创新药研发下一阶段的核心发力点。”许枞说。
破局的两个关键要素在于加速实验验证与构建高效的干湿实验闭环。
建设全流程自动化智能实验室，并将AI接入实验设备，是AI推动“湿实验”“提速”的必由之路。因为自动化实验室可以支持样品处理、培养和检测的7×24小时运行。
但单纯提高“湿实验”速度还不够。核心在于将其产生的训练数据反哺给AI，实现干湿实验数据闭环。“湿实验”每一次验证产生的成功或者失败数据，都能成为AI强化学习能力的“养分”，帮助它提高预测准确率，从而减轻后继验证压力。
许枞表示，药物牧场正在多地建设自动化实验室，推进干湿实验融合与快速迭代。“我们希望AI设计好分子后，由药物化学家完成合成，再交由生物部门进行测试，拿到数据，再让AI进一步优化分子设计。”
全球科技巨头同样在积极推进。
今年2月，OpenAI与合成生物学公司Ginkgo Bioworks宣布达成合作。GPT-5输出实验设计方案后，后者的自主实验室系统快速开展实验，全程无需人员持续值守。
9月，Anthropic公司证实，其已在旧金山湾区建设湿实验室，利用Claude智能体在实验室里指挥机器人开展验证。
10月16日，谷歌官方技术博客发文介绍，其研究团队通过将AI智能体置于物理实验室机器人中，能实现设计分子、安排实验、分析结果并根据反馈调整方案的闭环迭代。
“当AI完全实现自主设计方案、开展实验验证、主动纠错并优化方案时，它或许就不再只是‘工具’，而更接近一位‘科学家’。”胡柯说。
未来十年路在何方
当下，全球AI制药市场呈现爆发式增长。艾媒咨询数据显示，全球AI制药市场规模从2021年的7.9亿美元增至2025年的24.1亿美元，预计2026年将达到29.9亿美元。
中研普华产业研究院预测，2035年全球AI制药市场有望突破460亿美元。未来十年，AI制药将驶入增长快车道。
从全球市场规模看，北美地区占据约42%市场份额，在资本、算力、管线等方面领跑。美国将AI药物研发置于AI、生物科技和国家科技竞争力框架下。2025年11月，美国启动“创世纪计划”（Genesis Mission），旨在建设一个统一的国家级AI科研平台。
今年7月，美国启动“生物创世纪计划”，其目标是在未来5至10年里，让生物医学创新整体提速。该计划由美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）牵头，依托人工智能、先进算力、创新政策治理机制等，推动生物医学前沿探索。
NIH表示，这项计划并非只是把AI套用到现有的研究流程之中，而是重塑研究人员、科研机构、数据资源与科研基础设施之间的协作模式，攻克关键的生物医学难题。加快新药研发与临床转化便是六个攻关方向之一。
亚太地区是全球增长最快的创新药市场。尤其是中国生物医药领域，其勃兴已成为行业共识。
国家药监局9月披露，今年以来我国创新药对外授权交易总额已突破1200亿美元，达到2025年全年总额的九成。据统计，今年以来有59个创新药获批上市，其中13个为新机制、新靶点的首创新药。
2025年，多项政策相继出台落地，为行业释放了强烈信号。4月发布的《医药工业数智化转型实施方案（2025—2030年）》提出，研发推广AI药物发现与设计等医药工业软件，鼓励地方、园区、龙头企业等打造人工智能辅助药物设计、生产制造、流通供应平台。11月，多部门发布《关于促进和规范“人工智能+医疗卫生”应用发展的实施意见》，要求面向重大疾病以及罕见病和特定人群的疾病，开发新药筛选模型，加速新药智能研发。
今年1月，工业和信息化部等八部门印发《“人工智能+制造”专项行动实施意见》，提出“建设人工智能驱动的新药发现与虚拟筛选平台，通过多模态药效预测大模型，加速靶点识别与候选药物发现，降低药物研发周期与成本”，这使产业更加振奋。
我国持续加强国家级和区域性科技创新平台建设。以北京昌平实验室、上海临港实验室及合肥综合性国家科学中心大健康研究院等为代表的高水平科研平台，正推动人工智能、生命科学与药物研发深度融合，促进数据、算法、算力与实验验证的有效协同，并通过集聚高水平科研人才、深化跨学科与跨机构合作，为AI创新药研发营造良好的区域创新生态。
近年来，中国与赛诺菲、辉瑞、阿斯利康、武田制药等多个全球知名药企在AI制药领域的合作持续提速。今年，英矽智能与施维雅达成8.88亿美元AI药物发现合作，被称为“全球AI药物递送第一股”的剂泰科技与礼来达成11亿美元合作……
“依托国内雄厚的生命科学人才储备、日益增强的原始创新能力，以及扎实的工程化管理能力，我国新药研发从实验室到临床的‘快速执行’能力在全球范围内首屈一指。”宋明虎坚信，“在全球医药行业进入拼速度、拼成本、拼源头突破的新阶段，中国必将加速跃迁为‘全球创新策源地’。”

title: 智能互联网让智能体既“连得通”又“信得过”
content:
打车订餐、制定旅游规划、整理会议纪要……越来越多的日常事务正在被智能体“代劳”。如何让它们相互识别、安全协同，成为智能互联网发展必须回答的新课题。
11月4日，2026年世界互联网大会乌镇峰会“智能体互信互联互操作全球合作创新——携手构建智能互联网论坛”举行。论坛发布《智能互联网创新发展合作倡议》（以下简称《倡议》），推动各方共探智能互联网发展路径。
“智能体作为推动智能互联网发展的关键力量，正加速从对话交互向自主执行跃升、从局部辅助向全流程协同深化、从单体运行向跨域互信、互联、互操作演进。”国家互联网信息办公室副主任王京涛在论坛上表示，希望进一步凝聚各方共识，共建智能原生、开放创新、安全可信、普惠共享的智能互联网。
网络技术架构亟须升级
智能体的发展，首先带来的是网络连接对象和连接规模的变化。
“过去互联网连接的主要对象是人、机、物，未来还将包括智能体，以及数据、模型、Skills（技能）等各类要素。”中国工程院院士、中国移动总工程师、首席科学家王晓云表示，连接规模可能从过去的亿级向千亿级甚至万亿级拓展。
连接对象增多、协作规模扩大，对网络能力提出新要求。王晓云认为，网络服务范式将从过去的“尽力而为”转向面向高价值业务提供差异化保障，对时延、抖动、可靠性等指标提出更高要求。在模型训练和推理过程中，智算中心之间需要实现互联，网络协议也需要适应新的业务需求。
“今年可以说是智能体元年，智能体的出现对互联网技术架构提出新需求。”王京涛表示，应坚持创新驱动，加大对新型网络通信理论、智能原生网络架构等关键共性技术的研发投入，突破智能体环境感知、复杂推理、长程规划、可靠执行等技术，提升网络智能化水平。
为此，《倡议》提出，深化技术创新，驱动网络演进；共建基础设施，畅通泛在互联。协力推进IPv6、5G-A/6G、卫星互联网、智能算力等新一代信息基础设施协同部署与互联互通，为智能应用和服务的普及提供支撑。
互认互信机制加快建立
如果说网络基础设施解决的是智能体如何连接，那么互信机制要回答的就是智能体之间如何安全协作。“智能互联网不是人工智能技术在网络上的叠加应用，而是网络架构、资源组织与服务形态的系统性重构。”中央网信办数据与技术保障中心副主任、高级工程师薄兆一表示。
他提出，数量庞大的智能体需要标识、寻址与相互发现，网络不仅要解决“连得通”的问题，还要解决“认得出、信得过”的问题。因此，身份标识与互操作协议成为智能互联网发展的基础性技术议题。
蚂蚁集团副总裁、支付宝及大安全事业群首席技术官陈亮也认为，智能体时代需要构建信任基础设施，让身份、授权与责任进入每一次连接。
“智能体的规模化上限，不在‘能不能干完一件事’，而在‘能不能被托付一件事’。”陈亮说，只有建立起可信的身份和授权机制，明确智能体的行为边界与责任关系，才能为智能体承担更复杂的任务、开展更广泛的协作创造条件。
智能体的自主性和动态变化，也给安全治理带来新的挑战。中国工程院院士邬贺铨指出，相较于应用程序，智能体会自学习、持续变化，还可能穿透调用其他智能体，给监管和责任认定带来难题。
《倡议》提出，共同制定开放、非歧视、透明的智能体互操作国际标准，建立覆盖智能体发现、协商、执行全生命周期的互信框架。通过标准和规则建设，让不同平台、不同主体开发的智能体能够在可信基础上开展协作，减少生态割裂和重复投入。
论坛上，智能体身份注册与解析平台正式发布，重点解决身份编码、跨域解析和可信互通问题，支撑不同智能体之间的互联协作。论坛还发布《智能体发展自律公约》，提出八条自律措施，涵盖健全智能体信任体系、建设智能体互联基础设施等方面。

title: SNE Research: Chinese OEMs increasingly dominate global EV battery market - electrive.com
content:
In the first nine months of this year, Chinese manufacturers secured more than half of the battery market for electric and hybrid vehicles outside China - while Korean and Japanese suppliers lost ground. This is according to a new analysis by SNE Research.
Image: Cora Werwitzke
South Korean market research firm SNE Research has analysed the dynamics and market share distribution of the EV battery market outside China. The key finding: the total capacity of these batteries climbed to 426.7 GWh from January to September. The market thus grew by 24.7 per cent compared to the same period the previous year. The clear beneficiaries are Chinese battery manufacturers.
“The combined market share of the six Chinese companies, including [CATL, BYD, Gotion, SVOLT, CALB and EVE] rose 13.3 per cent from 43.1 to 56.4 per cent, exceeding half of the non-China market,” writes SNE Research. CATL and BYD alone account for 44.5 per cent of the market. In the same period in 2023, this figure was still 36.7 per cent.
SNE Research specifically analysed the sales of batteries for battery-electric vehicles (BEVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), and other hybrids, highlighting that regional demand developed differently. The Korean analysts note that demand in Europe and Asia compensated for the ongoing weakness in North America. Interestingly, China itself also appears to be faltering. While SNE Research certifies 24.7 per cent growth for the global market excluding China, the increase including China is only 19.7 per cent. Overall momentum is thus slowing in the People’s Republic.
The following figures are available for the manufacturers themselves: The three Korean manufacturers – LG Energy Solution, SK On and Samsung SDI – contributed a total of 113.0 GWh worldwide (excluding China) from January to September, a decline of 13.5 per cent compared to the previous year. Their combined market share fell sharply by 11.7 percentage points, from 38.2 per cent to 26.5 per cent. According to SNE Research, business in North America crumbled in particular, where the installed battery capacity of the trio nearly halved from 56.1 to 28.1 GWh. In Europe, however, there was a slight increase (from 58.7 to 63.0 GWh), as well as in Asia (from 13.1 to 17.5 GWh).
But let’s take it step by step. After the first nine months, CATL once again leads the ranking. Outside China, the company achieved a volume of 143.7 GWh, which corresponds to exactly one-third of the market. Compared to the previous year, CATL grew by 47 per cent. Its market share increased by 5.1 percentage points to 33.7 per cent. For Europe, SNE Research statistics show a 35 per cent increase from 71.5 to 96.8 GWh, while in Asia, the volume doubled to 27.1 GWh.
Table: SNE Research
According to the analysts,
LG Energy Solution
maintains second place with 69.8 GWh (-4.9 per cent year-over-year). Its business in Europe and Asia developed positively. In Europe, it increased by 13 per cent to 38.6 GWh, and in Asia by 49 per cent to 11.1 GWh. However, this was not enough to offset the sharp decline in North America (-45 per cent year-over-year, from 29.9 to 16.5 GWh). LGES’s market share fell significantly by 5.1 percentage points, from 21.5 per cent to 16.4 per cent.
Next is BYD – with 45.9 GWh (+67 per cent year-over-year) – in third place. The company’s market share grew from 8.0 per cent to 10.8 per cent. According to SNE Research, this growth was distributed across Europe (17.4 GWh, +67 per cent year-over-year), Asia (14.8 GWh, +41 per cent year-over-year) and South America (7.1 GWh, +136 per cent year-over-year).
Panasonic ranks fourth after the first nine months of the year with 35.6 GWh (-0.8 per cent year-over-year). “Tesla’s North American volumes supported its results, but growth fell well short of the non-China market,” the authors said. Panasonic’s market share fell by 2.1 percentage points to 8.4 per cent. Looking further back, Panasonic’s example particularly illustrates how much the market has changed in recent years:
Meanwhile, SK On in fifth place recorded significant losses, with its volume dropping to 28.2 GWh (-18 per cent year-over-year). Its market share plummeted from 10.0% to 6.6 per cent. “The company supplies batteries to Hyundai Motor Group, Ford, Volkswagen, and Mercedes-Benz, among others, but its usage declined 46.7 per cent in North America and 2.2 per cent in Europe,” the study states.
VW partner Gotion grew by 153.8 per cent to 17.6 GWh, thereby overtaking Samsung SDI, which slipped to seventh place. Samsung SDI recorded only 15.0 GWh (-34.4 per cent year-over-year) – the sharpest decline among the top 10. Its market share fell from 6.7 per cent to 3.5 per cent. While sales in Europe remained stable at 9.4 GWh, Samsung SDI experienced a debacle in North America (-66 per cent year-over-year, from 12.0 to 4.1 GWh).
The top 10 is rounded out by three second-tier Chinese suppliers – namely SVOLT, CALB and EVE Energy. SVOLT grew by 102 per cent to 13.1 GWh, CALB by 88.5 per cent to 10.6 GWh, and EVE Energy achieved a massive increase of 215 per cent to 9.5 GWh.
In summary, it can be concluded that the three Korean manufacturers and Panasonic each had to cede market share in the global market excluding China, while the six mentioned Chinese companies consistently and rapidly expanded their volume in Europe. A major factor here is cell chemistry: “The LFP share of the non-China market rising 11.9 per cent from 15.8 per cent to 27.7 per cent reflects the same trend. In North America,” the SNE research analysts stated. This is because it is primarily Chinese manufacturers that are leading the way in LFP technology. In Europe, the adoption of LFP is increasing – “mainly in entry-level models, making price competitiveness a key criterion in supplier selection,” they added.
Based on the data, the study’s authors believe that regional political frameworks and the diversification of demand will primarily determine the competitiveness of suppliers. Some manufacturers are now increasingly shifting to batteries for stationary storage to achieve greater diversification – particularly in North America. With regard to Europe, the analysts consider the Auto Package and the associated incentive of the so-called combustion engine phase-out, as well as potential ‘Made-in-Europe’ rules, to be a decisive influencing factor.

title: Campine boosts antimony market grip with Thai stake – Batteries International
content: European lead and metals recycler Campine is to acquire a minority stake in the manufacturing operations of Thai antimony smelting and trading firm Green Tech Antimony. Campine said on November 3 the undisclosed investment marks a major step in its speciality chemicals plans and gives it access to an Asian production base for antimony trioxide (ATO) — strengthening the supply chain for its Belgium-based operations and opening new opportunities in global markets. Green Tech Antimony operates a smelter at Kanchanaburi, commissioned in 2025, with an annual production capacity of 8,000 tonnes of antimony metal. The company’s Thai partners also own several antimony mines in Southeast Asia, providing access to ore concentrates. By the end of 2027, Kanchanaburi will be expanded with a 4,000-tonne ATO production unit using Campine’s proprietary technology, creating an integrated operation from antimony ore to finished ATO. The entire ATO output will be marketed through a new trading company, majority-controlled by Campine, primarily targeting Asian markets. The deal, expected to be finalised in January 2027, follows Campine’s pledge in January 2026 to invest €7 million ($8 million) in an expansion of its proprietary antimony recycling technology, following its acquisition of two battery recycling plants and one semi-finished lead-products facility from Ecobat in France. The strategic importance of antimony to a wide range of sectors — including batteries and solar panels and for defence and advanced manufacturing applications — has grown amid global supply chain disruptions and China’s export restrictions on antimony-related products. Campine said it became the global market leader in ATO in early 2025, following exceptional supply disruptions and sharp price increases. Since the end of 2025, improved raw material availability has led to a significant correction in antimony prices. Campine CEO Wim De Vos said: “By combining direct access to antimony metal with our technological expertise and a competitive Asian production, we are creating a solid foundation for further profitable growth.” The post Campine boosts antimony market grip with Thai stake appeared first on Batteries International .

title: US unveils ‘battery leadership’ blueprint alongside PNNL-led tech consortium – Batteries International
content: A new blueprint to guide industry and academia partnerships in developing next-gen battery technologies in America has been launched by the federal government. The US energy department’s Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation unveiled its strategy for American leadership in batteries on October 27 — alongside the Battery Manufacturing Accelerator (BattMan) Consortium, led by the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), The strategy set out the energy department’s priorities to build a fully integrated domestic battery supply chain by 2030, achieve “US leadership in battery technology and manufacturing by 2035”, and accelerate the commercialisation of safe, affordable, and reliable energy-storage solutions. Meanwhile, BattMan will focus on lowering manufacturing costs, speeding the transition of novel battery technologies from laboratory discovery to manufacturing deployment, and boosting US leadership in energy storage manufacturing. PNNL is a member of Battery Council International, which praised the US national lab’s work in connecting other national labs, industry and universities on next-gen battery technologies. “BCI applauds these efforts that line up closely with what our members do every day,” the trade body said. BattMan will harness super intelligence and advanced manufacturing capabilities to identify challenges earlier and improve production processes. The accelerator will also strengthen critical mineral supply chains by advancing battery materials made from more abundant domestic elements. Assistant US energy secretary Audrey Robertson said: “The advances we make today in battery manufacturing technology will determine America’s energy security and economic competitiveness for decades to come. “The Battery Manufacturing Accelerator will fast track commercialisation, strengthen domestic supply chains and help ensure that innovative domestic manufacturing is used for the next generation of battery technologies.” PNNL won BCI’s annual innovation award in 2025 for its Grid Storage Launchpad, a new US national capability for speeding up energy storage research. Also last year, BCI hosted the inaugural Flow Batteries North America conference in partnership with PNNL. Earlier this year, South Korea’s Energy Tech Solution installed a prismatic battery assembly line at PNNL. title: EnerSys in $320m take-over of Ultralife – Batteries International
content: EnerSys is to take over New York-based battery tech company Ultralife in a $320 million enterprise value acquisition. The lead and lithium manufacturer said on October 27 the deal expands its presence in advanced, differentiated battery technologies with US-based manufacturing. EnerSys expects to realise $15 million to $20 million in annual run-rate cost synergies within the first 18 months. Ultralife, which also has operations in Canada, the UK and China, is a leading provider of rechargeable and non-rechargeable batteries, battery systems, and related accessories for military communications and other specialised applications. The transaction, expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2027, will be funded through cash on hand. EnerSys president and CEO Shawn O’Connell said: “Building on the success of our recent acquisitions, Ultralife expands our portfolio of advanced, reliable, high-performance power solutions. Together, we will be better positioned to support the US Department of War and allied forces with leading-edge, cost-effective technologies for the increasingly electrified battlefield of the future.” Batteries International reported in July 2026 that EnerSys had refocused plans for its $500 million battery cell gigafactory in South Carolina for US defence needs — and was ending a tech partnership with French Li cells developer Verkor. The move came after EnerSys announced a realignment of its previous four operating units into a three-segment operating model. title: Solid Power Announces Significant Advancement in Commercial Pathway, Commissioning MOBIUS™ Continuous Electrolyte Manufacturing Line - Batteries News
content:
Solid Power Announces Significant Advancement in Commercial Pathway, Commissioning MOBIUS™ Continuous Electrolyte Manufacturing Line
Continuous manufacturing pilot line for sulfide-based solid electrolyte designed to increase Solid Power’s annual electrolyte production capacity at Thornton, Colorado facility by 150%.
Commissioning of MOBIUS™ is underway following substantial completion of construction with materials now being introduced into the line.
Advances Solid Power toward continuous production, which will support commercial readiness and potential cost curve advancements.
Primary powder processing site acceptance testing (SAT) is complete. Full SAT is expected by the end of the month, and operational startup is planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.
LOUISVILLE, Colo.–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Solid Power, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLDP), a leading U.S.-based developer of solid-state battery technology, today announced that it has begun commissioning MOBIUS™, its continuous manufacturing pilot line for sulfide-based solid electrolyte. Previously referred to as the SP2.5 Continuous Manufacturing Pilot Line, MOBIUS™ has reached substantial completion of construction at Solid Power’s SP2 facility in Thornton, Colorado, and materials are now being introduced into the line. MOBIUS™ supports Solid Power’s objective to manufacture and sell electrolyte to Tier 1 battery manufacturers and automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).
John Van Scoter,
President and Chief Executive Officer of Solid Power, Inc, said:
Bringing the promise of MOBIUS™ to fruition is a proud moment for our team and a critical step in positioning Solid Power for commercial readiness and long-term stockholder value creation,
“The name MOBIUS™ reflects what sets this line apart: continuous production designed to deliver the process control, repeatability, and scale our partners expect from a commercial electrolyte supplier. With MOBIUS™, we expect to increase our electrolyte production capacity at SP2 in Thornton, Colorado, by 150%, and we look forward to bringing the line into full operation and supporting material qualification with our partners.”
Solid Power has also completed SAT for primary powder processing on MOBIUS™ and expects to complete full SAT by the end of October 2026. SAT is an activity performed with Solid Power and the equipment manufacturer in parallel to confirm that the equipment works as specified and designed before progressing into production. With commissioning underway, Solid Power continues to work toward plant validation and operational startup, which remain planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.
MOBIUS™ is designed to add 45 metric tons of solid electrolyte production capacity per year. Following commissioning, total electrolyte production capacity at the SP2 facility is expected to reach approximately 75 metric tons per year. MOBIUS™ will operate alongside the facility’s existing batch production lines, using what Solid Power believes is the world’s first continuous manufacturing process for sulfide-based solid electrolyte.
MOBIUS™ plays a central role in Solid Power’s commercial readiness. Solid Power believes continuous manufacturing is fundamental to achieving the volume, consistency, and cost required for commercial electrolyte supply, and expects continuous production to deliver tighter process control and more consistent output than batch processing. MOBIUS™ will also support material qualification with automotive and cell manufacturing partners as Solid Power advances toward commercial electrolyte supply.
MOBIUS™ was built as part of a project supported by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) through an assistance agreement providing up to $50 million in federal funding.

title: Samsung SDI and Alpha Omega Power Sign 1 GWh Supply Agreement for US-Made Energy Storage - Batteries News
content:
Samsung SDI and Alpha Omega Power Sign 1 GWh Supply Agreement for US-Made Energy Storage
Supply deals with AOP totaling 1.5 GWh, with all products to be manufactured at the SPE plant in Indiana
SBB 1.7 features high-nickel NCA prismatic batteries and proven fire safety, supporting AOP projects in the WECC and ERCOT power markets
Samsung SDI expands its North American ESS presence as AOP grows its U.S. storage portfolio
HOUSTON & SEOUL, Korea–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Samsung SDI today announced that its Michigan-based subsidiary, Samsung SDI America (SDIA), has signed a 1 GWh agreement to supply energy storage system (ESS) solutions to Alpha Omega Power (AOP), a U.S. utility-scale battery storage developer and independent power producer. Including an initial contract signed late last year, the two agreements total 1.5 GWh.
AOP plans to deploy the ESS solutions supplied by Samsung SDI for large-scale power projects critical for grid reliability and power demand growth, scheduled to begin construction in the WECC and ERCOT power markets next year.
Under the latest agreement, Samsung SDI will supply its Samsung Battery Box (SBB) 1.7, a fully integrated ESS solution featuring nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) batteries. All cells and modules will be manufactured at the StarPlus Energy (SPE) plant in Kokomo, Indiana, and delivered by the end of this year.
SBB 1.7 features high-capacity, high-nickel NCA chemistry and delivers 17% higher energy density than its predecessor, SBB 1.5, while maintaining the same 20-foot footprint. The solution also incorporates Samsung SDI’s ESS design expertise, including AI-powered algorithms for early anomaly detection and battery life prediction, and is designed for 25 years of continuous use.
SBB 1.7 has also obtained certifications and met safety standards including NFPA 855, the National Fire Protection Association’s standard for the installation of stationary energy storage systems, and UL 9540, a safety standard for ESS. The solution also incorporates Samsung SDI’s proprietary Enhanced Direct Injection (EDI) technology, which directly injects fire-extinguishing agents into individual battery modules, further enhancing fire safety.
Samsung SDI has secured a series of ESS supply deals with U.S. energy companies this year and continues to discuss potential supply agreements with a number of local customers, with additional orders expected in the near future.
Industry analysts attribute Samsung SDI’s recent contract wins in part to its prismatic battery technology (PrismStack), known for its strong performance and safety.
Samsung SDI is currently the only non-Chinese supplier of prismatic ESS batteries in North America. With strong durability and fire safety compared with pouch-type batteries, its prismatic batteries have helped the company meet the stringent requirements of U.S. energy companies.
Paul Choi,
CEO of Alpha Omega Power, said:
American-made ESS from Samsung SDI will play an important role in AOP’s continued growth,
“This second agreement strengthens our domestic supply chain supporting the next generation of energy infrastructure.”
Fabrice Hudry,
President ESS, Samsung SDI America (SDIA), said:
Alpha Omega Power is one of the fastest growing independent power producers in the country, and the kind of sophisticated operator we want to partner with to tackle grid reliability challenges,
“With our differentiated technology and local production capabilities, we will continue to expand our business foundation and strengthen our position in the North American ESS market.”

title: Amorphous carbon coatings for longer-lasting lithium-metal batteries - Batteries News
content:
Amorphous carbon coatings for longer-lasting lithium-metal batteries
The demand for more powerful and lighter battery systems is growing. Batteries with high energy density and long service life are in high demand, particularly for electric mobility, aerospace, and stationary energy storage. The Fraunhofer Institute for Surface Engineering and Thin Films IST is therefore collaborating with the Fraunhofer USA Center Midwest (CMW) to explore new approaches for improving the performance and service life of future battery systems. One promising approach involves lithium-metal anodes, in which lithium itself serves as the active anode material; due to its high specific capacity, this enables battery cells with potentially higher energy density.
To harness the potential of lithium-metal anodes for longer-lasting battery cells, the new research project “LIMAC – Amorphous Carbon Interlayers for Reliable Lithium-Metal Battery Cells” focuses on thin amorphous carbon interlayers. The central question is whether these layers can stabilize the interface between the lithium-metal anode and the (solid) electrolyte, thereby contributing to more reliable and longer-lasting battery cells. To this end, the first step will involve developing thin amorphous carbon layers and depositing them onto copper current collectors using an innovative laser-arc PVD process. The coated materials will then be tested in battery cells and compared with reference cells. The aim is to determine which properties of the interlayers are crucial for achieving the most stable interface possible within the battery cell.
In addition to technical performance, the project also considers the environmental perspective and the potential for transferring the technology to larger cell formats. On the one hand, a life cycle assessment (LCA) will be used to examine relevant material and energy flows as well as the environmental impacts of the approach; on the other hand, a concept for scaling the technology to larger pouch cells will be developed simultaneously. In this way, the project combines material development and cell research with environmental assessment and initial considerations for future scaling. The goal is to comprehensively evaluate the potential of amorphous carbon interlayers for more reliable lithium-metal batteries and establish a foundation for further development toward larger cell formats.
In the long term, more powerful and longer-lasting lithium-metal batteries could help reduce the weight of battery systems while enabling high energy densities. This could benefit applications where weight, performance, and range play a key role – from electric vehicles to aerospace and stationary energy storage systems.

title: ITRI Partners with eJoule, Inc to Develop Long-Life NCM Batteries and Expand Applications in Drones, Electric Vehicles, and Energy Storage - Batteries News
content:
ITRI Partners with eJoule, Inc to Develop Long-Life NCM Batteries and Expand Applications in Drones, Electric Vehicles, and Energy Storage
FREMONT, Calif., and HSINCHU, Taiwan, Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — As performance requirements rise across drones, EVs, and energy storage systems, medium and high-nickel NCM batteries are seeing strong momentum in high-performance lithium-ion applications, driven by their high energy density and ability to enable greater range and lighter battery designs. Ongoing advances in cycle life, safety, and commercialization are helping broaden their adoption across demanding applications. The Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) has partnered with eJoule Inc. to advance next-generation mid- and high-nickel NCM battery technologies. The collaboration leverages eJoule’s high-performance single-crystal nickel-manganese-cobalt (NCM) battery cathode materials and integrates capabilities across cathode materials, electrode manufacturing, and cell engineering to accelerate the transition of advanced battery materials from R&D to production. The initiative targets applications including drones, autonomous robots, EVs, and energy storage systems, highlighting the R&D strength and commercial potential of Taiwan’s advanced battery materials ecosystem while supporting a more resilient, high-performance battery supply chain.
Jeffrey Kuo-Chan Chiou, ITRI’s Vice President and General Director of Material and Chemical Research Laboratories, stated that ITRI has long been dedicated to the R&D of battery materials and cell technologies. This collaboration with eJoule Inc. combines the R&D strengths of both organizations in materials and battery technology. eJoule contributes its high-performance single-crystal NCM cathode materials, while ITRI tailors cell specifications and capacity, optimizing rate capability, cycle life, and other electrochemical performance, creating a direct link between material properties and real-life cell performance. Testing to date shows that eJoule’s single-crystal NCM cathode materials offer advantages in cycling stability and capacity retention, maintaining stable performance even after extended charge-discharge cycling, with cycle life approaching that of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. These results highlight the development potential of single-crystal NCM materials to balance high energy density with long service life while offering improved safety compared with conventional NCM materials, broadening the options for high-performance applications such as drones and EVs.
eJoule Inc. is a California based deep-tech battery materials company with established operations in both the United States and Taiwan. At the core of its technology is the proprietary Dynamic Crystallization® Process (DCP®), which produces single-crystal cathode active materials directly from solution droplets without the conventional precursor (pCAM) stage. The process simplifies manufacturing and eliminates waste associated with precursor processing, while enabling precise control over chemical composition, dopant distribution and particle crystallinity to support improvements in battery performance, stability, and safety. Built on the DCP® platform, eJoule has developed a portfolio of mid- and high-nickel NCM products for high-performance battery applications
Dr. Minduan Liu,
Vice President of eJoule Inc, said:
This collaboration brings together eJoule’s cathode material capabilities with ITRI’s expertise in electrode fabrication, cell development, and battery integration,
“Together, we can integrate development from powder through electrode to cell, accelerating the path toward commercially viable, high-performance batteries.”
ITRI is committed to deepening its partnership with eJoule Inc. to accelerate the advancement and commercial adoption of mid- and high-nickel cathode materials and battery technologies. By extending the collaboration from material R&D through battery manufacturing and market deployment, the two organizations aim to strengthen Taiwan’s battery supply chain, expand into global markets, and enable a broader range of high-performance and sustainable battery solutions.

title: Agilent and University of Chicago Launch Center of Excellence for Energy Materials Research - Batteries News
content:
Agilent and University of Chicago Launch Center of Excellence for Energy Materials Research
Agilent CoE supports research on next-generation energy storage materials
SANTA CLARA, Calif. & CHICAGO–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–Agilent Technologies Inc. (NYSE: A), a global leader in analytical and clinical laboratory technologies, and the University of Chicago, one of the world’s leading research universities, today announced a scientific collaboration to establish the
Agilent Center of Excellence (CoE) for Energy Materials Research
The Agilent CoE will be based at the University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (UChicago PME) and will support the Energy Technologies Initiative (ETI), a partnership between UChicago PME and the University of Chicago’s Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth focused on driving innovation in energy storage technologies through academic and industry collaboration.
Mike Zhang,
senior vice president and president of Agilent’s Applied Markets Group, said,
Advancing energy storage research requires both scientific expertise and the analytical capabilities to understand how complex materials behave and change over time,
“By combining the University of Chicago’s interdisciplinary research strengths with Agilent’s advanced instrumentation and applications expertise, this Center will give researchers greater capabilities to investigate these materials, tackle some of the toughest challenges in battery and materials science, and accelerate progress toward new solutions.”
The CoE will use Agilent instrumentation, including mass spectrometry and atomic spectroscopy, to help researchers investigate the materials and systems behind next-generation batteries, including batteries for electric vehicles and connected devices as well as grid-scale energy storage.
Stuart Rowan,
interim dean of UChicago PME and faculty director for ETI, said,
The most important questions in energy storage require expertise and tools from across disciplines.
”This partnership will expand the analytical capabilities available to battery researchers across the University and create new opportunities for faculty, students and trainees to work together. I’m excited that Agilent is helping strengthen the research environment needed to pursue this work across the University of Chicago and beyond,”
The CoE will support the work of the Energy Technologies Initiative by bringing together researchers from across the University of Chicago and other academic and industry partners. By combining this interdisciplinary expertise with Agilent instrumentation, the CoE will support the development of analytical methods and workflows for research on energy storage materials and systems.
Advances in energy storage will be important to applications ranging from electric transportation and connected devices to grid-scale energy systems. By expanding access to advanced analytical instrumentation and supporting application development, the CoE will help researchers investigate the materials and systems underlying these technologies.
Y. Shirley Meng,
Liew Family Professor at UChicago PME and co-director of the Energy Transition Network, said,
Advancing battery research takes more than developing a promising material; we need to understand how materials perform, interact and change throughout a battery’s life,
Meng’s research combines first-principles, computation-guided materials discovery with advanced characterization using electron, neutron and photon sources. “The Center will give researchers across the University access to some of the most advanced analysis tools for deciphering the degradations in energy storage and conversion materials and devices.”
Battery development increasingly depends on precise answers about composition, impurities, interfaces and degradation pathways, all of which can influence battery performance, lifetime, and safety. The CoE will bring advanced analytical capabilities into the research environment where those questions are being investigated.
Shrayesh Patel,
associate professor at UChicago PME, a deputy director of ETI and director of the Center for Organic Battery Innovation (COBI), said:
The batteries we rely on today depend heavily on materials that can be costly, based on critical minerals, and challenging to recycle,
“At COBI, we’re exploring whether organic materials can offer a different path—one that could make energy storage safer, more affordable, and more sustainable by leveraging earth-abundant elements. Expanding the range of materials we can use in batteries is an important part of building a more sustainable energy future.”

title: Enevate Technologies Unveils Trifecta: Battery Technology That Ends the Energy, Power, and Cycle-Life Tradeoff - Batteries News
content:
Enevate Technologies Unveils Trifecta: Battery Technology That Ends the Energy, Power, and Cycle-Life Tradeoff
Longer drone flights, full-shift humanoid robots, lighter and faster race cars, and data centers that don’t burden the grid.
IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Engineers building drones, humanoid robots, race cars, data center power systems, and electric aircraft want more energy in less weight and space, plus the power to use it. Enevate Technologies today introduced Trifecta, a licensable cell technology designed so they no longer have to choose between energy density, power, and cycle life.
Battery engineers live by an unwritten rule: energy, power, or cycle life, pick two. At the cutting edge, they often get just one, paying for it with oversized packs, shorter missions, and lost payload.
Trifecta designs match or exceed the energy density of leading lithium-metal and solid-state cells without their usual safety and charge-rate problems, and long-life configurations reach 1,000 cycles.
Benjamin Park
, CEO of Enevate Technologies, said:
Engineers have spent years designing around their batteries
“Trifecta flips that. We want to have open conversations about how our technology can change how you design things.”
Trifecta comes in five modeled configurations:
Figures are for modeled designs that build on a successful proof of concept with earlier prototype cells.
Enevate Technologies works with each customer to match or tailor a configuration, then helps get cells built by a licensee, through a custom build, or by the customer’s existing supplier.
Battery manufacturers interested in licensing Trifecta to produce cells for their own customers are invited to reach out.

title: GWM’s Svolt began mass production of 100 kWh semi-solid batteries - Batteries News
content:
GWM’s Svolt began mass production of 100 kWh semi-solid batteries
GWM’s Svolt began mass production of 100 kWh semi-solid batteries, also called liquid-solid in China. Such a pack is built on the 900V high-voltage system, supporting 6C charging. This battery is capable of adding 500 km of range in 12 minutes of charging.
Svolt was formed by GWM back in 2012 as a subsidiary focused on EV battery production. It became independent in 2018. However, Svolt is still tightly connected to GWM, remaining its core supplier and strategic partner. On October 26, the company’s officials revealed that the first “Dragon Armor” hybrid semi-solid battery rolled off the production line in Changzhou. According to Svolt representatives, semi-solid packs with ternary chemistries are a “long-term technological path.”
There is currently no information about which vehicles will adopt the newly released battery. CarNewsChina expects the Wey V8X BEV to get this pack among the first vehicles. However, Svolt chairman and CEO Yang Hongxin said that more information about this battery will be revealed soon. He also added that this pack adopts a cell-level separator transfer-printing technology. It reportedly improves battery safety during fast charging. Thanks to the liquid cooling tech, this battery supports 6C charging, allowing it to add 500 km of range in 12 minutes.
A theoretical lifetime of this battery is over 1 million km, as it can achieve 3,000 charging cycles. At the same time, it adopts six layers of protection, reportedly offering impact protection three times the level of the Chinese governmental standard.
Svolt first revealed plans to mass-produce its semi-solid batteries in May 2026. However, it initially aimed to roll out the first batch in September. At the same time, Svolt officials highlighted that pure solid-state batteries are still distant from mass production. According to China EV DataTracker, Svolt’s battery installations from January to September 2026 reached 11.27 GWh (4.23 GWh LFP and 6.99 GWh ternary NMC). It currently holds 2% of the market share in China. The company aims to achieve a full-scale transition to hybrid solid-liquid technology for its ternary battery cells by the end of 2027, and plans to launch its third-generation hybrid solid-liquid technology in 2028

title: Gumi City Launches Battery Demonstration Center to Expand Advanced Industries - Batteries News
content:
Gumi City Launches Battery Demonstration Center to Expand Advanced Industries
Following semiconductor and robot complexes, Gumi strengthens secondary battery sector with new infrastructure
A demonstration center for comprehensively managing batteries, secondary batteries, will be established in Gumi, North Gyeongsang Province.
On October 28, the groundbreaking ceremony for the BaaS, Battery as a Service, test demonstration center was held at the First Industrial Complex of the Gumi National Industrial Complex, hosted by the Korea Testing & Research Institute (KTR). Approximately 300 attendees, including Gumi Mayor Kim Jang-ho, Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan, Gyeongbuk Vice Governor for Economy Yang Geum-hee, and KTR President Lee Seung-ryeol, participated.
BaaS is a business model that provides various services related to batteries, including repair, rental, charging, and reuse. The BaaS test demonstration center, built on a 24,576-square-meter site within the First Industrial Complex, spans a total floor area of 4,231 square meters and consists of six buildings. The total project cost amounted to 27.2 billion Korean won.
The center evaluates the performance and safety of used batteries and supports their reuse in energy storage systems, ESS. KTR plans to provide full-cycle services for secondary batteries—from manufacturing to reuse—by integrating the center with its existing testing and certification systems.

title: Basquevolt and Battera Technologies announce strategic collaboration to develop next-generation integrated battery solutions for high-performance aerospace applications - Batteries News
content:
Basquevolt and Battera Technologies announce strategic collaboration to develop next-generation integrated battery solutions for high-performance aerospace applications
Vitoria-Gasteiz / Irún, October 2026.
Basquevolt S.A., Europe’s leading developer of lithium metal solid-state battery technology and manufacturer of high-energy-density battery cells, and Battera Technologies S.L., a specialist in the development, manufacturing and industrialisation of advanced battery systems, today announced a strategic roadmap to jointly develop and deliver integrated battery solutions targeting aerospace applications requiring the highest levels of energy density, safety, reliability and European sourcing.
A shared ambition: European-made batteries for high-performance applications worldwide
The partnership brings together two complementary technology capabilities: Basquevolt’s design and manufacturing of next-generation electrolyte and lithium metal cells, which already deliver energy densities exceeding 400 Wh/kg, well beyond today’s commercial lithium-ion cells, and Battera’s battery system development, manufacturing and industrialisation capabilities, including experience in demanding aerospace programmes.
Building on this performance, both companies are targeting a clear roadmap to exceed 500 Wh/kg in the coming months, a performance threshold that positions their joint solution significantly ahead of any commercially available advanced battery systems globally.
Pablo Fernández Santos,
Managing Director of Basquevolt, said:
This collaboration marks a pivotal step in Basquevolt’s strategy to deploy our technology in the highest-value applications where energy density is not a convenience but a critical requirement,
“Battera brings its expertise in battery pack development, manufacturing and integration, enabling high-energy-density solutions with rapid industrialisation and scalable production. Together, we are building something that does not yet exist at scale in Europe.”
Javier Llamazares,
Managing Director of Battera Technologies, said:
At Battera, we believe that developing advanced battery solutions requires close collaboration between cell development and battery manufacturing from the start,
“Through this partnership, Basquevolt’s advanced lithium metal technology and cell manufacturing capabilities, together with Battera’s experience in battery pack development and manufacturing, will allow us to deliver batteries with high energy density, tailored to the needs of aerial platforms, with production capabilities and scalability not currently available in Europe.”
Industrial production targeted for 2027, with the highest European content
Beyond research and development, the partnership is oriented from the outset toward industrial-scale production. Both companies have agreed on a phased industrialisation roadmap, with series production of integrated battery solutions targeted for 2027. The full value chain, from electrolyte and cell manufacturing to pack integration and system delivery, will be anchored in Europe, delivering what both companies believe will be the highest European content of any comparable high-performance battery solution available in the market.
The partnership reflects a deliberate commitment to European technological sovereignty in advanced battery technology, at a moment when access to high-performance, domestically produced battery solutions is increasingly recognised as a strategic priority across the continent.
