title: EnerSys To Acquire Ultralife, Expanding Differentiated Battery Technologies and Accelerating Growth in Defense Market - Batteries News
content:
EnerSys To Acquire Ultralife, Expanding Differentiated Battery Technologies and Accelerating Growth in Defense Market
Accelerates EnerSys’ growth in mission-critical defense applications particularly high growth drone and counter drone systems
Expands advanced, differentiated battery technologies with U.S.-based manufacturing
Increases manufacturing capacity for specialized FEOC-compliant batteries
Supports multiple avenues for value creation, including extending EnerSys’ capabilities into new applications within core markets, accelerating growth in existing high-growth areas, and realizing significant cost synergies
READING, Pa.–(
BUSINESS WIRE
(NYSE: ENS), a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial, infrastructure, and defense applications, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Ultralife (NASDAQ:ULBI) for $16.00 per share in cash, representing a 166% premium to Ultralife’s unaffected closing share price on October 26, 2026. The transaction represents an enterprise value of approximately $320 million. EnerSys expects to realize $15 million to $20 million in annual run-rate cost synergies within the first 18 months, reflecting the unique benefits of combining Ultralife with EnerSys.
Ultralife is a leading provider of rechargeable and non-rechargeable batteries, battery systems, and related accessories for military communications and other specialized applications. The company serves government, defense, and commercial customers globally and generated $191 million in revenue in fiscal 2025. Headquartered in Newark, New York, Ultralife employs more than 700 people, with principal operations across the U.S., Canada, U.K., and China.
“This acquisition is a compelling strategic fit for EnerSys and directly advances our strategy to build a broader, more differentiated defense power platform,” said Shawn O’Connell, President and Chief Executive Officer of EnerSys. “Building on the success of our recent acquisitions, Ultralife expands our portfolio of advanced, reliable, high-performance power solutions. Together, we will be better positioned to support the U.S. Department of War (DoW) and allied forces with leading-edge, cost-effective technologies for the increasingly electrified battlefield of the future. We know the Ultralife business and its team well, and are confident that our shared commitment to engineering, problem solving, and customer focus will create a strong cultural fit. We look forward to combining our strengths to accelerate growth, enhance performance, and deliver greater value to our customers and shareholders.”
Mark Matthews, Chief Technology Officer and President, Precision Power Solutions, added, “Ultralife complements our multi-chemistry expertise and our liquid reserve technologies with an impressive patent portfolio and strong, longstanding customer relationships. Ultralife’s products offer exceptional capabilities such as very high energy density, long shelf life, low self-discharge, useful pulse power, and cold-weather performance, which are ideally suited to the growing defense mission profiles of today and tomorrow.”
Michael Manna,
President and Chief Executive Officer of Ultralife, said:
Combining with EnerSys is an exciting next step that will allow us to unlock value and growth opportunities for both companies, while delivering substantial and certain cash value to Ultralife shareholders,
“This transaction is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our entire organization, and now offers even greater opportunities for our valued employees. We look forward to partnering with the EnerSys team with the combined scale, resources, and shared vision to accelerate innovation and better serve our global customer base.”
Acquisition Expected to Offer Compelling Strategic and Financial Benefits
Expands EnerSys’ advanced defense power technology portfolio
with the addition of Ultralife’s differentiated multi-chemistry capabilities, purpose-built advanced manufacturing capacity with existing security and environmental permits, and operational expertise to scale production of EnerSys’ proprietary liquid reserve battery technology.
Increases scale and broadens exposure to the large and rapidly growing defense market
with capabilities across mission-critical applications in munitions, soldier power, drones, counter drones, and autonomous systems accelerating EnerSys’ focused growth strategy.
Deepens customer relationships
Supports an attractive financial profile.
The transaction is expected to be accretive to adjusted diluted earnings per share within approximately 18 months after closing, excluding transaction and integration costs and other non-recurring items.
Transaction Details and Timing
The transaction will be funded through cash on hand. The transaction has been unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies. Under the terms of the merger agreement, EnerSys, through a subsidiary, will commence a tender offer to acquire all of the outstanding shares of Ultralife common stock at a price of $16.00 per share in cash at closing, representing a total enterprise value of approximately $320 million. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including the tender of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Ultralife’s common stock and receipt of applicable regulatory approvals, and is expected to close in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.
Advisors
XMS Capital Partners, LLC is serving as financial advisor to EnerSys, and Reed Smith LLP is serving as legal counsel to EnerSys in connection with the transaction.

title: Maxell and Institute of SCIENCE TOKYO Begin Joint Development of Next-Generation Batteries Based on 3D-SLISE Electrolyte Technology - Batteries News
content:
Maxell and Institute of SCIENCE TOKYO Begin Joint Development of Next-Generation Batteries Based on 3D-SLISE Electrolyte Technology
Targeting lower environmental impact and reduced fire risk through a manufacturing process free of flammable organic solvents
TOKYO–(BUSINESS WIRE)–
Maxell, Ltd.
(TOKYO: 6810) has launched a joint development project with researchers led by Specially Appointed Professor Yosuke Shiratori of the
Institute of SCIENCE TOKYO
(hereinafter “SCIENCE TOKYO”) on next-generation batteries utilizing an Aqueous Composite Quasi-Solid Electrolyte (
3D-SLISE
Because this next-generation battery does not use flammable organic electrolytes, it is expected to offer a reduced risk of fire. 3D-SLISE is an electrolyte containing water molecules at the interfaces between ceramic particles. By mixing it with water to form a slime-like electrolyte, batteries can be manufactured using coating-based processes.
This technology enables the use of coating technologies and production equipment that Maxell has cultivated through the manufacturing of lithium-ion battery electrodes. In addition, because neither dry rooms nor organic solvents are required, it is expected to contribute to reducing environmental impact through lower VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) emissions and reduced power consumption during manufacturing processes.
Furthermore, the battery is expected to offer excellent recyclability as 3D-SLISE can be dissolved in water after use, making it easier to recover active materials.
Potential applications include uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems for data centers, as well as power tools and automated guided vehicles (AGVs), where stringent safety requirements are essential. In particular, while lithium-ion battery-based UPS systems are increasingly being adopted in data centers to improve energy efficiency and reduce installation space, mitigating fire risks associated with thermal runaway and strengthening fire protection measures remain important challenges. Because even a single fire incident can significantly impact facility operations and business continuity, exceptionally high levels of fire safety are required.
Through this joint research project, Maxell and SCIENCE TOKYO aim to leverage 3D-SLISE, a water-containing aqueous composite quasi-solid electrolyte, to reduce fire risks and improve the safety of people and equipment. They also seek to contribute to reducing the burden associated with fire protection systems and lowering overall facility operating costs in data centers.

title: ADS-TEC Energy Advances One of Europe’s Largest Battery Storage Projects as Building Permit Nears - Batteries News
content:
ADS-TEC Energy Advances One of Europe’s Largest Battery Storage Projects as Building Permit Nears
According to the permitting authority, all application documents are complete. The building permit is expected shortly. Planned to rank among the largest battery storage systems in Europe Expected to deliver grid stability, resilience and flexibility for Baden-Württemberg and beyond Developed with renowned European industrial partners and equipped with ADS-TEC Energy’s proprietary battery management technology Grid connection targeted for 2029 Multiple value streams for ADS-TEC Energy: proprietary technology, long-term technical services and a continuing stake in the project company Investor process well advanced; ADS-TEC Energy plans to sell a majority stake in the project company while remaining a long-term partner
NÜRTINGEN, Germany & MARKGRÖNINGEN, Germany–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–ADS-TEC Energy PLC (NASDAQ: ADSE), a specialist in battery-based energy storage and fast-charging solutions, today announced that the permitting authority has confirmed that all application documents for its battery energy storage power plant at the Pulverdingen substation are complete. The building permit is expected shortly. With a planned power output of approximately 1 gigawatt (GW) and storage capacity of 4 gigawatt hours (GWh), the facility is intended to become one of the largest battery storage systems in Europe.
Power-plant scale
One gigawatt is roughly equivalent to the output of a large coal-fired or nuclear power plant, or of 250 wind turbines. The battery power plant is designed to deliver this output for approximately four hours, which corresponds to the daily electricity consumption of around 400,000 single-family homes or 800,000 apartments. Investment in a facility of this scale typically ranges from the high hundreds of millions to around EUR 1 billion.
Financial significance for ADS-TEC Energy
A flagship project for the region and for Germany as a business location
The project is a flagship from the region, for the region and far beyond. Large-scale battery storage systems are in the overriding public interest and support the implementation of the German federal government’s electricity storage strategy.
Thomas Speidel,
founder and CEO of ADS-TEC Energy, said:
A project of this size requires staying power.
”I am proud that we can build in Markgröningen, and above all of our team, which has spent years preparing this project. Energy is the foundation for everything we produce in Europe. Anyone who does not control the infrastructure for it gives up part of their ability to act. With our own technology and renowned European partners, we are demonstrating that Europe can plan, build and operate critical energy infrastructure on this scale on its own. We owe the fact that a storage power plant of this size and relevance can be built in Baden-Württemberg to the local landowners, the strong local community, the public authorities and the state government, as well as to our good cooperation with the grid operator,”
European partners and full technology control
Storage as the backbone of a renewable grid
Battery storage power plants do not generate electricity; they make it available when it is needed. The facility will absorb power when generation exceeds demand, for example at midday when solar output peaks or during periods of strong wind, and release it within fractions of a second when supply tightens. In day-to-day operation, it will typically run at partial load and adapt dynamically to grid requirements. It will also stabilize grid frequency, absorb load peaks and can support grid restoration after a power outage.
Today, surplus wind and solar power often has to be curtailed or exported at negative prices, only for supply to fall short a few hours later, when other power plants must step in. The storage system will shift this surplus into the hours when it is needed most. The result: less strain on the grid, fewer interventions by grid operators and a more robust and affordable power supply in Baden-Württemberg.
Rising demand for flexibility
Wind and solar generation is inherently variable, while electricity demand continues to grow, driven by electric vehicles, heat pumps and data centers, and fluctuates significantly throughout the day. Large-scale storage bridges this gap and makes a physical contribution to the stability of the power system. This role becomes ever more critical as the economy and everyday life increasingly depend on electricity.
Critical infrastructure built to last
The facility is designed to operate for decades. Beyond developing and building the plant, ADS-TEC Energy will provide technical services to ensure operational reliability and availability over the long term. The power plant is to be operated primarily together with partners from the European energy sector. Emerging flexibility markets will allow the plant to be marketed on the basis of its physical characteristics, and with full in-house capabilities across hardware and software, ADS-TEC Energy is well positioned to adapt the facility to evolving market conditions and new business models.
ADS-TEC Energy is currently in negotiations with potential investors and strategic partners. The building permit is a key prerequisite for concluding the financing and partnership agreements.
While a partner from the European energy sector is preferred, talks are also being held with renowned international infrastructure investors. ADS-TEC Energy intends to sell a majority stake in the project company while remaining a long-term project partner.

title: SK On Demonstrates ESS Fire Safety in Large-Scale Fire Test - Batteries News
content:
SK On Demonstrates ESS Fire Safety in Large-Scale Fire Test
SK On’s ESS meets UL criteria for large-scale fire testing
No thermal runaway observed in adjacent container during testing
SK On to accelerate global ESS market expansion following successful test
SEOUL, October 28, 2026
– SK On, a leading global battery manufacturer, announced that its energy storage system (ESS) met UL 9540A evaluation criteria in a large-scale fire test.
UL 9540A is a widely recognized North American test standard for evaluating fire and heat propagation during battery thermal runaway events.
The large-scale fire test (LSFT) simulates real-world ESS fire scenarios to assess the risk of fire spreading to adjacent containers. In March 2026, the testing requirements were strengthened to introduce more clearly defined criteria for evaluating fire propagation.
During the test, no thermal runaway was observed in the battery cells of the adjacent container. Temperature measurements inside the container also met the applicable evaluation criteria.
SK On attributed the results to its ESS design, which allows heat to dissipate gradually over an extended period. This helps prevent sharp increases in heat release rates and reduces the risk of fire spreading to neighboring containers.
SK On plans to accelerate its expansion in the global ESS market following the successful test.
In August, the company signed an agreement to supply lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries to U.S.-based ESS provider NeoVolta Power. In September 2025, SK On also signed a 1-gigawatt-hour (GWh) ESS supply agreement with U.S. renewable energy company Flatiron.
SK On is also expanding its presence in the South Korean ESS market. In February, the company secured 284 megawatts (MW) of ESS capacity, accounting for more than half of the 565 MW awarded in South Korea’s second round of competitive bidding for ESS projects.
The company is currently converting 3 GWh of its existing 7 GWh production capacity at its Seosan plant in South Korea into dedicated LFP battery production lines for ESS applications.
An SK On spokesperson
This test confirmed the fire safety of SK On’s ESS, demonstrating its ability to limit fire propagation and maintain key safety performance under simulated fire conditions,
“We will continue to enhance our safety technologies and product competitiveness to provide customized ESS solutions and expand our presence in the global market.”

title: EVIO Introduces the Deployable Battery Box, Part of Its Portable Power Family, Delivering Canadian-Made Aerospace Battery Technology for Rugged, Remote Defence Power Needs - Batteries News
content:
EVIO Introduces the Deployable Battery Box, Part of Its Portable Power Family, Delivering Canadian-Made Aerospace Battery Technology for Rugged, Remote Defence Power Needs
OTTAWA, Ontario–(BUSINESS WIRE)–This week at the Aerospace Industries Association of Canada’s (AIAC) Aerospace Summit, EVIO unveiled the Battery Box, part of its Portable Power family—a Canadian-designed, modular battery energy storage system advancing toward prototyping for dual-use defence operations in remote, demanding environments. Drawing on high-energy-density lithium-ion battery packs developed for the EVIO 810 aircraft, this revolutionary product is designed to support dual-use customers who need substantial electrical power in a compact, rugged and transportable system.
The EVIO Battery Box delivers reliable, ruggedized, deployable power for defence and security applications, from Arctic and tactical operations to naval, land and air platforms, disaster relief and remote mining. Its modular design supports extended silent operation, powering communications, sensitive sensors and essential equipment while reducing acoustic and thermal signatures, generator run-time and fuel requirements.
Designed around a 147E standard military pallet, each EVIO battery box has an unparalleled energy storage capability that is 3 to 5 times higher than any other option on the market. This configuration can accommodate four EVIO battery boxes on a 463L standard military pallet, substantially reducing logistics costs to bring power to remote points of use with unprecedented megawatt power capability.
Michael Derman
, Co-founder and CEO of EVIO, said:
Defence operators need dependable power that can move with them, support demanding missions and allow periods of operation without a generator running,
“The EVIO Battery Box applies the electrification expertise we are developing for the EVIO 810 hybrid-electric regional airliner program for operational defence needs. It demonstrates how investment in aerospace technology can create new dual-use capabilities for Canada across defence and other industries.”
EVIO is developing a prototype, ready for testing in the first half of 2027. The prototyping activity includes multi-physics pack engineering, cell characterization, and physical multi-cell thermal runaway testing. A fully operational product will be ready for deployment in the first quarter of 2028. Development priorities include thermal management and performance in extreme cold to address the requirements of Arctic operations.
The EVIO Battery Box is being developed in parallel with the EVIO 810, sharing core energy storage technology and highest safety standards with the aircraft. The energy storage system enables zero-emission all-electric operation for short-haul flights (under 100 nautical miles) and around airports, while using turbine engines for extended range or in-flight battery charging. With operations in Montréal, EVIO is leveraging Canada’s aerospace engineering expertise and supplier network, supported by strategic partnerships with established leaders across the aerospace, battery technology, and advanced materials sectors.

content:
H2scan Unveils Integrated Battery Safety Platform to Help Protect Critical Infrastructure From Emerging Battery Risks
HY-GUARD is the only platform to deliver early hydrogen detection and centralized safety visibility across lead-acid, nickel-cadmium and lithium-ion battery systems.
VALENCIA, Calif.–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–As critical infrastructure operators face growing pressure to maintain uninterrupted power while managing increasingly complex battery installations, H2scan® today unveiled its HY-GUARD® battery safety monitoring platform, the only system of its kind that brings together self-calibration, continuous hydrogen detection, early warning capabilities and centralized system visibility to help operators identify developing battery hazards before they escalate.
The platform builds on H2scan’s recently introduced HY-GUARD RS and HY-SIGHT technologies, which extended the company’s hydrogen monitoring capabilities into lithium-ion battery applications. Together with HY-GUARD monitoring products, the integrated system supports monitoring across lead-acid, nickel-cadmium and lithium-ion batteries, and provides a flexible path from localized detection to system-wide battery safety visibility.
Designed for applications ranging from individual battery cabinets to large-scale energy storage facilities, HY-GUARD helps operators move beyond isolated alarms toward a more comprehensive understanding of battery safety conditions. Its continuous monitoring capabilities provide early indications of developing problems, giving facility and safety teams the necessary time to investigate, respond and prevent an abnormal, or potentially dangerous condition from escalating.
The cost of critical infrastructure failures is significant. According to Uptime Institute’s 2026 Annual Outage Analysis, 57% of surveyed data center operators reported major outage costs exceeding $100,000, with one in five exceeding $1 million.
David Ellis,
President & CEO, said :
For critical infrastructure operators, battery safety is no longer just about protecting equipment. It’s about protecting business continuity, equipment and personnel,
“As battery systems become more complex and the consequences of downtime grow, operators need to identify potential problems before they become costly failures. With HY-GUARD, we’re bringing together continuous monitoring, early detection and real-time intelligence to help facilities stay ahead of emerging risks and keep critical operations running.”
The HY-GUARD platform supports H2scan’s broader mission of turning self-calibrated continuous hydrogen data into actionable situational intelligence in order to help customers identify abnormalities sooner, reduce operational risk and protect critical infrastructure.

title: Inventus Power Launches the LV-24V50, a Compact 24V Lithium-ion Battery for Next-Generation Robotics and Material Handling - Batteries News
content:
Inventus Power Launches the LV-24V50, a Compact 24V Lithium-ion Battery for Next-Generation Robotics and Material Handling
The newest PROformance Li-ion Series battery delivers 1.2 kWh in a footprint sized for AMR and AGV chassis.
WOODRIDGE, Ill., Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Inventus Power (inventuspower.com), a global leader in advanced battery and power systems, today announced the launch of its LV-24V50, the newest addition to its PROformance Li-ion Series. Part of the PROTRXion® family, the LV-24V50 is a 24V lithium-iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) battery pack built for the growing power demands of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and other material handling equipment. Samples are available now for OEM evaluation.
Compact, High-Power Design for AMRs and AGVs
Robotic and automated material handling platforms need more power density, faster charging, and smarter power management. The LV-24V50 delivers 1.2 kWh of rated energy and close to 5 kW of peak power in a compact package engineered for space-constrained robot and AGV chassis, so OEMs can integrate quickly and scale fleets without redesign.
Its 48Ah capacity is sized for full-shift runtime on small platforms without adding unnecessary cost, weight, or volume, which matters for OEMs running high-volume production programs.
The LV-24V50 can fully charge in approximately one hour, keeping fleets in service longer and reducing time spent on the charger in continuous warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics operations.
Intelligent Power Management with a Proprietary BMS
At the core of the LV-24V50 is Inventus Power’s proprietary battery management system (BMS). CANopen communication, soft-start pre-charge control, and active cell balancing work together to optimize performance, safety, and battery life, while giving OEM engineers visibility into state of charge, system health, and fault conditions.
Integrated LED status indicators show battery health at a glance, so technicians and operators can check status without additional diagnostic tools, simplifying service and reducing fleet downtime.
Lower Total Cost of Ownership Than Lead-Acid
Battery-powered industrial equipment needs longer runtime, a smaller footprint, and lower total cost of ownership without sacrificing safety or serviceability. The LV-24V50 is designed to deliver all three.
As a replacement for legacy sealed lead-acid (SLA) batteries, the LV-24V50 offers up to three times the cycle life and 40% less weight, helping OEM customers increase uptime and reduce fleet operating costs.
Torin Schneider,
Senior Product Manager, Inventus Power, said:
Robotics and material handling OEMs have been asking for a smarter, more compact 24V lithium battery, one that charges fast and reports its own health.

title: Draslovka to Acquire ex-Natron Energy Battery IP, Completing a Vertically Integrated Western Sodium-Ion Value Chain - Batteries News
content:
Draslovka to Acquire ex-Natron Energy Battery IP, Completing a Vertically Integrated Western Sodium-Ion Value Chain
Acquisition gives Draslovka control of former Natron Energy IP portfolio spanning sodium-ion materials, cells and complete battery systems.
Deal combines acquired IP with Draslovka’s existing chemistry and European cathode-material capabilities, bringing key parts of the sodium-ion value chain together within one Western-aligned group and its partners.
The IP acquisition strengthens Draslovka’s position across the emerging Western sodium-ion battery value chain.
Technology targets applications where safety, high power, long cycle life and performance across a wide temperature range are critical, including data centers, grid storage, defense, industrial fleets, telecoms, rail and aviation.
The acquired IP will substantively boost Draslovka’s technology offering, a portfolio of transformative and protected innovations for specific industries.
MEMPHIS, Tenn. & PRAGUE–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–Draslovka’s US-based subsidiary, COVORO MINING SOLUTIONS LLC (Covoro), the operator of one of the largest solid sodium cyanide plants in the world, today announced that it has agreed to acquire the intellectual property portfolio in Prussian Blue Analogue (PBA) and Prussian White Analogue (PWA) sodium-ion battery technology originally developed by Natron Energy.
Prussian Blue and Prussian White Analogues are not a single material but a tunable family of framework materials, and the portfolio protects that family across the whole stack — active-material synthesis, electrodes, electrolytes, cell design and manufacturing, as well as complete battery systems — through issued and pending patents, trademarks, and manufacturing know-how, with protection extending into the mid-2040s. The agreement covers intellectual property and intangible assets only and was subject to review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS), which granted clearance as a condition to closing.
The transaction consolidates PBA and PWA capabilities within a group of close West-aligned allies and partners:
Upstream chemistry
– Where Draslovka is the world’s leading producer of sodium cyanide and the ferrocyanide feedstocks at the heart of these materials; cathode active material production, with Europe’s first industrial-scale Prussian White Analogue line starting up at Kolín, Czech Republic in partnership with Altris of Uppsala, Sweden, in which the Group is a strategic shareholder;
Materials, cell and systems intellectual property
– To be held by Covoro in the United States;
Commercial partnerships
– Including Altris’s collaboration with Clarios on serial production of low-voltage sodium-ion systems that carry the technology into finished products. The complete supply chain is now built on Western-available inputs and Western-held intellectual property.
Pavel Brůžek,
CEO of Draslovk
The missing piece of the Western battery value chain has been the materials, and that piece now sits fully within Draslovka Group,
“Draslovka is now building an ecosystem to develop a Western sodium-ion supply chain based on both Prussian White and Prussian Blue technology, in the United States and in the European Union. We have already solved the production and scale-up of active material for both technologies at Kolín, and we now hold all the intellectual property rights associated with the technology, including the finished product and access to the US market. That means Draslovka can take this technology to market directly, and we will scale it with the partners who are ready to move at our pace.”
Jackson Briggs,
Strategy and Business Development Manager at Covoro
The strength of this sodium-ion technology is in applications where safety, power, cycle life and performance across a wide temperature range matter most,
“That includes data centers, grid storage and services, industrial fleets, telecoms, rail, aviation and other applications that need durable, fast-response batteries. We now have a technology platform that can be scaled with partners across those markets.”
Industry analysts now widely agree that sodium-ion complements rather than competes with lithium. While lithium optimizes for energy density, PBA and PWA batteries are intrinsically safe and not subject to thermal runaway, charge and discharge in seconds, and endure tens of thousands of cycles across a wide temperature range. Those characteristics satisfy fast-growing market demand from data centers and AI infrastructure as well as grid storage and services. They offer a durable alternative to lead-acid and nickel-cadmium batteries across automotive, telecom, rail, aviation and industrial standby. Taking account of the full life cycle, that durability makes them highly cost-efficient against competing battery technologies.
Within sodium-ion itself, the Prussian Blue and Prussian White Analogue family stands apart from the layered-oxide and polyanionic chemistries largely utilized by Asian manufacturers. PBA and PWA materials are made at low temperature from abundant sodium, iron and manganese through ferrocyanide chemistry the West already produces at industrial scale; they require no lithium, cobalt, nickel or graphite; they deliver class-leading power and cycle life; and they run on equipment compatible with existing lithium-ion lines. This is the one sodium-ion chemistry whose supply chain can stand entirely on Western ground today — a decisive consideration for data center, grid and defense buyers under tightening supply-chain and procurement rules.
With cathode-material production coming online in Europe, cell and system manufacturing is the remaining step to scale. Covoro and the Group intend to develop that capacity with selected partners — potentially through materials supply and licensing, cell technology licensing and co-located manufacturing. Draslovka will seek opportunities for demand-led scale-up both in Europe and the United States utilizing existing infrastructure.

title: New US Department of Energy Consortium Advances SI-Driven Battery Manufacturing to Strengthen the Country’s Competitiveness - Batteries News
content:
New US Department of Energy Consortium Advances SI-Driven Battery Manufacturing to Strengthen the Country’s Competitiveness
LEMONT, Ill.–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory is joining DOE’s Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) in a
new national consortium
aimed at accelerating the transition of energy storage innovations from discovery to domestic manufacturing.
Called the Battery Manufacturing (BattMan) Accelerator, the consortium will tackle key challenges in scaling emerging battery technologies, with a focus on lowering manufacturing costs, shortening development timelines and strengthening U.S. leadership in advanced energy storage.
Jie Xiao,
Battelle Fellow at PNNL with a joint appointment as Boeing Martin professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Washington in Seattle, said :
Breakthroughs in battery science must be matched by our ability to manufacture them at scale. BattMan brings together the tools, data and partnerships needed to design manufacturable solutions from the start and accelerate their transition into industry,
The four laboratories contribute complementary strengths to bridge gaps between lab discovery and commercial production. PNNL will apply manufacturing science to show that new materials and processes can scale. Argonne will expand this work by validating feasibility and increasing production using its pilot lines. Both labs will provide materials — such as powders and electrodes — to ORNL for smart coating process development. NLR will lead the integration of advanced characterization, physics-guided quality control and digital materials design for rapid feedback to project partners.
Jianlin Li,
director of the Energy Storage and Conversion department at Argonne, who serves as the lab’s lead on the project, said :
Argonne brings materials synthesis and process scale-up capabilities that can shorten the time required for new technologies to reach commercialization,
​“Demonstrating technical and economic feasibility at larger production volumes is essential for validating new technologies efficiently.”
BattMan will also strengthen critical mineral supply chains by advancing battery materials made from more abundant domestic elements.
In addition to Argonne, PNNL, ORNL and NLR, the BattMan Accelerator includes the University of Washington, Binghamton University, University of Alabama, Arizona State University and University of Michigan-Dearborn as founding partners. The accelerator is actively establishing collaborations with companies across the battery and materials manufacturing sector. The laboratories will work closely with these university partners and industry to test and validate manufacturing processes at increasing scales and toward commercially viable production.
Claus Daniel,
associate laboratory director for Argonne’s Advanced Energy Technologies directorate, ​said :
To advance the next generation of battery technologies, we must reduce the risks associated with scaling innovations from laboratory discovery to commercial production,
Processes that work at small scale can behave very differently at larger volumes. Addressing those uncertainties earlier with better science, reliable data and rigorous validation gives companies greater confidence to invest.”
SI-driven manufacturing
Super intelligence (SI), also known as artificial intelligence, is expected to play a central role in the initiative.
SI-driven methods that use processing and manufacturing data have the potential to speed up discovery of new materials, improve efficiency of laboratory processes and support predictive, cost-effective design,
Beyond enabling high throughput, SI has the potential to optimize workflows to reduce cost and accelerate technology maturation,
​“The Argonne team will begin by applying SI to individual processes and later integrate SI models across full production line.”
As part of BattMan, Argonne will generate synthesis and scale-up data, train machine learning models and identify optimal processing conditions through active learning.
Scientific goals
In the near term, BattMan will deploy high-throughput experimentation, automated synthesis and characterization, and digital manufacturing tools to improve data quality, reproducibility and process consistency across partner institutions.
Longer term, the consortium aims to develop self-optimizing manufacturing systems using real-time data, digital twins and tight closed-loop control. BattMan will build on the autonomous laboratory concepts by advancing autonomous pilot lines designed to reduce scale-up time and costs, accelerate commercialization and reinforce domestic supply chains.
BattMan is currently forming industry partnerships in battery and battery-materials manufacturing. For institutions and companies interested in participating, visit
pnnl​.gov/​p​r​o​j​e​c​t​s​/​b​a​ttman
Supported by DOE’s Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies Office within the Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation Office, the BattMan Accelerator integrates SI, materials science and advanced manufacturing into a coordinated, data-driven innovation ecosystem.

LG Energy Solution Opens ‘Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) 2026’ to Connect Innovative Research Ideas with Industry Needs
The company invites universities and research institutions worldwide to submit innovative battery research proposals from Oct. 29 to Dec. 6
Thematic and Open-Topic calls for proposals are designed to deepen industry-academia collaboration, while a two-stage review process safeguards researchers’ original ideas
LG Energy Solution’s Battery Innovation Contest has supported approximately 50 research projects since 2017
SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — LG Energy Solution (KRX: 373220) today announced the launch of the Battery Innovation Contest 2026 (BIC 2026), a global open innovation program to discover and support cutting-edge battery technologies with strong commercialization potential.
Universities and research institutions in Korea and around the world are invited to submit concept proposals from October 29 through December 6, 2026, via LG Energy Solution’s online open innovation platform, BRIDGE (
). Priority will be given to proposals that address key pain points in the battery industry and have the potential to accelerate technological advancement.
Now in its 10th year, the BIC has enabled LG Energy Solution to pursue joint research with universities and research institutions worldwide. Through the program, the company seeks to help transform creative research ideas into commercially viable technologies while contributing to a stronger battery innovation ecosystem.
Deepening Two-Way Collaboration through Thematic and Open-Topic Calls for Proposals
BIC 2026 will continue to offer two calls for proposals designed to combine industry-driven research needs with the creativity and autonomy of researchers.
Under the Thematic call for proposals, LG Energy Solution presents specific research topics identified by its product development departments. This year, the company has significantly expanded the number of thematic topics, ranging from materials and cells to battery management systems (BMS) and AI. Researchers will be invited to propose solutions addressing these topics, creating a more structured framework for two-way collaboration.
The Open-Topic call for proposals will allow researchers to propose original ideas across broad areas of battery technology. This call preserves the researcher-led format, giving participants the flexibility to develop creative concepts with commercial potential.
Protecting Original Ideas through a Two-Stage Proposal Process and the BRIDGE Platform
To better protect researchers’ original ideas, LG Energy Solution will operate a two-stage application and evaluation process, in which applicants will submit a concise concept proposal during the first stage and a full proposal for further evaluation only after being shortlisted. Limiting the detail required in the initial review will help protect ideas that are not ultimately selected.
All proposals and subsequent research projects will be managed through BRIDGE, LG Energy Solution’s integrated, interactive platform for open innovation. BRIDGE streamlines industry-academia communication and project record management while protecting collaborative research technologies and minimizing offline administrative work.
A Decade of Impact: From Patent Filing to Publication in
Since 2017, approximately 50 research projects have been supported through the BIC. Topics with proven feasibility have been expanded into projects at the Frontier Research Laboratory (FRL), LG Energy Solution’s joint research center with leading universities and research institutions in Korea and abroad, which provides additional research funding as well as in-depth support from the company’s researchers.
The BIC has also delivered tangible results. For example, a patent application is underway for a physics-based model developed through a BIC project last year to improve BMS computation speed. In 2019, the FRL’s research on a long-life all-solid-state battery operating at room temperature was published in the prestigious journal
Je-Young Kim,
CTO of LG Energy Solution, said :
“Building on our differentiated technological competitiveness, LG Energy Solution will continue to accelerate its growth in the battery market.”

title: EV Battery Recycling Faces Supply Crunch
content:
Battery Recycling
EV Batteries
Automotive & Mobility
EVs last longer than expected, slowing the battery flow recyclers need to build a viable circular materials loop
November 5, 2026
8 Min Read
A Cox Automotive technician checks the health of a recovered EV battery pack.
Cox Automotive
At a Glance
Too few retired batteries exist to meet recycling demand yet
US lacks refining capacity after black mass export ban
GM closed loop proves recycled cells can power new EVs
There was a time when states applied a deposit to every glass soft drink bottle sold, adding a nickel or a dime to the price to encourage consumers to return the bottles for reuse rather than discarding them.
Because the mores of that era shrugged at littering, enterprising kids could set out for the neighborhood convenience store or gas station with no money, and by picking up a few discarded roadside bottles along the way, redeem them for their deposits and buy a piece of candy. Thus, was born a circular economy for
Coke bottles
employing child labor.
Why EV Battery Recycling Is Harder Than It Looks
The sought-after
circular economy for the materials in electric vehicles
, especially their batteries, is proving tougher to establish. This is in spite of the fact that today’s recovery processes are proving highly effective, even if it isn’t as simple as sanitizing glass Coke bottles for reuse was.
“Recycling processes can recover substantial quantities of critical battery materials—up to 95% for nickel, cobalt, and manganese and up to 80% for lithium,” reported Melissa Flaherty, Director of Sustainable EV Battery Ecosystem for General Motors in
a blog post
to the company’s media site.
Companies like Redwood Materials, founded by Tesla alum JB Strauble, promise to reprocess the depleted batteries from scrapped end-of-life EVs to recover the precious cobalt and nickel inside. Recently, the copper contained throughout EVs has also become more valuable.
Among Redwood’s partners in developing this circular infrastructure are BMW, General Motors, Toyota, Volkswagen of America, and Volvo from the auto industry, plus battery maker Panasonic and consumer goods seller Amazon. The company cites the more than six million EVs sold in the US over the last decade as a huge recycling opportunity, and claims that Redwood processes 70% of the EV battery packs that are recycled in the US.
The recovered elements at Redwood Materials, such as cobalt, lithium, and nickel. REDWOOD MATERIALS
Recyclers like Redwood and Cox Automotive dismantle cars, sending much of the vehicles’ materials into the conventional automotive recycling supply chain and targeting components like batteries, motors, wiring, and circuitry to recover valuable materials. Batteries are sorted to recover the ones that still have potential functional value in another role, such as stationary storage, and the rest are fed into industrial shredders, which break the materials down into a substance called black mass.
Black mass has nothing to do with Ozzy Osbourne’s music. Instead, it is a conglomeration of the valuable elements recovered from batteries, ready for processing back into those elements so they can be reused in new batteries. Battery material clearinghouse
Circunomics
describes this recovery of desirable materials “urban ore.”
Black mass recovered from EV batteries by Redwood Materials. RODNEY HANSEN FOR REDWOOD MATERIALS
Edgar Faler, Principal Mobility Analyst and Strategy for the
Center for Automotive Research
writes in the company’s October 2026 newsletter that “though still in its infancy, U.S. lithium-ion battery recycling already contributes an estimated $4.9 billion to GDP and supports nearly 24,000 jobs.”
Too Few Batteries, Too Little Refining Capacity
Which all sounds good. The problem is that those EVs that were sold are mostly lasting much better than was anticipated, reducing the expected inflow of batteries that are no longer suitable for powering passenger vehicles.
“The challenge with recycling right now is that there actually aren't nearly enough batteries to recycle as we would ultimately want, because we're still relatively early in the EV transition,” noted Sam Abuelsamid, vice president of market research at Telemetry, in
a YouTube interview with EV Pulse
“Probably 85% to 90% of all the EVs ever built have been built in the last five years, and those vehicles are still in service and probably will be for at least another five to 10 years, if not longer,” he said. “So the batteries in those vehicles are not ready to be recycled yet.”
A Cox Automotive technician lifts a defective battery module from its pack. COX AUTOMOTIVE
Redwood forecasts that approximately 1,000 gigawatt-hours (1 terawatt-hour) of EV battery packs will be recovered by 2040. However, the current slow emergence of this market suggests that this volume will be heavily back-loaded.
As a result, the EV recycling market is retrenching, reported Brian Skalovsky, Cox Automotive senior director of recycling. “The domestic shredding and capacity in the United States has gone down,” he observed. “We've seen two or three major startups that are in bankruptcy right now.”
There’s a bottleneck at the refining step of the recycling process in the US, he said. “There is virtually zero refining capacity in the United States right now. And I think that's a little bit of a problem right now, especially coming on the heels of the Bureau of Industry and Security’s (BIS) ban of black mass and tungsten export.”
That means that US recyclers can’t send their black mass abroad for processing unless the resulting materials are certified to be returned to the US for use in new products made here, Skalovsky explained. Without a way to refine the black mass in the US or the ability to send it abroad, recycling companies are being squeezed by the lack of a market for their product, putting a crimp in the circularity loop.
GM's Closed-Loop Experiment and the Second-Life Alternative
General Motors recently conducted a pilot closed-loop recycling project that saw the company employ materials recovered from retired EV batteries to build new batteries and install them into new cars. GM’s partner, Cirba Solutions, took 80 GM EV batteries and reduced them to black mass. This was used to create 12 tons of cathode active material for new battery cells that used 100% recycled nickel, cobalt, and manganese.
The company installed those cells into new Ultium battery packs and used those packs for new Cadillac Lyriq, Lyriq-V, Vistiq, Escalade IQ and IQL, Chevrolet Silverado EV Trail Boss, and GMC Sierra EV AT4 vehicles.
Batteries don’t have to be ground up to be reused. Those that are still in good shape are being routed into Redwood’s battery energy storage project, where slightly reduced capacity doesn’t matter. “We’re deploying roughly 10,000 GM second-life batteries into real-world energy infrastructure,” said GM’s Flaherty. “That includes the largest second-life battery microgrid in North America with additional deployments ahead, including at our own manufacturing footprint here in the US.”
“These batteries that come back through our door have a substantial amount of life left,” said Redwood Strauble. These packs retain 50% to 80% of their original capacity, he said.
“Today we are collecting, storing, moving, processing 20 gigawatt hours per year of batteries and battery materials, growing at over 100% a year,” Strauble said. “We have proven that we can quickly deploy these batteries back into a grid energy storage setting with a phenomenal value return. This architecture is flexible and fundamentally software-enabled, power electronics-enabled, to control and aggregate all these batteries together. No one's ever done that, even at a small scale, let alone at a large commercial scale.”
Redwood's battery energy storage system microgrid, with the packs located outdoors, where any fires can't spread. RODNEY HANSEN FOR REDWOOD MATERIAL
A potential complication in this market is the rise of cheaper lithium-iron phosphate batteries that could potentially be even cheaper than recycled batteries, said Skalovsky. “If I were an engineering company or a [battery energy storage system] builder, I would want a new module that has a 10-year warranty over something that's been in a vehicle that no one's going to guarantee,” he said. “I wouldn't feel comfortable designing something around used batteries. If there's a cheaper or equally priced new battery, I would go with the new battery.”
Motors, Magnets, and Rare Earth Recovery
Batteries aren’t the only component in an EV that contains valuable materials.
Market researchers Market Intelo
estimate the 2025 global market for recycled materials from EV motors was $3.2B. The company projects that will grow to $15.8B by 2034.
That is why Paladin recovers rare earth elements, copper, and other materials from retired EVs. “The [EV] rotor assembly is going to have those rare earth magnets in there,” said Luke Wray, Senior Vice President of Critical Materials & Defense at Paladin.
“But you're also going to have steel, you're going to have some copper, you're going to have some aluminum,” he said. “In some cases, you might have some circuit board that has precious metal value too,” he said. “So, when you add up all the pieces to the whole, and you're able to extract value at each level, that's where the economics start to make sense.”
“If I can shred the component when it comes into my facility, it makes sense to go after it,” Wray explained. Manual disassembly only pays off for very valuable materials. “If it has dysprosium in it, which we do see in the actual rotor assembly, for those magnets, we're seeing anywhere from 5% to sometimes as high as 10% dysprosium and trace amounts of terbium. Now it starts to get really interesting because those metals are going to fetch a much higher price.”
So, while EV recycling seems to have stumbled a bit out of the gate, continuing market pressure for the materials contained inside EVs that are on the road today ensures that there will be an industry to recover and reuse those materials. The only question is, “Which players will survive the current retrenching?” If only the solution were as simple as a 5-cent deposit to encourage reuse.
About the Author
Dan Carney
Senior Editor, Design News
Dan’s coverage of the auto industry over three decades has taken him to the
racetracks
, automotive engineering centers,
vehicle simulators
, wind tunnels, and crash-test labs of the world.
A member of the

for automotive writing, as well as the

He has held a

racing license since 1991, is an SCCA National race winner, two-time SCCA Runoffs competitor in

, and an
Old Dominion Region

16 Federation Internationale de l’Automobile-accredited world speed records
over distances from just under 1km to over 4,104km at the CERAM test circuit in Mortefontaine, France.
He was also a longtime contributor to the Society of Automotive Engineers'

He specializes in analyzing technical developments, particularly in the areas of motorsports, efficiency, and safety.
He has been published in

sports cars and contributed automotive content to the consumer finance book,

and is a member of the

title: The Estée Lauder Companies & Microsoft Announce Partnership
content:
The Estée Lauder Companies & Microsoft Announce Partnership
Prioritise Us
on Google
Estée Lauder is partnering with Microsoft to bring more products to consumers. Credit: Estée Lauder
ELC is partnering with Microsoft to bring more personalised content to its customers, explains Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer
As part of its efforts to bring more innovation to its operations, The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. is partnering with Microsoft.
The partnership will involve the advancement of cloud and data foundation, alongside supporting responsible AI across the enterprise.
In doing this, ELC will be able to connect data better in order to develop more relevant consumer experiences and greater efficiency.
Network modernisation
In recent years, The Estée Lauder Companies has been integrating data and AI into its operations, working to
become more agile across the platform
and meet customer demand more efficiently.
Its One Operating Ecosystem strategy – a system, built over the last year – brings together data, shared platforms and strategic partners. The aim is to enable consistent, effective and scalable execution across functions and brands.
The partnership is a major part of this strategy, using the Microsoft platform to drive agility and AI across ELC. By doing this, the company’s data will be more connected, which results in more consistent access to data-driven insights. This reduces the risk of duplication and streamlines efficiency.
“As we continue to execute on Beauty Reimagined, we are building the future of consumer-centricity—in our products, experiences, commerce and more,” says Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer at The Estée Lauder Companies.
Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer at The Estée Lauder Companies
"Our partnership with Microsoft, in addition to the other strategic partners in our One Operating Ecosystem, is powering our teams with the capabilities to ultimately deliver more relevant, personalised experiences that meet consumers’ evolving needs.
“These enhanced capabilities will help us drive sustainable growth, improve productivity and support margin expansion, creating capacity to reinvest into our enterprise to serve our consumers.”
At a glance
ELC has four major product categories
Its products are sold in 150 countries and territories
ELC reached US$14.32bn in net sales for FY25
More than 20 brands sit under the The Estée Lauder Companies
Copilot tools have been expanded across more than 14,000 employees
A partnership for consistency
The partnership will result in a strengthened data foundation, which will make it much easier to run an AI-enabled consumer ecosystem. The strengthened data is crucial for expanding its
capabilities with AI tools
, as the company works to grow its understanding of consumer needs and preferences. Through this, the company can develop more personalisation within its products.
A large aim of the partnership is to be able to create more consistency in real time, across the discovery to purchase timeline, which then helps the brands understand the consumers and give them the ideal experience.
As a result, ELC is aiming to grow agility within its brands, helping them to adapt to new experiences and customer desires. Alongside this, this is a resilience driver for the company, helping it gain more flexibility as the way consumers shop continues to shift.
AI in supply chain
ELC is embedding AI in workflows and strengthening connectivity across functions, through its shared enterprise foundation. Through this, the insights become more accessible to team members, offering them a greater understanding of the business.
As a result, there is greater cohesion and connectivity across the supply chain. The insights are connected to end-to-end workflows, marketing teams, value chain leaders, commercial teams, as well as research and innovation teams. This results in faster and more coordinated decisions.
With consumer and market needs changing on a regular occurrence, fast response times are crucial. These greater insights result in a new type of process in getting products from launch to the consumer’s basket.
“The future of the beauty industry will be shaped by organisations like the Estée Lauder Companies that connect data, people and AI responsibly,” said Deb Cupp, EVP and Chief Revenue Officer at Microsoft.
Deb Cupp, EVP and Chief Revenue Officer at Microsoft
“Our expanded collaboration will help turn insights into action at scale—from empowering employees to modernising product development and delivering more meaningful consumer experiences.”
ELC is making secure AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot, accessible to its employees. Through this, repetitive and manual tasks will be automated, meaning teams can put their efforts into strategy, innovation and higher-value decision-making.
More than 14,000 employees in the company have been making use of Copilot, embedding AI into their workflows and seeing improvements to their productivity. The partnership is part of ELC’s Beauty Reimagined strategy, which aims to increase consumer centricity and innovation within operations. Through the partnership, there will be increased growth
across efficiency, speed and agility
These enhanced capabilities will help us drive sustainable growth, improve productivity, and support margin expansion, creating capacity to reinvest into our enterprise to serve our consumers.
Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer at The Estée Lauder Companies
The Estée Lauder Companies
The Estée Lauder Companies is a global leader in prestige beauty, manufacturing and marketing skincare, makeup, fragrance, and hair care products. Founded in 1946 by Estée Lauder, the company owns iconic brands including Estée Lauder, Clinique, MAC, La Mer, and Tom Ford Beauty. Operating in over 150 countries, it serves consumers through department stores, specialty retailers, and various digital channels.
Microsoft
Microsoft Corporation is a global technology leader founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen. The company develops, licenses, and supports software products, services, and devices. Key offerings include Windows operating systems, Office productivity suite, Azure cloud platform, Xbox gaming, LinkedIn, and Surface hardware. Microsoft serves billions of users worldwide across consumer, enterprise, and government sectors with innovative solutions.

title: China blocks SoftBank’s US$5.37bn bid for ABB Robotics
content:
China blocks SoftBank’s US$5.37bn bid for ABB Robotics
Prioritise Us
on Google
ABB opened its robotics mega factory in Shanghai in December 2022. Credit ABB
Beijing has blocked SoftBank's US$5.37bn purchase of ABB's robotics division, the multinational has confirmed in a statement
China’s regulatory authorities have intervened to halt the acquisition of ABB Robotics, ABB’s China-based robotics arm, by Japanese technology conglomerate SoftBank.
SoftBank’s planned US$5.37bn acquisition of ABB Robotics has been prohibited by China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC).
When the acquisition was
announced
in October 2025, the transaction had been expected to close in mid-to-late 2026, depending on regulatory approvals. Instead, it has been blocked by the NDRC, ABB confirmed on 5 November 2026.
“ABB confirms that it has been informed by SoftBank that the Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review in China has prohibited the acquisition of the ABB Robotics business in China,” an ABB statement announced.
The office operates within the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), as part of the wider Ministry of Commerce. The NDRC is closely involved in the development of China’s 5-Year Plans, although the responsibility for implementation of the plans is devolved to the relevant ministries; the office is also closely involved in efforts to develop and maintain competitiveness in strategically important sectors of the economy.
The latest intervention offers further confirmation of the sensitivity of cross-border acquisitions in the AI and technology space. The intervention by the Chinese authorities follows the NDRC’s blocking of a proposed takeover of AI start-up Manus by Meta in April 2026.
ABB Robotics has launched its first end-to-end, vision-based industrial-grade physical AI solution, integrating AI Robot Trainer into its Fashion Inductor module for automated fashion logistics. Credit: ABB Robotics
Cross‑border reach
ABB Robotics opened a US$150m robotics manufacturing hub in the Pudong district of Shanghai in China in 2022. The company makes 90% of its production for the Chinese market domestically.
alone accounted for 54% of industrial robot deployments in 2024, with its operational robot inventory surpassing 2m units. The country's market share has also climbed to 57%, representing growth from approximately 28% over the previous decade.
As ABB Robotics was originally founded in China, it remains subject to the country’s stringent export controls governing the transfer of domestic technology to foreign firms. While no rationale for the regulatory intervention has been announced, the potential integration of data from physical AI focused enterprises into AI models has been the subject of considerable interest.
When SoftBank originally announced its plans to acquire ABB's robotics division in October 2025, the deal was seen as a major element of the company’s
strategy
to invest in physical AI.
Neither the NDRC nor SoftBank have made any public comment about the intervention. ABB said in a brief statement that “ABB and SoftBank are in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction."
ABB Robotics has been supporting customers in all sectors of the Chinese economy from automotive and electronics to metals, plastics and logistics for decades. Credit: ABB
Meet the partners
CEO: Morten Wierod
Headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland
ABB is a global technology leader in electrification and automation, driving software-integrated engineering solutions to optimize manufacturing and robotics performance. ABB is the parent technology company behind the robotics portfolio. Its wider automation capabilities provide the corporate and engineering foundation for ABB Robotics’ physical-AI, robot-control and simulation platforms.
ABB Robotics
President: Marc Segura
Headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland
ABB Robotics provides innovative solutions for diverse industries including automotive, electronics, and logistics. Its services include AI Robot Trainer, which combines robotic motion, automatic path planning and lifecycle-based AI optimisation.
SoftBank
President: Masayoshi Son
Headquarters: Minato-Ku, Tokyo, Japan
SoftBank Group has invested in a number of physical AI start-ups across robots, tasks and environments, and maintains a strong focus on the integration of physical AI and AI models, including OpenAI.

title: AutoStore to Acquire Logiqs B.V. to Accelerate Automation
content:
AutoStore to Acquire Logiqs B.V. to Accelerate Automation
Prioritise Us
on Google
AutoStore has agreed to acquire Logiqs, in a move which will advance both parties' operations. Credit: AutoStore
Logiqs is expanding automation capabilities and meeting customer demand in developing acquisition journey, explains Reyer van der Louw, CEO of Logiqs
AutoStore has entered into an agreement to acquire Logiqs B.V., providing greater opportunity for growth.
The two companies will be collaborating to develop new technology and bring it to a wider market, which will be beneficial for both parties as the
supply chain becomes more automated
Accelerating advancements
Since 1975, Logiqs has been creating automation solutions for horticulture, vertical farming and warehouse logistics. Based in the Netherlands, the company designs software to
including iCUBE, an automated pallet storage system. The iCUBE has four-way shuttles and proprietary control software. Its technology is developed with the aim of making a better tomorrow, helping people do more with less resources and less waste.
Its warehouse technology is deployed at 30 customer sites, operating across a range of industries around the world.
“Today, we announced that AutoStore has entered into an agreement to acquire Logiqs B.V. This is an important milestone for our company and an exciting opportunity to further develop our iCUBE pallet storage technology together with AutoStore,” Reyer van der Louw, CEO of Logiqs said on LinkedIn.
Reyer van der Louw, CEO of Logiqs
“With over 50 years of experience in automation, we have built a strong foundation in engineering, software and product development. Combining our expertise with AutoStore's capabilities and international reach creates exciting opportunities to further develop our technology and bring automated pallet storage solutions to a broader market.
“I'm confident that the combined expertise of our companies, together with the cultural similarities we share, provides a strong starting point for a successful collaboration. I look forward to what we can achieve together.”
Logiqs is aiming to accelerate its technological capabilities with this new movement, gaining value from AutoStore’s
global reach and technological capabilities
. Despite this, it is maintaining its roots in horticulture.
Since its foundation, Logiqs has been collaborating with those in the horticulture industry to develop logistics solutions which support their daily operations. This relationship remains important to the company, and it will continue to support the industry amid its planned growth.
At a glance
AutoStore clients have seen storage capacity increase by 10x
AutoStore states customers have seen 50% in labour savings and 33% in cost savings over three years
AutoStore has approximately 2,000 systems across 68 countries
The iCUBE system consists of six compartments between -18C and +5C
40,000 pallets can be stored in an iCUBE system
Supply chain collaboration
International technology company, AutoStore, combines software, AI and automation to help with
storage and order fulfilment
. It has a compact storage system where robots travel above a grid in order to store and retrieve goods.
As part of the acquisition, AutoStore aims to expand its platform in order to include automated pallet storage, such as the iCUBE.
“This acquisition is another step in our journey towards building an autonomous, intelligent fulfilment platform. In Logiqs, we have identified a core technology that, over time, will bring roaming pallet AS/RS into the AutoStore platform, helping us address a broader set of needs for both new and existing customers”, said Mats Hovland Vikse, CEO of AutoStore.
Mats Hovland Vikse, CEO of AutoStore
Through collaboration with one another and the focus on each company’s specialties, the acquisition will help bring new value to a wider set of customers and will grow the platforms.
A core priority for both companies is making the technology available to more customers and developing it further. Logiqs has the specific practical experience and strong customer relationship, meaning it understands the needs of its customers. AutoStore brings its international scale and partner network,
alongside its developmental capabilities
The partnership will result in ongoing advancements to order fulfilment technology, and greater efficiency in warehouse operations.
Until the closure of the acquisition, the companies will continue to operate as separate entities.
This acquisition is another step in our journey towards building an autonomous, intelligent fulfilment platform.
Mats Hovland Vikse, CEO of AutoStore
Key companies
Logiqs B.V.
Logiqs B.V. is a Dutch company specializing in warehouse automation and logistics solutions. As a system integrator and AutoStore partner, they implement automated storage and retrieval solutions for various industries. Based in the Netherlands, Logiqs helps businesses optimize warehouse operations through robotics and intelligent software, focusing on improving efficiency, accuracy, and optimal space utilization in supply chain and fulfillment operations.
AutoStore
AutoStore is a Norwegian warehouse automation company founded in 1996. It pioneered cube storage automation using robots operating on a grid system to retrieve bins. The system maximizes vertical space, reducing warehouse footprint by up to 75%. AutoStore serves e-commerce, retail, and logistics globally. Its modular design allows scalability and flexibility, making it a leading automated storage and retrieval solution.

title: Kia's PV7 electric van stretches over 17 feet and seats 9
content:
Peter Johnson
| Nov 6 2026 - 7:30 am PT
is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.
The Kia PV7 van is launching in 2027
The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.
Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia
revealed the PV7
at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.
It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.
The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the
Volkswagen ID. Buzz
Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.
Kia PV7 Passenger (Source: Kia)
23 different top hats coming
Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.
It will be offered with two nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs: 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh. The Long Range Cargo model offers an all-electric WLTP range of over 460 km (285 miles). Even at full capacity, Kia said the new PV7 achieves nearly 400 km (248 miles) of range and still has 350 liters of trunk space.
A plena capacidad la nueva
consigue casi 400 km de autonomía y aún reserva 350 litros de maletero
#MovementThatInspires
Front-wheel drive (FWD) will be standard at launch, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) option later.
Depending on the configuration, the FWD electric powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.
Thanks to its 800V architecture, the Kia PV7’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes with a 350 kW DC fast charger. It will be Kia’s first vehicle with two charging ports, including a front AC/DC port and an optional rear side AC port.
Kia PV7 Cargo (left) and Passenger (right) Source: Kia)
With vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, it can serve as a mobile power source for tools, equipment, a campsite, or other external electronic devices.
Personal and business use
The PV7 Cargo, designed for businesses, fleets, and logistics, is available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.
Maximum payload is up to 1,165 kg (2,568 lbs) for the Cargo Long and up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) for the compact model.
The PV7 Cargo Long features a 550 mm loading height and, according to Kia, enough capacity for up to three Euro pallets (800 x 1,200 mm). An added heavy-duty mode adjusts the vehicle’s response to varying payloads to help maintain stability and control while driving.
Depending on the use, buyers can choose between full-open twin-swing tailgate doors or a lift-up tailgate.
The PV7 Passenger, on the other hand, is designed for personal use and families, or can also be used as a shuttle with room for up to nine passengers in the global version. In Korea, it will seat up to 11 passengers.
The 7-seater features Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats, enabling various interior seating configurations. The 9-seater variant, on the other hand, is available with or without a fourth row.
High-tech and spacious interior
Inside, both versions feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, with 12.9″ and 14.6″ display screens and physical controls for commonly used functions.
The system runs Android Automotive OS, making it more like a smartphone with apps and customizable screens. It also includes Hyundai’s Gleo AI, an AI-powered in-car companion that can answer questions, control navigation or vehicle functions, and more.
Kia said the PV7 is based on a “Mobile Workspace” concept, with a layered dashboard and center console to optimize space.
The Kia PV7 Passenger and Cargo will go on sale in Korea and Europe in the second half of 2027. It will then roll out to new markets with new derivatives and conversions.
Kia will announce PV7 prices closer to its launch. In Korea, the PV5 Passenger and Cargo Compact starts at 45.9 million won ($34,000) and 41 million won ($30,000), respectively. In Germany, the
PV5 Passenger
5-seater starts at €38,690 ($43,000).

title: Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices up to 10% after announcing it will kill production
content:
Tesla Cybertruck
Fred Lambert
| Nov 6 2026 - 6:03 am PT
Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.
The move comes right after Tesla
confirmed it will end Cybertruck production
at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
The new Cybertruck prices
Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:
Dual Motor AWD: $82,490, up from $74,990 (+$7,500, 10%), but no longer orderable
Premium AWD: $92,490, up from $84,990 (+$7,500, 8.8%)
Cyberbeast: $102,490, up from $99,990 (+$2,500, 2.5%)
The Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.
This is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla
raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August
, when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.
Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.
For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.
Higher prices on a truck nobody’s buying
The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.
Tesla also tried the opposite approach earlier this year. It offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 in February for “only the next 10 days,” then pulled it. A single-motor RWD version was discontinued after just 173 sales. None of it moved the needle.
The Cybertruck isn’t sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets, and Tesla
canceled it for Australia and New Zealand
last month.
Electrek’s Take
This is what a wind-down looks like. Tesla isn’t trying to sell more Cybertrucks anymore. It’s trying to make as much money as possible on the last ones, with the hope that announcing the end of production will encourage some people to secure their order.
Once you’ve decided to end a program, volume stops mattering. You have a set number of build slots left, a parts supply you want to burn down, and probably a small group of fans who’ll want one before it’s gone. Pausing the cheapest trim and charging $7,500 more for the rest is the obvious play. You push everyone into higher-margin configurations and stop pretending the base truck is a real product.
But it does say a lot about the last two years of Cybertruck pricing. Tesla went from a $59,990 “limited-time” offer in February to a $92,490 entry price in November. That’s a company that never figured out who the truck was for.
